when a Brahmin’s field is seized, three generations of the family are destroyed.
One who seizes land is not purified even by a thousand ponds and wells, nor by a hundred horse-sacrifices, nor by the gift of ten million cows. (37)

Whatever has been performed, given, practiced as austerity, or studied—whatever dharma has been established by anyone—is destroyed by the seizing of even half a finger’s breadth of land belonging to another. (38)
By obstructing a watering place for cattle, a village road, or even a cremation ground and a village, one goes to hell until the dissolution of all beings. (39)
One destroys five by lying about a maiden; one destroys ten by lying about a cow;
one destroys a hundred by lying about a horse; one destroys a thousand by lying about a human being. (40)
One who speaks falsehood for the sake of gold destroys both those born and those unborn; one destroys everything by speaking falsehood regarding land. Do not speak falsehood regarding land! (41)
One should not cause displeasure to a Brahmin even at the cost of one's life, though it be hanging by the throat;
those burnt by fire grow back, but one burnt by a Brahmin does not grow back.
Those burnt by fire sprout again, and likewise those scorched by the sun;
so too do those struck down by royal punishment and those slain by the curse of a Brahmin.
And these cows, nourished by the property of Brahmā,
repeatedly perish at the time of their task, just like grains of sand heated by the sun.
A man who seizes the property of a Brahmin goes to the Raurava hell;
they say that poison is not truly poison—it is the property of a Brahmin that is called poison. (45)
Poison kills only a single person, but the property of a Brahmin destroys one's sons and grandsons.
A man may digest iron filings, stone powder, and poison; [but not the sin of seizing a Brahmin’s land]. ||46||
What man in the three worlds could ever consume the property of a Brahmin?
The happiness derived from the property of a Brahmin is like the joy of a god, while that derived from the property of a deity is but a source of distress.
That wealth leads to the destruction of the family and brings about one's own ruin;
the property of a Brahmin is like the sin of killing a Brahmin, as is the wealth of a poor man. (48)
O Vāsava, one should cause even the teacher, a friend, or gold to suffer, even if they reside in heaven, provided it is for the sake of a learned man of noble birth who is impoverished. 49.
To one who is contented, disciplined, and possesses all his belongings;
who is devoted to the study of the Vedas, austerity, knowledge, and the restraint of the senses.
O best of asuras, that which was given by you—beneficial and inexhaustible—is like milk, curd, ghee, or honey placed in an unbaked clay vessel. (51)
Out of weakness he breaks the vessel, yet the vessel is not destroyed;
likewise [he seeks to break] cows, gold, clothing, food, land, and sesame seeds. (52)
The ignorant person who accepts such a gift is reduced to ashes like a piece of wood. He who constructs a new pond, or causes an old one to be excavated, [attains great merit]. 53.
Having uplifted his entire family, he is glorified in the heavenly world;
[he gains] ponds, wells, tanks, and the products of gardens.
O Vāsava, these pearls, which yield the fruit of refinement when brought back again,
remain as water during the summer season.
O best of gods, one shall never encounter a difficult, uneven, or arduous situation, provided that water remains on the earth for even a single day. (56)
By the offering of the light of a lamp, he shall deliver his own family as well as seven generations before and seven after him; that man shall become endowed with a radiant body.
By the giving of a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), one bestows memory and intelligence;
even after committing a sinful act, he who gives it away in repentance [is purified]. (58)
He is not tainted by sins, especially when land, cows, or a slave are forcibly seized from a Brāhmaṇa. (59)
O Vāsava, he who does not announce [the arrival] when a marriage, a sacrifice, or a gift is at hand, they call him a slayer of a Brahmin.
He who, out of delusion, commits an obstacle against a creature is born as a worm;
wealth bears fruit through giving, and life through the protection of living beings.
One enjoys beauty, sovereignty, health, and the fruit of non-violence;
through subsisting on fruits and roots one attains worship, and heaven is obtained by means of truth. (62)

By fasting unto death (prāyopaveśana), one enjoys a kingdom and happiness everywhere; through the initiation of Śakra, one attains happiness; and by subsisting on grass, one becomes a traveler on a good path.
One who possesses a physical body and bathes at the three periods of the day may attain the fruit of a sacrifice by drinking air;
one who bathes daily should be diligent, joined with the twilight prayers and the recitation of the Vedas.
One who enters the fire with self-restraint attains sovereignty over the world of the serpents, the unassailable back of heaven, and is glorified in the world of Brahmā.
Upon the withdrawal of the tastes, he bestows cattle and sons;
he who observes the fast dwells for a long time in the heavenly realm.
He who constantly sleeps on the ground shall attain his desired goal;
for one who practices the hero’s posture, the hero’s bed, and the hero’s station.
His worlds shall be inexhaustible, and likewise he may go wherever he desires;
O Vāsava, [he attains] fasting, initiation, and consecration.
Having practiced this for twelve years, one excels even the station of a hero;
performing this purifying dharma, he is glorified in the heavenly world.
Those best of the twice-born who recite this meritorious doctrine of Bṛhaspati—for them, these four increase: longevity, knowledge, fame, and strength. (70)
Nārada said: O King, thus was that entire treatise on dharma, composed by Bṛhaspati for Indra, fully proclaimed to me, his devotee, by Maheśa.

Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, titled "The Discourse on Dharma," in the dialogue between Umāpati and Nārada within the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, consisting of fifty-five thousand verses.
(33) Chapter Thirty-Three.
Nārada said:
O best of asuras, please tell me how the affliction caused by Saturn is overcome;
for from your mouth I hear that by this [knowledge], one is indeed liberated from it.
Mahādeva said:
O celestial sage, hear the account of how [the Sun] was released from the bondage of Namuci;
he is the king of the planets, the son of Sūri, and the supreme lord of all. 2.
This very one is renowned as the great planet Kālarūpī;
with matted hair and adamantine bristles, he is the bringer of terror to the Dānavas.
O Lord, there is no account of his that is renowned in this world which has not been protected by me; indeed, I have never spoken of it to anyone at any time.
In ancient times, there was a king named Daśaratha, highly renowned in the lineage of Raghu;
he was a great hero, a universal monarch (cakravartin), and the sovereign of the seven continents.
Having been informed by the astrologers that they had recognized the thunderbolt to be in Kṛttikā, he said:
"And Śani will go toward Sāṃpratā after piercing through Rohiṇī. (6)
A most terrible division of the Śākaṭa type, causing fear to both gods and asuras, will occur;
for twelve years there will be a most dreadful famine.
Having heard these words from me, the king then deliberated with his three ministers: "What is this terrifying danger that has arisen? (8)
And seeing the world—including the people of the city and the countryside—in a state of agitation, the people everywhere say: "This destruction has arrived. (9)
Then, the regions, along with their cities and villages, being terrified by that fearlessness,
all together questioned the twice-born sages headed by Vasiṣṭha while the king remained intent upon his vow.
"O best of the twice-born, tell me truly: what arrangement exists here?"
Vasiṣṭha said: "This constellation belongs to Prajāpati; now that it has been split, how can there be offspring? Indeed, this yoga is impossible to achieve even for Brahmā, Śakra, and the others."
Having thus reflected in his mind, he spoke these supreme and great words;
then, taking up his divine bow along with its divine weapons, he prepared himself.
Having mounted his chariot, he went with speed to the circle of the stars,
situated one hundred thousand and twenty-five thousand yojanas above the sun.
In former times, King Daśaratha mounted the back of Rohiṇī upon a certain divine chariot adorned with jewels and precious gems.
I, shining with great jewels and radiant with a crown and diadem, am mounted upon a chariot yoked with horses of matching color, which possesses a towering, magnificent banner.
Shining like a second sun in the sky, he drew his bow back to his ear and discharged the weapon of destruction (saṃhārāstra). ||17||
Seeing the weapon of destruction, which causes fear to both gods and asuras, Śani laughed out of fear and spoke these words: ||18||
Śani said:
O king of kings, your supreme manliness causes fear even to your enemies;
so too do the gods, asuras, humans, siddhas, vidyādharas, and uragas. (19)
"O King, those who have not been looked upon by me are reduced to ashes.
O Indra among kings, I am pleased with your austerity and your manly valor; choose a boon, whatever you desire in your heart, and I shall grant it. (20)
Daśaratha said:
"One must never go by piercing through Rohiṇī;
[this shall hold] as long as the rivers flow to the ocean, and as long as the moon, the sun, and the earth endure. (21)
"I have requested this from you; I desire no other boon.
"So be it," Śani replied, having granted the eternal boon.
Being pleased, he spoke once more: "O you of excellent vows, choose a boon.
Then Śani, with a joyful heart, requested another boon.
O son of the Sun, you must not break this cart;
a twelve-year famine must never be brought about by you.
Śani said:
"A twelve-year famine shall never occur;
this fame of yours shall circulate throughout the three worlds. (25)
Having obtained the two boons, the king’s hair stood on end with joy; he set down his bow upon the chariot and, with palms joined in reverence, stood before him.
Having meditated upon the goddess Sarasvatī and Gaṇanātha Vināyaka,
King Daśaratha then spoke this hymn to Sauri.
Daśaratha said: Salutations to Kṛṣṇa, to Nīla, and to him who resembles Śitikaṇṭha;
salutations to him whose form is like the fire of time (Kālāgni), and salutations indeed to the protector of all beings. 28.
Homage to the one who is without flesh yet possesses a body, and to the one with long beard and matted hair;
homage to the one with wide eyes and a terrifying appearance with a withered belly. (29)
Salutations to the one with a robust body and thick hair, or rather salutations;
salutations to the tall one with a withered body; salutations be unto you, O Kāladaṃṣṭra!
Homage to you, O cave-eyed one, who are difficult to gaze upon;
homage to you, the terrible, the fierce, the fearsome, the bearer of skulls.
Homage to you, the consumer of all; homage to you, O Aṅgada! Homage to you, son of the Sun; homage to you, O Bhāskara, the giver of fearlessness! (32)
Homage to you who look downward; homage to you, Saṃvartaka! Homage to you who move slowly; homage to you, Nistriṃśāyana! ||33||
Salutations always to him whose body is consumed by austerity and who is constantly devoted to yoga; salutations indeed always to him who is afflicted by hunger and yet remains unsatisfied. ||34||
Salutations to you, the Knower and the Seer, the son of the daughter of Śukra;
when pleased, you bestow sovereignty, but when enraged, you take it away in an instant. (35)
Gods, asuras, humans, siddhas, vidyādharas, and serpents—all of them, when beheld by you, go to destruction along with their very roots. (36)
"O best of gods, show me favor; I have come before you as one worthy of your grace.
Thus was the son of Sūrya, the mighty king of planets, then praised.
And the son of Bhāskara, his hair standing on end with joy, spoke these words again:
"O king of kings, O observer of noble vows, I am pleased by this hymn of yours. Choose a boon, O descendant of Raghu; I shall grant it according to your own desire. (38)
Daśaratha said: "From this day forward, no one among gods, asuras, humans, beasts, birds, or reptiles shall cause any affliction to Sauri. (39)
Śani said:
"All planets are known as 'seizers' (grahas) because they seize; all planets are considered to be causes of affliction.
O King, since you have asked for that which ought not to be given, I shall say what is appropriate. (40)
The person who shall recite this hymn spoken by you, whether once or twice a day, shall be freed from suffering in an instant. (41)
I shall grant death unto death itself for gods, asuras, humans, siddhas, vidyādharas, and rākṣasas, at their fourth birth.
Furthermore, one who is endowed with faith, having become pure and composed, should worship an image of me made of iron with *śamī* leaves. (43)
One should give iron mixed with black gram, rice, and sesame seeds as a sacrificial fee;
or else, one should give a black cow or even a bull to a member of the twice-born.
One should worship with this hymn, which is distinguished by its specific power over me;
having worshipped, one should recite the hymn while standing with palms joined in *añjali*. (45)
I shall never cause him any affliction, whether in his period (gocara), his birth ascendant (janmalagna), his major periods (daśās), or his sub-periods (antardaśās). 46.
I shall constantly protect him from the affliction of that planet;
by this very rite, the world shall be freed from suffering. 47.
Thus, O descendant of Raghu, I granted the boon through this reasoning;
and having obtained those three boons, King Daśaratha then [departed].
Having paid homage to Saturn, who considered his purpose already accomplished,
and being permitted by Saturn, he, full of speed, mounted his chariot.
The king returned to his own place and then attained prosperity;
whoever, having risen at dawn, should recite this hymn on Saturday, [shall likewise attain success]. (50)
And the man who listens with faith to this hymn as it is being recited is liberated from sin and is glorified in the heavenly world. ||51||

Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, titled "The Prayer for Protection Composed by Daśaratha," in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, within the dialogue between Umāpati and Nārada. ||33||
Chapter Thirty-Four.
Nārada said:
O Lord of All, please describe in detail the vow known as Trispṛśā.
Having heard which, the world is instantly liberated from the bondage of karma. ||1||
Mahādeva said: Listen to the incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, the great vow known as Trispṛśā, which pacifies the flood of all sins and destroys great suffering. 2.
O Brahmin, listen as I describe the vow known as Trispṛśā, which grants desires to those with longing and liberation to those free from longing. (3)
O great sage, he who constantly performs the recitation of the *Trispṛśā* has effectively worshipped Keśava in this Kali age as if by direct perception.
When no preliminary purification (puraścaraṇa) has been performed, the destruction of all sins occurs merely by the Trispṛśā; of this there is no doubt. ||5||
Nor by Nāgas, nor by those beginning with Nupuras, nor by crores of Tīrthakas,
nor by many multitudes of vows, nor even by the Tridaśas who have performed worship.
O best of Brahmins, if the Trispṛśā is not observed, liberation does not occur;
for the sake of liberation, this Vaiṣṇava lunar day was ordained by the God of gods himself.
Sāṃkhya is difficult for the twice-born to understand, especially in the Kali age;
for there is no restraint of the senses, nor is there stability of mind.
For those who are detached from sense objects, who have abandoned meditative absorption and dhāraṇīs,
and who are addicted to sensual enjoyments, she bestows liberation upon those who possess the three-fold touch.
And it was previously told to me by the four-faced one (Brahmā) in the ocean,
the Milky Sea, when the wielder of the discus (Viṣṇu) had assumed the form of a fish for those who were prostrate before him.
Even those who, though joined with sense objects, practice the triple-spark yoga—though they lack the Sāṃkhya—liberation has been granted to them by me. (11)
O Great Sage, this [teaching], which bestows liberation upon those attached to the enjoyment of desires even while observing the three-fold fast, was composed by many assemblies of sages. 12.

If the *tri-spr̥śā* [lunar day] occurs during the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika, it destroys ten million sins, even when conjoined with Monday or a [Monday] born under the Moon (the Rohiṇī nakṣatra). ||13||
For the Great Lord, who was engaged in killing while observing a fast, the skull of Brahmā fell from his hand to the ground at that very moment. (14)
The goddess who flows through the three paths was liberated from the floods of millions of stains of the Kali age by the instruction of Mādhava and by fasting on the Trispṛśā day.
O Great Sage, eight murders previously committed by Bāhuvīrya were extinguished through the instruction of Bhṛgu and by fasting on the Trispṛśā day. (16)
O best of Brahmins, a Brahmin who was killed in the forest by Śatāyudha was liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin through the fast of Trispṛśā.
The sin of killing Namuci incurred by Śakra was destroyed by the fasting observed on the Trispṛśā day under the guidance of the chief of sages. 18.
O best of Brahmins, even sins such as the killing of a Brāhmaṇa dissolve through fasting on the Trispṛśā;
what then need be said regarding other sins? 19.
O best of Brahmins, liberation does not occur at Prayāga, nor at Kāśī, nor on the Gomatī, nor in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, if the Trispṛśā vow is not performed on that day.
By dying at Prayāga, at the Gomatī, or in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, eternal liberation is attained merely by bathing in the Gomatī. (21)
Liberation is attained even at home through the fast of Trispṛśā,
even for one who dwells in the midst of sensory objects and is possessed of desires and enjoyments.
Even for one who has withdrawn from sense objects, liberation is difficult to attain through Sāṃkhya alone;
therefore, O best of Brahmins, perform the Trispṛśā rite which bestows liberation.
Nārada said: What is that great vow called Triṣpṛśā, O best of gods,
which you have now described to me as the bestower of liberation for the twice-born?
Mahādeva said:
"O Brahmin, in former times this Jāhnavī was described out of compassion by Mādhava on the bank of the Prācī Sarasvatī for the sake of Trispṛś."
Jāhnavī said:
"Those who, though burdened by floods of millions of sins of the Kali age, such as the killing of a Brahmin and others, perform their bath in my waters during the Kali era, [attain purity]. (26)
O Great God, whose banner is Garuḍa, how shall their body—defiled by hundreds of sins and faults—go [to the higher realms], given its great transgression? 27.
Prācīmādhava said: "I shall tell you; do not have any doubt, O daughter of Mā, do not weep.
Śyāmavaṭa is the abode of Tumu, and Prācīdevī is before me. (28)
Having seen the Goddess of the Suras ahead on the daughter of Brahmā, perform your bath here constantly; you shall become purified. (29)
Where the daughter of Brahmā flows eastward, there I am; of this there is no doubt.
Endowed with hundreds of millions of sacred fords, I dwell together with the gods.
This sacred place, dear to me, which destroys ten million killings, was granted by me out of satisfaction, because they are dearer to me than my own life. (31)
O Jāhnavī, by my command, thousands of millions of sacred fords remain eternally present in the waters of the Prācī Sarasvatī at all times.

From killing a Brahmin, from drinking liquor, from killing a cow, from killing a low-caste woman, from seizing the property of a Brahmin, and likewise from failing to honor one's mother and father; ||33||

Due to the transgression of the wheel, due to treachery against the guru, due to the eating of what is unfit to be eaten, and due to the committing of every sin—[one must bathe] in the daughter of the eastern daughter of Brahmā. (34)
"O best of rivers, perform your bath before me; it shall dispel all sins entirely, and you shall become free from evil. (35)
Jāhnavī said:
"O Lord of Gods, I am indeed unable to come constantly;
tell me, O Mādhava, how my sins may be destroyed. (36)
Prācīmādhava said:
"O Daughter of Jahnu, since you are unable to come [to me] constantly,
I shall then explain something else from which my feet have originated."
It is superior to the Sarasvatī, superior to hundreds of millions of sacred fords, superior even to ten million sacrifices, and superior to all vows and gifts. (38)

Let this auspicious Trispṛśā rite be performed, which bestows the fruits of the four goals of human life for those devoted to recitation and fire-offerings, and the fruits of Sāṃkhya and Yoga for those devoted to them. (39)
In whichever month the full moon arrives, O best of rivers, that [observance] should be performed on the day of the full moon; by doing so, one is liberated from sin. (40)
Jāhnavī said:
"O Sumādhava, tell me what this Trispṛśā is like,
since you have just now described its greatness to me."
O Lord, when the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth lunar days (Bhadrā) coincide on a single day, that is known as Trispṛśā; please explain this correctly to me. 42.
Kṛṣṇa said: The goddess Āsurītrispṛśā, whom you have described,
must be avoided with great effort, just as a husband is abandoned by a wife who lacks virtuous conduct.
The *tusāra* (frost) of the Asuras is said to destroy life-force and strength;
it should be avoided with great effort, just like a woman in her menses. 44.

Having abandoned one's own caste and entered into lower castes, that very [caste] must be especially avoided; likewise, a day joined with the tenth lunar mansion (Aśvinī) and a cold day [must be avoided]. 45.
Just as those devoid of knowledge are defiled by contact with a woman in her courses,
so too is my day defiled for men when it is joined with the tenth lunar day.
One who fasts on the Trispṛśā day destroys a hundred thousand murders:
when the eleventh lunar day (Ekādaśī) lasts through the day and night, and the twelfth (Dvādaśī) extends into the remainder of the night [and the thirteenth (Trayodaśī) follows]. 47.
The Trispṛśā [Ekādaśī] should be known as one that is not joined with the tenth day;
for even after committing an offense, a man may be liberated by performing the appropriate expiation. 48.
O Ganges, you cannot endure the defect born from the piercing of the tenth lunar day;
by him [who observes it], the consumption of the Hālāhala poison has been ingested.
Thinking, "The Ekādaśī vow has been performed by someone who mixed it with the tenth day," one must not observe my day when it is joined with the tenth. (50)
The merit accumulated over ten million lifetimes is exhausted within one's continuum;
such a person causes their own family to fall from heaven and leads them to the Aurasava and other hells.
Having purified one's own body, this day of mine (Mama-vāsara) must be observed;
it is to be abandoned when there is *vṛddhi* (increase in lunar days), and it is joined with [the asterisms] Śravaṇa and others even without the *vedha* (piercing conjunction).
The merit of birth goes to destruction for those who observe the fast on Ekādaśī;
this is especially so when there is a doubt regarding the increase of the lunar day. (53)
By my command, the beloved Dvādaśī must be observed. ||54||
Jāhnavī said:
"O Lord of the World, I shall do as you have commanded;
by your command, I shall be completely liberated from all sins. (55)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "Go to your own abode; may it be well with you. You should never fear anything. O best of rivers, no sin shall be transferred to you. (56)
Those who, having bathed in the waters of the Sarasvatī and having worshipped Mādhava,
bow down to the Lord of the World, go to the supreme goal.
Jāhnavī said:
"O Brāhmaṇa, tell me the ritual procedure; I shall perform it with my very life.
I shall propitiate Dāmodara, the Lord of Gods, who is free from all ailment. (58)
Prācīmādhava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the ritual procedure for Trispṛśā;
having heard it, O best of rivers, a man is liberated from his sins. (59)
"An image of me should be fashioned out of gold—using a *pala*, half a *pala*, or even half of that—as far as one's wealth permits. (60)
They should prepare a vessel made of copper filled with water, as well as a bright jar containing water and endowed with the five precious gems. ||61||
After bathing and anointing [the image], one should subsequently install Dāmodara, who is encircled by flower garlands and perfumed with camphor and agallochum.
Then the investiture should be performed, accompanied by a pair of garments;
worship should be performed with mantras proclaimed in the Purāṇas, using auspicious flowers produced in season and tender leaves of tulasī. (63)
One should offer an umbrella to Viṣṇu, well-joined with a pair of sandals, as well as many pleasing offerings and fruits. (64)
A new, firm sacred thread (upavīta), along with an upper garment, should be given;
he should cause a bamboo staff to be given that is handsome, straight, and firm.
One should worship the feet with "Salutation to Dāmodara," the knees with "Salutation to Mādhava," the private parts with "Salutation to Kāmaprada," and the waist with "Salutation to Vāmanamūrti."
I bow to the navel of Padmanābha, to the belly of the source of the universe,
to the heart of him who is attainable through knowledge, and to the throat of the one who goes to Vaikuṇṭha.

Having worshipped according to the rules with devotion Him who has a thousand arms, whose arms are His eyes, and who possesses the form of Yoga, one should offer the *argha* oblation according to the prescribed rite.
Indeed, with a bright coconut placed upon the conch and wrapped with threads on both hands as well; 69.
O Janārdana, you are remembered as the one who daily removes sins,
as well as bad dreams and ill omens conceived by a troubled mind.
O Mahādeva, whatever fear of hell, of gods, or of miserable rebirths may arise for me—whether pertaining to this world or the next—[may it be removed]. (71)
Therefore, O Lord, protect me; accept this *argha*; salutations to You!
May Your merciful glance fall upon me, O Dāmodara. (72)
One should offer incense, lamps, and food offerings, and then perform the lustration ceremony (nīrājana);
one should then wave a lotus flower over the head of Hari with the most excellent river water.
Having performed this rite, one should then worship one's own guru;
one should give gold, garments, a turban, and a tunic.
Sandals, an umbrella, a ring, a water-pot, food, betel-leaf, seven kinds of grain, and a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). ||75||
Having worshipped the Guru, the Lord of Gods, one should perform a vigil for Hari, accompanied by song and dance, as well as the study of the scriptures. (76)
At the end of the night, having offered arghya to the deity according to the prescribed rite,
and having performed the rites such as bathing, one should eat together with the brāhmaṇas.
Śiva said:
O twice-born one, by hearing this wonderful and hair-raising narrative called Trispṛśā, one obtains the merit arising from bathing in the Gaṅgā. (78)
One obtains the fruit of thousands of horse-sacrifices and hundreds of Vājapeya sacrifices by fasting on the Trispṛśā day. ||79||
Together with his paternal kin, his maternal kin, and likewise his own kin—released from all of them—he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. ||80||
Whatever merit is found in ten million sacred fords (tīrtha) and whatever fruit is found in ten million holy sites (kṣetra),
one obtains that same fruit by fasting on the Trispṛśā day.
Even Kṣatriyas with darkened minds perform [this] for Brāhmaṇas,
as do Vaiśyas, those born as Śūdras, and likewise those of other castes.
O best of the twice-born, they all attain liberation after leaving this earth;
for among all mantras, the twelve-syllabled mantra is indeed the king of mantras. (83)
And just as this Trispṛśā has been performed by some as a vow,
it was not previously established by Brahmā, but was later performed by royal sages.
O Brahmin, for others who touch [the water] three times, this Trispṛśā vow, which bestows liberation like a mere conversation with a crow, arises through this procedure. (85)
Listen, O Brahmin, as I shall describe the fruit for that man who performs this with devotion:
it is the same fruit as that obtained by bathing in the Gaṅgā at Vārāṇasī.
The fruit that is obtained by bathing in the Yamunā for ten million years is attained by merely touching the Prācī with three steps.
A man who performs the Trispṛśā vow obtains that same fruit as one would by ten million solar eclipses at Kurukṣetra. (88)
Even by gifts of hundreds of loads of gold on the occasion of the Trispṛśā festival, that [merit] is not equal [to the merit of observing the vow];
for it destroys thousands of crores of sins and hundreds of crores of killings. (89)
By a single fast alone, that which is known as the Trispṛśā vow—which grants a destination to those who have no destination—is swiftly reduced to ashes. (90)
O brahmin-sage, even hundreds of great sins seek their own destruction when spoken by Kṛṣṇa himself in the presence of the son of Parāśara. (91)
O twice-born one, for whoever writes this Vaiṣṇava work and makes it known, there shall be liberation even for one who is bound by a multitude of sins. (92)
O learned one, even after hundreds of Manvantaras, it is attained through merits;
yet the Trispṛśā, which is difficult to find in this world, is obtained by men only through such merit. 93.
If, having obtained the Trispṛśā [conjunction] during the Kali age, the lowest of men do not perform [the rites], their fruit of birth and their very life shall be in vain. 94.

O wise one, even those who lacked the means for ancestral rites and were without sons have completely crossed over the state of being a preta by performing the Trispṛśā rite even once during the Kali age. ||95||

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, titled "The Narrative of Trispṛśā," in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, within the dialogue between Umāpati and Nārada. ||34||
Chapter Thirty-Five.
Mahādeva said:
Therefore, I shall fully explain to you the unsurpassed Unmīlanī [Vidyā].
By the mere hearing of which, one is liberated from the bondage of birth and saṃsāra. ||1||
The evil-souled man is liberated from sins and is glorified in the heavenly world;
even the gods and the ancestors shall attain his presence.
A seeker of knowledge obtains knowledge and shall attain all desires;
by observing this vow, there is no doubt that he is glorified in the heavenly world. ||3||
Having reached his own abode there, he is glorified in the world of Śiva;
therefore, O King, you should perform the worship of the Vaiṣṇavas. ||4||
O King, as for those who constantly perform service for the Vaiṣṇavas, the lord of men did not inflict punishment upon them. ||5||
O King, after their meal, he partakes of food;
for Viṣṇu is worshipped by those very people by whom He has been worshipped with devotion.
O protector of the earth, you daily wear with great devotion around your neck the Śālagrāma stone, which has become the embodiment of the goddess Mūrdhanī. (7)
O King, you devotedly partake of the remnants of Viṣṇu’s incense;
O Lord of men, having always performed the *ārārtika* ceremony, you cause it to be known among the devotees.
O Śeṣa, having devoutly whirled auspicious water over the head of Hari,
you constantly bear it upon your own head and bestow it upon the Vaiṣṇavas.
O Brahmana, having prepared the food offering every day along with all necessary ingredients and having given it to Viṣvaksena, you should then eat yourself.
The food offered to Viṣṇu is eaten together with the Vaiṣṇavas;
daily, with devotion, he praises Janārdana by means of the Thousand Names.
O best of kings, you perform the offering of lamps and water for Viṣṇu, and you engage in song and dance; you worship Śyāmā with kura flowers—thus you worship the one worthy of worship. 12.

The worship of Śyāmā with *kura* flowers along with the constant worship of Vatsa is extremely rare to obtain; yet, when performed with *dūrvā* grass, it yields merit equal to the gift of the entire earth. (13)
Therefore, there is nothing else in this world on earth equal to dūrvā grass;
one who desires union with Viṣṇu should perform worship with it. 14.
Therefore, you should always perform worship with dūrvā grass;
specifically, you should perform worship with barley and unbroken rice grains. 15.
O best of kings, O great monarch, the Dvādaśī vow which was performed by you in every fortnight according to the rules is the destroyer of great sins. 16.
Bestowing liberation, bestowing happiness, and always bestowing long life—this is declared to be the Viṣṇu-vow, which grants liberation to the Vaiṣṇavas. (17)
It bestows happiness upon householders and grants liberation to ascetics;
it pacifies all diseases and the like, and is pure, purifying the body. (18)
O lord of men, perform this very vow, or indeed cause it to be performed; observe it free from the overlap of the tenth day and accompanied by a vigil. (19)
O best of kings, you daily worship Hari with heaps of Tulasī leaves,
and you wear on your forehead a mark made from Gopīcandana paste.
O King, it is worn by all the worlds as a means of purification;
therefore, you too wear that which originates from Gopīcandana.
A killer of a Brahmin, a stealer of gold, a drinker of liquor, likewise one who has approached those who should not be approached, a cow-killer, a great sinner, and a speaker of falsehood; ||22||
All those who diligently wear this *tilaka* attain liberation;
do you not always wear one made from the *dhātrī* fruit around your neck? (23)
A garland made of ten thousand primary tulasī leaves, joined with a śālagrāma stone originating from Dvārakā; ||24||
O King, you constantly worship the Purāṇa named Padma, which bestows the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation; and you recite it before Lord Hari. (25)
O King, [I have related] the life of Prahlāda, the king of the Daityas,
and the day of Vāsudeva, which bestows all spiritual merit upon those men who perform it.
O protector of the earth, having diligently examined the scriptures, you should prohibit [the practice] in that kingdom where the day of Viṣṇu, along with its prescribed rites, prevails.
By being stained with that sin, the king becomes a denizen of hell;
yet, having abandoned the fourfold piercing and fasted on the day of Hari,
he uplifts ten million members of his lineage and is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
Gautama said: Listen, O King, I shall describe the great vow known as Vaiṣṇava;
by hearing which, even all sinners attain liberation at that very moment. (29)
I have declared this merit arising from the twelfth day (dvādaśī) to no one else.
O great king, you are a devotee of Viṣṇu among men; therefore, listen to that most secret vow of the Vaiṣṇavas as described in the Bhāgavata. 31.
O King, I shall relate to you that which was told by Mādhava, who was well-pleased, out of his ancient devotion to me, to Unmīlanī. 32.
If a single ghaṭikā remains at dawn on the eleventh day (ekādaśī), that should be known as Unmīlanī;
it is especially dear to Hari.
Whatever holy fords, sacred places, sacrifices, Vedas, and austerities exist in the three worlds, they are all equal to only a ten-millionth part of this.
There is nothing that has been, nor will there ever be, equal to Unmīlanī;
neither Prayāga, nor Kurukṣetra, nor Kāśī, nor Puṣkara.
Neither the Himalaya mountain, nor Meru, nor Gandhamādana;
neither Nīla, Niṣadha, nor Vindhya, nor even Naimiṣa. (36)
The Godāvarī, Narmadā, Kāverī, Candrabhāgā, Navedikā, Natā, Pīnā, Payoṣṇī, Nak, Kṣiprā, and Navacandanā; 37.
The Carmaṇvatī, the Sarayū, the Candrabhāgā, the Nagaṇḍikā, the Gomatī, the Vipāśā, and the great river known as the Śoṇa. ||38||
O Lord of Men, what need is there for further repeated words here?
There is nothing whatsoever equal to the Unmīlanī [mantra], and no deity other than Keśava. (39)
Having reached Unmīlanī, those who have performed the worship of Keśava find that the heaps of their multitudes of sins fall away in an instant. (40)
In whichever month the lunar day known as Unmīlanī occurs for the protector of the earth, Govinda should be worshipped with great effort under the name of that month. 41.
Endowed with faith and devotion, Mādhava, who is Viśvarūpa, should fashion a seat out of gold according to his own ability. ||42||
A water-pot joined with purifying water, endowed with the five jewels,
provided with scents, flowers, and unbroken grains of rice, and adorned with garlands and wreaths.
A vessel should be prepared filled with wheat, joined with various jewels, and honored with various fragrances. ||44||
It should be diligently filled with jasmine flowers endowed with the fragrance of *mallikā*, worshipped with *jātī* blossoms, and likewise with white *dūla* flowers. 45.
One should present a pair of garments and an excellent sacred thread;
O royal sage, a pair of sandals and an umbrella over the head.
Food, a water-vessel, and the seven grains along with salt, silver, cotton, and a ring for Hari— having prepared these together— 47.
A cow that destroys [the cycle of] rebirth should be given away, accompanied by a calf and a bronze vessel;
likewise, its horns should be made of gold, its hooves of silver, and its back of copper.
At that time, one should give a cow with a bronze milking vessel and a jeweled tail to a Vaidya;
furthermore, one should devoutly present a bed with its furnishings to a virtuous person.
One should offer incense, lamps, food offerings, fruits, and leaves;
Keśava is to be worshipped by those of great devotion with these mantras. (50)
With flowers produced in season accompanied by *tulasī* leaves, one should worship the two feet and the two knees with the names of the months, [addressing them] as having the form of Viṣṇu.
O Secret One, O Lord of Secrets, O Sole One, O You clad in yellow garments!
O You who bear the form of Brahmā, O Source of the Universe within Your belly! 52.
To the one accessible through the knowledge in the heart, to the Vaikuṇṭha-form in the throat;
to the upward-moving one on the forehead, and to the destroyer of the wicked in the arm. ||53||

One should worship the supreme [form] with the mantra "O Lord of the Ganas," and all [forms] with "O you who possess all forms"; likewise, one's own weapons and other implements should be worshipped with devotion using their respective names. (54)
The offering of *argha* should be performed together with coconuts and other such items;
having placed water upon a conch shell, it should be provided with fragrance, flowers, and unbroken grains (*akṣata*).
Having wrapped it with a thread, one should offer the *argha* according to the ritual injunctions:
"O God of gods, Great God, Śrī Keśava, Janārdana! (56)
O Subrahmaṇya, homage be to you, who increase the mass of merit;
lift me up from the ocean of existence, which is filled with the great evils of grief and delusion. (57)
Not even in hundreds of millions of births has any good deed been performed;
nevertheless, O Great Lord, deliver me from the ocean of existence! (58)
O Lord of Gods, by this vow, those others who were my ancestors,
as well as others who have entered into inferior wombs or fallen under the power of an untimely death, [shall be liberated].
Those who will be in the future and those who have passed away—deliver them from the world of the departed!
I am weary; my devotion to you, the Independent One, is unwavering. (60)
"O wielder of the mace, accept this arghya offered by me with devotion;
having offered the arghya, worship Viṣṇu with incense, lamps, and food offerings consisting of the products of Viṣṇu. (61)
One should satisfy Hari with hymns of praise, lustration rites, songs, and servants;
one should satisfy the guru with garments, gifts, gifts of cows, and meals.
One should act in such a manner that the guru may obtain satisfaction,
since the guru was created by the Creator for the sake of delivering the worlds.
Therefore, the worship of the Guru must indeed be performed with great effort;
he destroys what is harmful and always reveals what is beneficial. 64.
That guru should be known as one who possesses the [true] meaning and is skilled in the purpose of all dharmas;
without practicing deceit regarding his wealth, he should present himself to that [guru]. (65)
Once the offering has been presented to the Guru, the vow becomes complete;
having first performed the ritual of *ātana*, one should partake of the meal together with the Brahmins.
O tiger among kings, this day should be spent with sacred narratives;
by this procedure, one should perform the Unmīlanī vow. (67)
They shall dwell in the presence of Viṣṇu for thousands of millions of kalpas.

Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter, titled "The Unmīlanī Vow," in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, within the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, in the dialogue between Umāpati and Nārada. ||35||
The thirty-sixth chapter.
Nārada said:
What is the nature of that which is known as Mahādevapakṣavardhanī?
By performing this sacrifice once, one is liberated from great sin. ||1||
Śrī Mahādeva said:
When the new moon day becomes full, it then arises as a complete [fortnight];
having become sixty nāḍikās, it arises on the first day of the lunar fortnight (pratipad).
That [practice] which increases one's side (or fortnight) would be equal to ten thousand horse-sacrifices. ||2||
Nārada said:
O best of gods, I ask you about the procedure for worshiping her,
by performing which one may obtain great fruit from Mahādeva.
Mahādeva said:
O delighter of the twice-born, I shall now proclaim the procedure for the worship of Sāṃprata;
when Viṣṇu is worshipped and honored, one obtains the fruit [of this] without a doubt. (4)
By whatever ritual of worship Mādhava attains satisfaction—[namely], a flawless water-pot filled with water and adorned with sandalwood paste. (5)
A copper vessel, endowed with the five jewels and encircled by a garland of flowers,
should be placed upon a jar together with wheat.
One should have an image of the deity named Māsa made of gold; then, according to the prescribed rite, one should perform a beautiful ablution with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
One should have the Lord of the gods, the Master of the world, the Lord of the universe, fashioned;
and anointing should be performed with saffron, kumkuma, agaru, and sandalwood.
A pair of garments, along with an umbrella and sandals, should be offered;
one should worship the Lord of Devas seated upon the vessel atop the water-pot.

To the one whose feet are like the navel of a lotus, salutations; to the one whose form is the universe, salutations to his knees; to the one who is accessible through supreme knowledge, salutations to his thighs; and to the one who bestows the gift of generosity, salutations to his hips.
The belly to Viśvanātha, the heart to Śrīdhara, the throat to Kaustubhakaṇṭha, and the arms to Kṣatrāntakārin. ||11||
One should worship the forehead with "Vyoma," the head with "Mūrdhan," and the entire form with "Śiras";
and one should worship the lotus with its own name and the entire divine-syllabled speech (Gī) with "Sarvā. ||12||
Having thus worshipped according to the prescribed rite, the wise one should then offer the arghya water to the God of gods, the wielder of the discus, using a bright coconut.
By this very offering of arghya, the vow becomes complete.
O Lord of the World, lift me up, for I am submerged in the ocean of saṃsāra. (14)
You are the Lord of all worlds; you are manifestly the Master of the universe.
Accept this water offering given by me; salutations to You, O Padmanābha! (15)
Food offerings that are wholesome and especially possess the six flavors should be given with particular devotion to Keśava. (16)
One should devoutly offer a betel leaf with camphor to the Lord;
furthermore, one should offer a lamp with ghee or with sesame oil. (17)
Having performed the worship of the Guru according to the correct procedure,
one should cause garments, a turban, and a jacket to be presented.
And one should cause the preceptor to receive a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to one's ability;
having offered food and betel, one should then cause the water offering (argha) to be presented.
Those who are destitute of wealth should perform the Dvādaśī Pakṣavardhinī with effort according to their ability, using inference from their own means, by means of a proper exertion. 20.
Then one should observe a vigil accompanied by song and dance, together with the recitation of Purāṇas, and filled with laughter and joy. (21)
Those who praise and extol the Wielder of the Discus while awake shall have a perpetual festival in their homes for ten births.
Therefore, this most auspicious rite, which increases one's side [of merit], must be performed;
having performed it, one undoubtedly attains the fruit of all merit. ||23||
Those wise ones who hear the greatness of Pakṣavardhanī have performed every act of merit until the dissolution of all beings.
Whatever merit may be obtained from the practice of the five fires or from visiting sacred pilgrimage sites, one attains that same merit by performing a vigil for Viṣṇu. 25.
This merit-increasing Pakṣavarddhanikā is a purifier that destroys sin;
it destroys ten million killings committed during the observance of a fast. ||26||
O son of Muni, this [stotra], which was formerly composed by Vasiṣṭha and Bhāradvāja, and performed by Dhruva and Ambarīṣa, is beloved by Viṣṇu. 27.
This [place] is equal in merit to Kāśī; this is equal to Dvārakā.
Fasted with a single meal, it grants whatever is desired.
This [practice] is most auspicious, the destroyer of ten thousand sins;
it must be performed especially by Vaiṣṇavas who are devoted to knowledge. 29.
The Lord who is the master of all must be served by those intent on their vows;
what more need be said? This supreme vow must be performed. (30)
Just as the moon increases especially during the bright fortnight,
so too does the Pakṣavardhinī [vow] increase because of devotion.
Just as darkness perishes at the moment of sunrise,
even so does sin meet its destruction through the performance of Pakṣavardhinī.

Thus ends the "Glorious Majesty of the Ekādaśī that Increases the Fortnight," titled the dialogue between Umāpati and Nārada, within the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Śrī-Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses.
Chapter Thirty-Six ||36||
(37) Chapter Thirty-Seven.
Mahādeva said:
Listen, O Nārada, I shall speak of the majesty of the vigil (jāgara);
by hearing which, even a great sinner attains liberation, without a doubt. (1)
Nārada said:
"Oh, Viṣṇu is the Lord of the Universe and the eternal purifier!
Indeed, O Śiva, I have heard from your own lips the greatness of fasting unto him."
Nevertheless, I wish to hear about the majesty of the vigil:
what is the nature of the majesty of the vigil, and what is the nature of devotion during the night? (3)
O Lord, Master of the Universe, tell me of the worship performed during the watches of the day;
for you are always worthy of worship in all worlds, for you, O Janārdana, are indeed the God.
You are indeed the God, the Lord of the Universe, since devotion is centered upon Janārdana. (4)
Among all devotees indeed, you, O Lord of Umā, are the most excellent;
in this world, your name always exists eternally through devotion. (5)
Therefore, O Lord of the Universe, tell me by what means liberation indeed comes to people, and describe the greatness of the vigil.
Mahādeva said:
On the eleventh day, having worshipped Viṣṇu with devotion at night,
a person should keep a vigil before Viṣṇu together with the Vaiṣṇavas.
Song, instrumental music, as well as dance, and likewise the recitation of the Purāṇas;
incense, lamps, food offerings, flowers, perfumes, and ointments. ||8||
O best of Brahmins, [these are]: fruit, honor, as well as faith, charity, restraint of the senses, speech endowed with truth, and action joined with [right] conduct. (9)
The man who always performs [this] with joy and free from drowsiness becomes liberated from all sins and is beloved by Viṣṇu. ||10||
When the time for keeping a night vigil has arrived, those Vaiṣṇavas who indeed sleep have lost their fast and their vow dedicated to Viṣṇu. 11.
O wise one, those men who perform the vigil known as Viṣṇu-jāgara with devotion to Kṛṣṇa never sleep again. (12)
Those who repeatedly utter the name of Kṛṣṇa with their minds are to be known as most blessed, especially on this night. (13)
At every moment, however, the gift of a cow is multiplied fourfold at each *ghaṭī*;
it is multiplied ten million times during a *prahara*, and becomes incalculable during these four watches of the day.
But for one who remains awake for even half a moment before Keśava, that fruit is multiplied ten millionfold; its measure cannot be known. (15)
That best of men who performs a dance before Keśava does not lose his merit from birth until the end of death. ||16||
Full of wonder and enthusiasm, free from sinful talk and the like, accompanied by circumambulation, and preceded by prostrations. ||17||
O highly fortunate one, with an undaunted mind, you should perform the *ārātrika* rite for Hari during this watch of the night, accompanied by the *nīrājana* ceremony. (18)
The man who, endowed with devotion, performs the vigil on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī) joined with the twenty-six virtues, is not born again on this earth. (19)
Whoever performs the vigil for Viṣṇu on this day with devotion, free from stinginess regarding wealth, merges into the Supreme Self. (20)
That wealthy man who does not suffer sleeplessness over the embezzlement of his riches has surely lost his own soul through that wicked gambler. 21.
He who mocks when the vigil for Viṣṇu has arrived shall be born as a worm in excrement for sixty thousand years. (22)
A Brahmin who knows the Vedas, yet especially delights in dancing and is intent on derision, is indeed called a Cāṇḍāla. ||23||
He who remains awake for even a moment or half a moment attains the imperishable state of virtue, wealth, pleasure, and liberation. ||24||
One who is constantly devoted to the Vedas and Shastras, and who always performs sacrifices, falls into a low state if he engages in criticism when the time for a night vigil has arrived. (25)
One who performs my worship while being intent on reviling Viṣṇu goes to hell along with twenty-one generations of his lineage. ||26||
"Viṣṇu is Śiva and Śiva is Viṣṇu; they exist as a single form divided into two.
Therefore, under no circumstances should one utter censure [of either].
Those bitten by the serpent of the Kali age sleep during the day of the honey-thief (the month of Madhava). (27)
Those who have reached the Ekādaśī in the Kali age without keeping a vigil are deluded by illusion and do not keep a vigil at all. (28)
They have perished without a doubt, because life is transient;
yet by giving away his pair of eyes, he has attained the station of Viṣṇu. (29)
By performing this very Hari-jāgara, even sinners behold [the Lord];
furthermore, in the absence of a reciter, one should have singing and dancing performed.
O divine sage, when there is a reciter, one should first read the Purāṇa;
it is equal to a thousand horse sacrifices and ten thousand Vājapeya sacrifices.
O child, O Brahmin, when a vigil for Viṣṇu is performed during the fortnight of the ancestors, the fortnight of the mother, or the fortnight of the wife, the merit is multiplied ten millionfold.
By performing a vigil for Hari on the day of the fast, even when it is intercalary, one uplifts these very families; [therein lies] the vigil and the worship of Hari. (33)
Just as all gifts and other acts performed for those who are ungrateful are in vain,
so too is the observance of staying awake during the vigil on a day when the fast has been commenced on an intercalary (defective) lunar day.
Having left that place and having uttered a curse, Viṣṇu departs;
those who perform the all-night vigil on a day other than that of Viṣṇu are as if pierced by a thorn. ||35||
Among them, Hari, being pleased,
performs a dance for as many days as he keeps a vigil before Keśava.
For as many days as one dwells without performing the vigil for Hari, for that many ages one is honored in the world of Viṣṇu. (37)
For that many thousands of years one does not return from Raurava,
if one lies down on the eleventh lunar day without performing the vigil for Hari.
He who remains like a mute and does not practice the recitation of the Gānas shall be born mute for seven lifetimes due to his lack of vigilance regarding Hari.
O Brahmana, know that he who, being utterly deluded in soul, dances before Lord Hari while He is awake,
shall suffer lameness for seven births.
Furthermore, for one who performs song, dance, and the vigil for Hari, his status is truly Brahma-like, mine, and indeed Vaiṣṇava. 41.
The Vaiṣṇava who awakens people and is devoted to the vigil of Viṣṇu shall dwell for a long time in Vaikuṇṭha together with his ancestors. ||42||
The man who offers his counsel regarding the vigil for Hari shall dwell in Śvetadvīpa for sixty thousand years. ||43||
Whatever sin has been committed by human beings throughout ten million lifetimes, all of it is destroyed during the night of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s vigil, O Vāḍava. 44.
For those who perform a vigil before a Śālagrāma stone, it is declared that for every watch (yāma) they obtain the fruit arising from ten million lunar fasts (aindavāni). ||45||
When the day of Viṣṇu has arrived, those who do not perform the vigil (jāgara) find that all they have done becomes fruitless, due to their censure of the Vaiṣṇavas. (46)
Sensual pleasures, wealth, prosperity, sons, fame, and eternal worlds—these are not obtained even through ten thousand sacrifices without the night-vigil on the twelfth day. 47.
He whose mind does not incline toward keeping the vigil on the twelfth day has no eligibility whatsoever for the worship of Keśava.
As many steps as one takes while proceeding toward the abode of Keśava for the purpose of keeping vigil, so many merits equal to the Aśvamedha sacrifice shall be attained. 49.
As long as one remains fallen upon the earth, with dust clinging to one's feet,
for that many thousands of years does one dwell in heaven in a state of wakefulness.
Therefore, one should depart from that house for the vigil at the temple of Keśava during the twelve Dvādaśīs, which destroy the impurities of the Kali age.
My mind was occupied with slandering others, devoid of serenity, lacking the guidance of the scriptures, wandering aimlessly, and likewise deprived of the lamp of wisdom. (52)
Devoid of power and ritual service, indifferent, accompanied by reproach, joined with strife, and especially characterized by wakefulness—this is known as the ninefold state. (53)
Accompanied by the scriptures, with the vigil consisting of dance, song, and the Gandharvas, joined with musical instruments and rhythmic beats, together with lamps and offerings of honey. (54)
Accompanied by loud sounds, as previously described, and imbued with devotion, it is pleasing, generates satisfaction, and delights the deluded people of the world. (55)
Endowed with twelve qualities, the vigil (jāgara) dear to Mādhava should be performed with effort during both the bright and dark fortnights. (56)

What is the use of performing many vows, or what is the use of dwelling at sacred pilgrimage sites for him who, when the day of the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī) has arrived, does not perform the vigil (jāgara) for Hari? 57.
But he who, O Āḍavā, does not abandon the vigil for Vāsudeva on the twelfth day even when exhausted on a journey while traveling abroad—he is dear to me. (58)
My devotee who, deluded by sin, does not perform the vigil for Hari,
his worship of me is in vain— he who does not worship that which is worthy of my worship.
He who eats on the day of Viṣṇu is neither a Śaiva, nor a Saura, nor a Śākta, nor a servant of the Gaṇas; indeed, he should be known as worse than a beast. (60)
An offense has been committed by that very wicked and sinful man,
who, relying on the power of my devotion, eats indeed on the day of Hari.
Those who perform the vigil for Viṣṇu on this day are liberated from their bodies, which are both internal and external, though encircled by millions of sins.
By him who observed the vigil for Viṣṇu and performed the unbroken vow of the twelfth day (dvādaśī-vrata), his elbow was given to the messengers of Yama and to Yama himself.
By that very act, the doubt of even the best of sages who aspire for heaven is dispelled;
having pierced through [the cycle of birth], they attain the desired happiness of the hells by making a single day of Hari pass.
By him the Pitṛs were slain and the destruction of the gods was brought about;
the kingdom was given to the Daityas after making the day of Hari pierced.
With a heart exceedingly joyful, he danced without striking anyone;
singing with his mouth, he displayed many wonders.
Standing before Vāsudeva during the night vigil,
he recited the deeds of Kṛṣṇa while joyfully praising the hosts of Vaiṣṇavas.
With his hair standing on end from joy, he plays music with his mouth,
displaying various types of servants and engaging in conversations according to his own whim.
Whatever merit a man performs during the vigil for Hari through these dispositions is said to yield, moment by moment, the fruit of ten million sacred pilgrimage sites.
But he who, with an undisturbed mind, performs the incense offering and the lustration rite for Hari during the night vigil, shall become the sovereign of the seven continents.
Whatever sins there may be, even those equal to the killing of a Brahmin,
all of them go to destruction, piece by piece, through the vigil for Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī.
On one side are all the sacrifices completed with the bestowal of excellent sacrificial fees; on the other side is the vigil for the God of gods, which is dear to Kṛṣṇa. (72)
Therein are Kāśī, Puṣkara, Prayāga, Naimiṣa, Gayā,
the great field of Śālagrāma, and the Arbuda forest.
Indeed, at Mathurā, all the sacred fords (tīrthas) including Pauṣkara, as well as the four Vedas and the sacrifices, attend the vigil for Hari. 74.
The Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Tāpī, Yamunā, Śatadrū, Candrabhāgā, and Vitastā—all these rivers are indeed present there. (75)
O best of the twice-born, all lakes, ponds, and indeed all oceans go to the vigil for Kṛṣṇa on the eleventh day. (76)
Men who, during the vigil for Kṛṣṇa, dance and sing, delighted by the playing of lutes, become objects of envy even for the gods and serpents. (77)
Having thus kept vigil and worshipped the Great Hari,
one should break the fast on the twelfth day along with Vaiṣṇavas, according to one's own capacity.
Mahādeva said:
Listen, O Brahmin, I shall proclaim the supreme majesty of Dvādaśī;
for Dvādaśī is always to be known as the bestower of sons, wealth, and liberation. (79)
Having bathed in the morning and worshipped Hari, one should offer the fast with these words:
"O Keśava, by this vow, may the darkness of my ignorance be destroyed. (80)
"Be gracious and become one with a pleasant countenance; grant the vision of knowledge.
Then, one should perform the breaking of the fast (pāraṇa) before [the deity] according to what is available. (81)
From this point forward, one should perform [the rites] as desired according to the prescribed rule;
however, O twice-born, when the twelfth day (dvādaśī) is very short, it should be observed until the breaking of the fast.
Therefore, one who desires liberation should perform the breaking of the fast (pāraṇa) during the night;
in that case, the fault of "nocturnal fasting" (anarātri-doṣa) would not apply, nor would it ever be prohibited.

As it has been said: "One should not bathe at night, nor should one eat during the middle of the night; for the first and last watches of the night, one should perform one's duties as if it were day. (84)
When the twelfth day (dvādaśī) for breaking the fast becomes very short,
one should perform both the morning and the midday rites at dawn.
I am not capable of describing the specific merit of that man by whom the Dvādaśī has been observed at all times on this earth. ||86||
Having accomplished all their desires, the great people, including Ambarīṣa and all others who are renowned on earth as devotees, attained [the supreme goal]. ||87||
Having accomplished the twelfth day [of the lunar fortnight], they have gone to the abode of Viṣṇu;
this which has been told by me to you is true, true, and again true. (88)
There is no god equal to Viṣṇu, nor is there a lunar day equal to the twelfth;
whatever is given, eaten, or offered in worship here [on that day] is likewise [infinite]. (89)
All that reaches fulfillment when Mādhava is worshipped;
what need is there for much speaking? Hari is beloved by his devotees. (90)
It bestows all desires until the dissolution of all beings;
whatever is given on the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī), all that shall become fruitful.
O best of divine sages, just as that which is given at Kurukṣetra never becomes fruitless, so too does that which is given on the twelfth day [of the lunar fortnight] become so. 92.

Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Vigil on the Twelfth and Eleventh Days," in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, within the dialogue between Umāpati and Nārada.
[38] The thirty-eighth chapter. Mahādeva said:
Once, having gone to my son, I was in the presence of Viṣṇu;
there, I previously asked about the greatness arising from the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī).
Nārada said:
O Mahādeva, what is this supreme Mahādvādaśikā like? O Lord of all, tell me what the fruit of its vow is.
Śiva said:
O Brāhmaṇa, this Ekādaśī bestows the fruit of great merit;
it should be observed by the best of sages when conjoined with specific lunar mansions (ṛkṣa). ||3||
Jayā, Vijayā, and Jayantī, who destroys sins—these [mantras] which remove all evils should be performed by those desiring results. (4)
When the Punarvasu asterism occurs on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight, that lunar day is known by the name Jayā; it is the most excellent among all lunar days. (5)
By fasting on that day, a person is liberated from sin; of this there is no doubt.
And when the Śravaṇa asterism occurs on the twelfth lunar day of the bright fortnight (Śukla-dvādaśī), [that is the time].
The day known as Vijayā is the most excellent of lunar days;
on that day, the feeding of Brahmins yields a gift multiplied a thousandfold. (7)
Likewise, when the Prājāpatya yoga occurs on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight, the performance of oblations and fasting yields a thousandfold fruit. ||8||
That lunar day is called Jayantī; it removes all sins, whether the sin committed over seven lifetimes be small or great. (9)
Govinda certainly bathes in that [river] when he has been worshipped, whenever the Puṣya asterism occurs on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight. (10)
That [gift] bestows great merit and destroys the sins accumulated over a lifetime;
he who constantly gives a *prastha* of sesame seeds for the duration of a year [attains this]. (11)
One who performs the accumulation of fasts on that [lunar day] is considered equal to this;
on that day, the Lord of the World, Hari, the God and Sovereign of All, is pleased.
In that regard, the fruit is traditionally remembered as being as if it were directly perceived;
it was accomplished by Sagara, Kakutstha, and Nahuṣa. 13.
In that [city], Kṛṣṇa was propitiated by him and granted everything on earth,
specifically through speech, mind, and especially through bodily action.
One is liberated from the sins committed over seven lifetimes; there is no doubt about this.
Having fasted on that single day conjoined with an auspicious lunar mansion (puṇyanakṣatra), [one attains this result]. 15.
A human being obtains the fruit of ten thousand Ekādaśīs through bathing, giving gifts, recitation, burnt offerings, Vedic study, and the worship of deities. (16)
Whatever is performed for her is remembered as having inexhaustible fruit;
therefore, this [rite] should be performed with effort by those who desire its results. (17)
When Yudhiṣṭhira had bathed after the fifth horse-sacrifice,
that righteous soul questioned Kṛṣṇa, the upholder of the Yadu clan.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
O Lord Janārdana, tell me everything regarding fasting, eating only at night, and eating only once a day—what is their merit and what is their fruit? 19.
The Blessed Lord said:
O Pārtha, when the beautiful month of Mārgaśīrṣa has arrived,
one should fast on the twelfth day (dvādaśī) of its dark fortnight.
On the tenth day, eating only one meal, with a pure mind and firm vows. ||20||
Having thus understood that it is night, one should always remain self-restrained on the tenth day,
during the eighth division of the day when the sun has grown dim.
One should understand that *nakta* is not merely eating at night;
for a householder, *nakta* is prescribed as taking food until the appearance of the stars. (22)
In the eighth part of the day for an ascetic, there is a prohibition regarding that [time] at night;
thereafter, at the time of dawn, the observer of the vow should perform the ritual observance (niyama).
At midday, O Pārtha, one who is pure should likewise perform a bath;
bathing in a well is inferior, while bathing in a large oblong pond is middling. (24)
Bathing in a pond is excellent, and bathing in a river is superior to that; for the power of the water remains unimpaired when it stays within the midst of its waters. (25)
O Pārtha, when bathing is performed there, sin and merit become equal;
moreover, bathing at home is excellent, for it purifies the water itself.
Therefore, O best of the Pāṇḍavas, one should perform a ritual bath in the house;
[and likewise, O Earth,] when the earth has been traversed by horses and then traversed by Viṣṇu.
O Earth, take away this sin which has been accumulated by me in the past;
having utterly abandoned anger and greed, may I be firm in my vow with a single-minded heart. (28)
One should avoid those who do not speak [the truth], those who abandon [their duties], as well as heretics, those devoted to false speech, and those who revile Brahmins. (29)
And others who are of evil conduct, those devoted to approaching women who should not be approached, those who steal the property of others, and those who go to the wives of others. ||30||
Having worshipped Keśava, one should present an offering there;
with a mind full of devotion, one should offer a lamp in that house.
On that very day, O Pārtha, one should avoid sleep as well as sexual intercourse;
one should spend the entire day in the diversion of studying the Dharma-śāstras.
Having kept a vigil at night, O best of kings, one should, endowed with devotion,
give sacrificial fees to the Brahmins and, having prostrated, ask for their forgiveness.
Just as with the dark fortnight, so too with the bright fortnight; one should observe the Ekādaśī according to this very rule. O Pārtha, a twice-born man must never cause a division between them.
Listen now to the fruit that belongs to one who thus utters the *hi* sound:
having bathed at Śaṅkhoddhāra and beheld the Lord Gadādhara, a man [attains this result]. (35)
O best of kings, even one who bestows four hundred thousand *saṃvartas* does not merit a sixteenth part of the fast of Ekādaśī. (36)
The merit obtained at the sacred site of Prabhāsa during an eclipse of the moon or the sun does not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of fasting on the eleventh lunar day (Ekādaśī).
That fruit is surely produced for one who observes the fast on the eleventh day;
by drinking the water at Kedāra, rebirth no longer exists.
Thus, Ekādaśī destroys the dwelling in the womb of Pārtha;
it yields that fruit which one might obtain from the Aśvamedha sacrifice on earth. (39)
Therefore, the merit of one who fasts on the eleventh day is a hundred times greater than that of the best of the twice-born who eat at the house of an ascetic. (40)
That fruit is surely born for one who fasts on the Ekādaśī;
it is the same merit as that obtained by giving a thousand cows to one who has mastered the Vedānta.
Therefore, the merit of one who fasts on Ekādaśī is a hundredfold greater than that [of the former],
for in whose body reside the three gods— Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.
Those who fast on the eleventh day are equal to them;
those men of meritorious deeds are the devotees who worship Hari. (43)
Even the measure of the merit of the Ekādaśī vow is not known;
such shall be his merit as is difficult even for the gods to attain. 44.
Half the merit of this is obtained by eating only at night; for embodied beings, half the merit of eating at night is obtained by eating only once a day. (45)
All sacred fords, charities, and religious observances roar [with merit] only so long as one does not fast on the day dear to Viṣṇu. (46)
Therefore, O best of the Pāṇḍavas, observe this vow.
I do not know the measure of merit, O Pāṇḍava, regarding that which you ask.
O Pārtha, this supreme vow, which is equal to performing a thousand sacrifices, has been told to you; it is that which is most worthy of being kept secret. 48.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
How did this meritorious Ekādaśī lunar day originate, O Lord? How is it pure throughout this entire universe, and how is it dear to the gods? (49)
The Blessed Lord said: O Pārtha, in former times, during the Kṛta-yuga, there was a Dānava named Uraṇa,
who was most wonderful, exceedingly fierce, and a source of terror to all the gods.
O King, even Indra was conquered by that great asura, who was like Death itself and possessed of a wicked soul; likewise were all the gods defeated by him. (51)
Excluded from heaven by him, they wandered upon the surface of the earth;
all of them, terrified by the fear of Śaṅkara, went to Maheśvara.
Indra related everything in the presence of Īśvara as well:
"Having fallen from the heavenly world, they wander upon the surface of the earth. (53)
O Maheśvara, since the gods have taken their place among mortals, our splendor has faded; tell us, O God, what means there is, for what state do the immortals now go? (54)
Mahādeva said:
"O King of the Gods, O Best of Asuras, there stands the one whose banner is Garuḍa;
he is the refuge, the Lord of the World, the protector, and the ultimate resort. (55)
"O best of gods, go there; Soma will provide protection.
Having heard the words of Īśvara, the high-minded King of the Gods [departed]. (56)
O Yudhiṣṭhira, having gone there together with the thirty gods,
he saw that Lord Gadādhara sleeping in the midst of the water.
Having joined his palms in reverence, Indra uttered this hymn of praise.
Indra said:
Oṃ, salutations to the Lord of the gods of gods, who is worshipped by gods and dānavas;
O enemy of the Daityas, lotus-eyed one, slayer of the serpent, Madhusūdana! (59)
All the gods have come together, terrified by the Dānava;
O Lord of the World, you who are affectionate toward your devotees, take refuge in you and protect us! (60)
Save us, O God of gods! Save us, save us, O Janārdana!
Save us, O lotus-eyed one, O destroyer of the Dānavas! 61.
All have come into your presence; you alone are our refuge, O Lord!
O Lord, please grant assistance to these gods who have sought refuge. 62.
You are the Lord, you are the intellect, you are the deity, you are the agent, and you are the cause;
you are the mother of all worlds, and you alone are the father of the universe.
O Blessed One, Lord of Gods and Gods, you who are compassionate toward those who have come for refuge;
the deities, terrified and seeking safety, have come to you for refuge. 64.

"O Lord, all the deities have been defeated and cast down from heaven by that exceedingly fierce Daitya named Mura, who possesses great prowess. Having heard Indra's words, Viṣṇu spoke these words: 65. "All the deities have been conquered and deprived of heaven, O Lord, by that most terrible Daitya named Mura, who is possessed of great majesty. Having heard Indra's speech, Viṣṇu addressed him with these words.
The Blessed Lord said:
"O Śakra, what is the nature of that Dānava? What is his form and what is his strength?
Where is the abode of that wicked one? What is his prowess and what is his valor?"
O Mahāmati, tell me: what is better for that wicked one?
Indra said:
"Formerly, O Lord of Gods, there was a great Asura named Tālajaṅgha, who was born from the lineage of Brahmā and was exceedingly fierce. (67)
His son was the famous Dānava named Mura,
who was exceedingly fierce, possessed of great heroism, and a source of terror to the gods.
He truly resided in that place named Purīcandrāvatī;
by him all the gods were conquered and banished from heaven. (69)
Indra and Yama were made his two shoulders by him, as were Vāta and Hutāśana;
furthermore, he made Candra and Sūrya his two arms, as well as Vāyu and Varuṇa. (70)
"O Janārdana, everything was done by him; it is true, it is the truth!
By him, the world of the gods has been made devoid of all its stations. (71)
Having heard those words of his, Janārdana became enraged and said,
"I shall now slay the wicked Dānava who causes fear to the gods."
Accompanied by the thirty gods, the Lord went to the city of Candrāvatī;
there he saw the lord of the Daityas roaring again and again.
Then all those who had gone to the celestial realm, having conquered [the world], looked toward Hari and said to the Dānava, "Stay! Stay! (74).
The Blessed One spoke to him, his eyes bloodshot with anger.
The Blessed One said:
"O Dānava of wicked conduct, behold my arm! (75)
Then all those wicked dānavas, facing Viṣṇu,
were struck again by his divine arrows and became overwhelmed with fear.
O Pāṇḍava, that discus was released by Kṛṣṇa among the hosts of Daityas;
by it, many hundreds were cut down and met their death.
There, fighting again and again alone against the Danavas,
all the gods were destroyed by him, and even Madhusūdana was defeated.
A hand-to-hand combat ensued, which that Daitya had conquered;
he engaged in wrestling for a thousand divine years.
Viṣṇu fell into anxiety, and all the deities were cast down;
Viṣṇu, having been defeated by him, went to the Badarikāśrama.
O Pāṇḍava, Janārdana was sleeping there in a cave named Guhāsindhāvatī, which extended for twelve yojanas and had but a single entrance.
Having entered into her while she was fast asleep, I, a Dānava, was then prepared for a great battle; yet by means of his yogic power (yogamāyā), he became exhausted by that very conflict.
The Dānava, clinging to her back, then entered the cave;
seeing me there fast asleep, the Dānava was filled with joy.
Thinking that I have been thus defeated and that Hari has entered Śaṅkhahara, I shall undoubtedly slay him, who causes terror to the Dānavas. (84)
O Yudhiṣṭhira, from the body of Viṣṇu there emerged a maiden there,
beautiful and highly auspicious, equipped with divine weapons and armaments.
From a portion of his splendor was born a daughter of great strength and prowess, who was seen by the lord of the Dānavas named Mura;
O Dhanañjaya! [86]
A battle was joined by him, and it was indeed requested by the woman;
there, the maiden, who was skilled in all forms of combat, fought.
By the utterances of "huṃ," the great asura named Mura was reduced to ashes; when that Dānava had been slain, the god regained his consciousness there.
Seeing the Dānava fallen, he was then filled with wonder:
"By whom has this fierce and most terrible enemy of mine been slain? (89)
"A most terrible deed has been done; it was performed by me out of mercilessness.
The maiden said:
"Because of that, the gods, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Uragas, and Rākṣasas—" (90)
Indra and all the others were conquered and driven out from heaven; Hari was asleep and not seen by me when Mura arrived at his back. (91)
"When Jālandhara is asleep, he will withdraw the three worlds.
Having heard those words of hers, Viṣṇu spoke these words.
"If he has conquered me, how could he have been defeated by you?
Ekādaśī said: "O Lord, by your grace, that great Daitya was slain by me. (93)
The Blessed Lord said: "O auspicious one, tell me what is in your mind, which the sages and deities regard as the source of bliss throughout the three worlds."
I shall give it, of this there is no doubt—even that which is difficult for even the gods to obtain. ||94||
Ekādaśī said: "O Lord Janārdana, if you are pleased with me, what has been spoken is the truth; O Master of the Universe, I desire one boon from you in my heart. (95)
O Lord of Gods, O Master, I pray for that which is desired by me;
O Lord of the World, if my three words are true, grant them to me. (96)
The Blessed Lord said:
"It is true, it is true, O lady of excellent vows; what I have spoken to you must necessarily come to pass. Three words have been granted by me, and here there shall be no failure of my word. (97)
Ekādaśī said: "O Lord of gods, throughout the three worlds and across the four yugas, such as this has never been seen anywhere in the three realms; O Master, grant me such a boon."
"By your grace, O Goddess, may I become the foremost of all holy places, the destroyer of all obstacles, and the bestower of all accomplishments. (99)
O Janārdana, those people who shall fast for me with devotion and with devotion to you— O Lord, if you are pleased with them, may they attain all perfections.
O Mādhava, he who observes fasts, eats only at night, and takes but one meal a day—his wealth, his dharma, and his liberation, O Vaidehī, [are attained]. 101.
Viṣṇu said:
"O auspicious one, all that you say shall come to pass; O blessed lady, you shall obtain all your heart's desires, and it shall not be otherwise."
O Lord, those who are my devotees in the world, and those who are devoted during the month of Kārttika,
are indeed renowned throughout the four yugas and in the three worlds.
And I consider you to be Śakti; those who remain steadfast in the Ekādaśī vow will perform my worship and thereby attain liberation—of this there is no doubt. (104)
The third, the eighth, the ninth, the fourteenth, and especially the eleventh—these lunar days are dear to Hari.
The merit is superior to all sacred fords; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. (105)
Having granted her this boon, she uttered three words; there is no doubt that Ekādaśī, who possesses the great vow, became joyful and well-nourished. 106.
You slay the enemy and grant him the supreme goal;
you destroy all obstacles and bestow the boon of all accomplishments. 107.
O Pārtha, the Ekādaśī is equally auspicious for both fortnights;
one should not make any distinction between the bright and the dark. 108.
No distinction whatsoever should be made by those who observe all the vows, whether by day or by night, as they listen with devotion as their sole focus. (109)
The lunar day (tithi) may be the same for both fortnights;
indeed, the Ekādaśī may be very short at the end, and likewise the Trayodaśī.
But when the twelfth lunar day is full in the middle [of the three], that Trispṛśā is dear to Hari;
one should indeed fast on that single day, for it yields the fruit of eleven thousand Ekādaśīs.
