and who possesses knowledge, austerity, and renown— he is the one who partakes of the fruit of the sacred ford.

One who lacks faith, one who is evil-minded, an atheist, one whose mind is cut off [from the truth], and a proponent of mere logic—these five do not partake in the fruits of the sacred ford (tīrtha). ||26||
The Brahmin who, having risen early in the morning, always bathes at a sacred ford (tīrtha), being liberated from all sins, attains the Supreme Brahman. ||27||
O Six-faced One, those who know the rules of bathing have declared that there are four kinds of baths;
they are traditionally remembered as the Vāyavya, the Vāruṇa, the Divya, and the Brāhmya. (28)

The Vāyavya bath consists of dust from cows; the Vāruṇa bath takes place in oceans and similar bodies of water; the Brāhmya bath is that prescribed by Vedic mantras; and the Divya bath consists of rainwater and sunlight. (29)
Among all types of baths, the Vāruṇa bath is the most distinguished;
a Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, or a Vaiśya should perform the bath accompanied by mantras. (30)
O Six-faced One, for the Śūdra and likewise for women, silence alone [is prescribed];
this applies to the child, the young woman, and the old woman, as well as men, women, and eunuchs. (31)
People are liberated from all sins by bathing during the months of Kārttika and Māgha;
indeed, those who bathe in Kārttika obtain their desired fruit. (32)

Thus ends the one hundred and seventeenth chapter, titled "The Dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā" within the "Dialogue between Śrī Śiva and Ṣaḍānana," in the *Kārttika-māhātmya* of the *Uttara-khaṇḍa* of the glorious *Padma Mahāpurāṇa*, consisting of fifty-five thousand verses.
(118) The one hundred and eighteenth chapter.
Sūta said:
Again the Blessed One, the Great God whose banner is the bull, spoke, approaching the six-faced one who was filled with devotion and intent on listening. ||1||
Īśvara said:
Kārttika is indeed the month of Viṣṇu, the best among all months;
in this month, during the Kali age, the thirty-three gods are present.
In the month of Ūrja, O highly fortunate ones, one should provide meals to the twice-born, as well as sesame-cows, gold, silver, land, and garments. (3)
O observer of excellent vows, they shall give gifts of cows with their whole being;
yet among all gifts, the gift of a maiden is preeminent. (4)
Those men who here give a daughter to a Brāhmaṇa according to the prescribed rites shall dwell in Vaikuṇṭha for as long as fourteen Indras endure.
When the time for the appearance of body hair has arrived, Soma enjoys the maiden;
at the time of menstruation, the Gandharvas; and upon the appearance of breasts, Agni.
One should marry off a girl before she reaches puberty;
indeed, the marriage of an eight-year-old girl is commended by the wise. (7)
It should be given specifically to a Brahmin who is learned in the Vedas, an ascetic, one who has directly studied the Vedas, and a celibate student, according to the prescribed rule. ||8||
O son, this very same rule is prescribed for a maiden who has reached the age of marriage; indeed, it corresponds to the number of hairs upon the body of that maiden. 9.
For that many thousands of years he is honored in the world of Rudra;
indeed, [the merit of] a thousand cows is equal to a hundred oxen.
A vehicle is equal to ten oxen, and a horse is not equal to ten vehicles;
the gift of an elephant excels a thousand gifts of horses.
The gift of gold is equal to thousands of gifts of elephants;
and the gift of knowledge is equal to thousands of loads of gold. ||12||
The gift of land excels the gift of knowledge by ten millionfold;
the gift of cows excels a thousand gifts of land. ||13||
The gift of food is indeed superior to a thousand gifts of cows;
for this entire world, both stationary and moving, has food as its support. (14)
Therefore, O Peacock-Vehicle, one should give with effort during the month of Kārttika;
there are three gifts that are equal, and three fruits that are equal. (15)
Kārttikeya said:
O Mahādeva, you ought to tell me other duties as well,
by performing which one may wash away all sins and become a god.
Sūta said:
Thus questioned, Śambhu then proceeded to speak again:
"O you whose wealth is penance, listen to that which has been praised in so many ways; what is the use of further elaboration? (17)
Īśvara said:
He who avoids the food of others while observing the vow in the month of Kārttika shall obtain the fruit of the Cāndrāyaṇa penance simply by that avoidance of another's food. ||18||
Seeing that the month of Kārttika has arrived, the man who avoids food given by others obtains, day after day, the fruit of the kṛcchra penance. ||19||
In Kārttika one should avoid oil; in Kārttika one should avoid honey;
in Kārttika one should avoid bell-metal and, especially, food collected from many sources.
By eating meat even once, one enters the womb of a rākṣasa;
for sixty thousand years, one is tormented in excrement. (21)
Released from that, the sinner is born as a village pig that eats excrement, provided that a restriction regarding the foods normally consumed is observed during the month of Kārttika. ||22||
The state of being Viṣṇu himself is necessarily attained, which is the station that bestows liberation;
there is no month equal to Kārttika, and no deity higher than Keśava. (23)
There is no scripture equal to the Veda; no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā;
no conduct equal to truth; and no age equal to the Kṛta-yuga.
There is no satisfaction equal to that of the tongue; no happiness like that of giving;
no friend like Dharma; and no light equal to the eye. 25.
He who does not observe for a month that vow which is dear to Dāmodara should be known as fallen from his duty; he is born into low wombs. ||26||
The month of Kārttika is the most excellent, always dear to the Vaiṣṇavas;
it is a meritorious river flowing to the ocean, difficult to obtain for those who delight in ritual bathing.
A daughter of noble family and virtuous character is difficult for a man to find as a wife; likewise, a mother is rare in this world, and a father is even rarer still. (28)
The honor of the virtuous is difficult to obtain; a righteous son is difficult to find;
residence in Dvārakā is difficult to attain; and the sight of Kṛṣṇa is difficult to behold. ||29||
Rare is the bath in the Gomatī, and rare is the vow of Kārttika; yet these are attained by giving land to Brāhmaṇas during lunar or solar eclipses. (30)
O child, whatever fruit one obtains [by other means], that same fruit belongs to him who sleeps upon the ground;
he should honor the food given by the twice-born to his husband and wife with ointments.
Blankets, jewels, and various garments, as well as mattresses together with coverlets, should be given. (32)
O Pāvaka, give sandals and an umbrella in the month of Kārttika to that man who daily offers leaf-plates as food during Kārttika. ||33||
He does not fall into an evil rebirth for as long as fourteen Indras endure;
he obtains the fruit of all desires and the fruit of all sacred fords. //34//
Nor shall one see hell by eating from *brahma-plates*;
this *pālāśa* tree is remembered as Brahmā himself, the granter of all desires. (35)
O Śikhivāhana, one should avoid the middle leaf in the month of Kārttika;
for Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra—these three gods reside in the three leaves.
One should avoid a leaf belonging to Īśvara; Brahmā and Viṣṇu are unsurpassed.
By eating from all other leaves, one obtains every merit. (37)
O tiger among sages, by eating from a middle leaf-plate, or likewise from the milk of a Kapila cow, a man shall fall into hell. (38)
But he who, out of ignorance, drinks the milk of a Kapilā cow—whether he be a Śūdra or anyone else—becomes pure by giving a Kapilā cow to a Brāhmaṇa during the month of Kārttika. //39//
The gift of sesame seeds, bathing in a river, the constant sight of the virtuous, and eating from the leaves of the *brahma* tree—these grant liberation in the month of Kārttika. (40)
One who observes silence, eats from leaves, bathes in water, is always patient,
and sleeps on the ground during the month of Kārttika destroys the sins accumulated over many ages.
O General, he who performs a vigil at dawn in the month of Kārttika before Lord Dāmodara shall obtain the fruit of giving a thousand cows.
The merit that men obtain by giving food during the fortnight of the ancestors (Pitṛpakṣa) and by offering water in the months of Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha,
is attained in the month of Kārttika by lighting the lamps of others.
By lighting the lamps of others and by serving the Vaiṣṇavas during the month of Kārttika, one obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.
For one who does not perform a river bath, listen to the stories of Viṣṇu, or behold the Vaiṣṇavas during the month of Kārttika, ten years' worth of merit shall be taken away.
O tiger among sages, for that wise person who remembers Puṣkara by deed, mind, or speech during the month of Kārttika, the merit shall be a hundred thousand times ten millionfold.
Prayāga in the month of Māgha, Setubandha in Kārttika, and likewise Puṣkara in the month of Vaiśākha—these destroy the sins accumulated over an entire Yuga. 47.
Blessed are those men in the world, especially in this age of Kali, who constantly perform the service of Hari in every way, O Skanda. (48)
O Sage, what is the use of offering many funeral cakes through rites such as the *gayā-śrāddha*?
By that [act], the ancestors are undoubtedly delivered from hell. (49)
The bathing of Viṣṇu with milk and other substances is performed for the sake of the ancestors;
having attained heaven for ten million kalpas, they dwell there together with the gods. (50)
O best of Brahmins, for those by whom the lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa has not been worshipped in the month of Kārttika, Lakṣmī shall not dwell in their home for ten million lifetimes.
Those by whom Hari was not worshipped with devotion using black or white lotuses have been bitten, they have perished, and they have fallen into the jaws of the Kali age. (52)
Whoever worships the Lord of Gods, the husband of Kamalā, with a single lotus, effects the destruction of the sins of ten million years. ||53||
The Lord of Gods, when bowed to and worshipped with even a single lotus, may forgive thousands and seven hundred offenses.
O best of sages, he who worships Hari with a hundred thousand Tulasī leaves during the month of Kārttika obtains the fruit of a pearl for every single leaf.
O son, whatever is performed mixed with the fragrance of tulasī,
Keśava becomes pleased for thousands of millions of kalpas.
He who carries Tulasī, brought forth by Kṛṣṇa, upon his face, head, or body out of devotion to the Six-faced One (Kārttikeya), is not touched by the Kali age. (57)
O Six-faced One, by wiping the Yoga-amulet with the flower-offerings discarded after being worn by Kṛṣṇa,
one becomes liberated from all diseases as well as from sins.
O son, when one’s body is touched by the remains of Viṣṇu’s fire-offering, misfortunes perish and diseases go to their destruction. (59)
The water from the conch of Hari, devotion to Him, the remains of His garlands, the water from His feet,
sandalwood paste, and the residue of incense— these destroy even the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Thus, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa, in the *Kārttika-māhātmya*,
within the dialogue between Śrī Śiva and Kārttikeya, [this is] the chapter titled "The Question and Answer."
The one hundred and eighteenth chapter. ||118||
(119) The one hundred nineteenth chapter. Īśvara said:
O best of devotees, listen to the greatness of the Māgha bath;
O high-minded one, there is no devotee of Viṣṇu equal to you in this world.
Whatever fruit a mortal obtains by seeing Hari at Cakra-tīrtha and Keśava in Mathurā, that same fruit is obtained through the Māgha bath. ||2||
He who, with senses conquered and mind tranquil, endowed with virtuous conduct, performs his bath during the month of Māgha, shall not become a worldly being again. ||3||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
I shall describe the greatness of Śūkara before you;
by the mere knowledge of which, my presence is always [attained]. 4.
Sūta said:
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa sang many songs for Satyabhāmā.
I shall relate that to you; listen to it, O you whose wealth is austerity! (5)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: In the abode of Hari at Śūkara, which extends five yojanas,
even a living being who is a donkey becomes four-armed upon dwelling there.
The measurement of the boar is prescribed as three thousand cubits, three hundred cubits,
and three cubits.
O Goddess, he who performs austerities elsewhere for sixty thousand years obtains that fruit in Śūkara by even half a watch (of the day).
The fruit that is proclaimed for the gift of a Tulāpuruṣa at Sannihatī in Kurukṣetra when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu is [the same as] this. ||9||
It is said that [the merit] at Kāśī is tenfold, at the Veṇī it becomes a hundredfold,
and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean it is said to be a thousandfold.
And that very food should be understood as [equivalent to] a boar in the temple of Hari;
elsewhere, one gives a hundred thousand [times more] by means of the Kārttika rite.
By giving even a single [grain] right here, it becomes equal to this;
and likewise at Śūkara, at Veṇī, and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.

By bathing there even once, a person destroys the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa. O Six-faced One, in ancient times, Alarka obtained the earth with its seven continents simply by hearing the greatness of Śūkara-kṣetra.
"Go, my son, on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.
Kārttikeya said:
"O Blessed One, I wish to hear about the most excellent of all vows."
The procedure for the month-long fast and its appropriate fruit [have been explained]. (14)
Just as the practice of the vow should be performed by men according to the rules,
so too should it be commenced as before and likewise completed according to the prescribed ritual.
O Maheśvara, O sinless one, tell me in detail how many times this vow— which bestows happiness and prosperity— should be performed.
Śrī Rudra said:
O sinless one, O best among the intelligent, listen as I speak; by your devotion, I shall tell you everything that you have asked regarding Pāvaka. 17.
Just as Viṣṇu is among the gods, as the sun is among those that give heat, as Meru is among the peaks, and as Vainateya is among the birds; ||18||
Just as the Gaṅgā is among sacred fords, just as a merchant is among people, so too is the month-long fast the best among all vows. (19)
Whatever merit exists in all vows and indeed in all sacred fords, one who observes the month-long fast shall obtain that very merit, even more abundantly.
One does not obtain that merit through various sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma accompanied by abundant sacrificial fees, which one obtains from the observance of this month-long vow.

Therefore, the man who performs the month-long fast according to the prescribed rule has performed recitation, offered oblations, given gifts, practiced austerity, and offered ancestral libations. (22)
Having performed the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice and having worshipped Janārdana,
one should then undertake the month-long fast after obtaining the permission of the guru.
Having performed all the Vaiṣṇava vows as prescribed,
such as the auspicious Dvādaśī and others, he should then observe a fast for an entire month.
Having performed the Atikṛcchra and Pārāka penances, he should then perform the Cāndrāyaṇa;
thereafter, with the permission of his preceptor and the Brahmins, he should observe a month-long fast.
Having fasted on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina,
one should undertake this vow for thirty days.
The man who, having worshipped Vāsudeva, fasts throughout the entire month of Kārttika, shall become a partaker of the fruit of liberation.
With devotion, he worshipped Acyuta’s abode three times a day with auspicious white water-lilies,
jasmine, blue lotuses, *budhna* flowers, and fragrant lotuses.
Having anointed [the image] with flowers, uśīra, camphor, and excellent sandalwood paste,
one should worship Janārdana with food offerings, cakes, lamps, and other such items.
A man who possesses great devotion, has conquered his senses, and is a widower, should worship the one whose banner is Garuḍa through mind, action, and speech. (30)
One should engage in such discourse concerning the names of Viṣṇu day and night;
with devotion, one should utter the praise of Viṣṇu, avoiding all false speech. (31)
Endowed with compassion for all beings, peaceful in conduct, and non-violent, whether asleep or seated on an external seat, one should glorify Vāsudeva. (32)
One should avoid smelling the food, looking at it, tasting its fragrance, and praising it; one should also avoid dwelling upon it and the releasing of morsels. (33)
One observing a vow should avoid oil for the limbs, oil for the head, betel-leaf with ointment, and all other things that are prohibited. (34)
One established in the ninefold vow should not touch anyone engaged in improper acts, nor should one move such a person;
standing in a temple of the deity, even one who is not a householder may certainly perform [the vow].
Having observed a month-long fast according to the prescribed rule, a man, or a virtuous woman who is not widowed, should worship Vāsudeva. (36)
Having thus performed this vow for thirty days without deficiency or excess, one who is self-restrained and has conquered the senses should observe a month-long fast.
Then, on the twelfth lunar day, one should indeed worship the Meritorious One who has Garuda as his banner;
one should honor him with flower garlands, perfumes, incense, and ointments. ||38||
A person should satisfy Acyuta with garments, ornaments, musical instruments, and the like;
and with devotion, one should bathe Hari with water from sacred fords mixed with sandalwood paste.
Having anointed [the image] with sandalwood paste, adorned it with fragrant flowers,
and having fed the best of the twice-born with gifts of clothing and other offerings, ||40||
One should give them a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) and, having prostrated, ask for their forgiveness;
thus, having performed the month-long fast and having worshipped Janārdana.
Having fed the twice-born, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu;
thus, having performed the month-long fasts, [he feeds] thirteen Brahmins. (42)
Then, listen to the various methods by which one should cause them to attain liberation:
having fasted on the eleventh day (ekādaśī), one should perform a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice.
Having worshipped Hari, the Lord of Gods, with the permission of the preceptor, and having honored him according to one's ability, one should likewise salute the guru. ||44||
Then, preceded by a salutation, he should feed the Brahmins who are devoted to pure lineage and conduct and intent upon the worship of Viṣṇu. 45.
Having thus honored all of them and fed the thirteen, [one should give] betel, pairs of garments, food, and coverings. (46)
Indeed, one should give yoga-bands, threads, and sacred threads to the foremost of the twice-born, having honored them and bowed down. (47)
Then, according to one's capacity, one should worship the bed, which has been prepared with a coverlet, is auspicious and excellent, provided with a sheet and pillows, and is well-adorned. ||48||
Having had an image of himself made of gold according to his means,
he should place it upon that bed after honoring it with garlands and other offerings.
One should provide a seat, sandals, an umbrella, a pair of garments, shoes, purificatory materials, and flowers for the bed. (50)
Having thus resolved upon the bed and prostrated before those twice-born ones, he should request their approval, saying: "I am going to the world of Viṣṇu. (51)
Then that best of men should proceed to the nameless abode of Viṣṇu; meanwhile, he should repeatedly address the praised Brahmins stationed at the pavilion as follows: (52)

O best of the twice-born, that which was deficient in mantras, deficient in ritual action, or deficient in everything else—may all of it attain completeness through the grace of your words. Thus has the procedure for the month-long fast been fully proclaimed according to the rules. (53)

Thus ends the one hundred and nineteenth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Month-long Fasting," in the *Kārttika-māhātmya* of the *Uttara-khaṇḍa*, within the *Śrī-Padma Mahāpurāṇa*, a compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā. ||119||
(120) The one hundred and twentieth chapter.
Sūta said:
Having heard these words, the son of Agni asked again:
"O you whose wealth is penance, listen once more to [the account of] the worship of the Śālagrāma."
Kārttikeya said:
"O Blessed One, best among yogis, I have heard all the dharmas;
O Lord, tell me in detail about the worship of the Śālagrāma."
The Lord said:
"Excellent, excellent, O highly wise one, that you indeed question me!
I shall explain that to you; listen, my dear child. (3)
O noble-minded Mahāsena, the three worlds, including all things mobile and immobile, eternally abide united within the Śālagrāma stone. (4)
Whoever has seen, bowed to, bathed, or likewise worshipped [it], shall obtain merit ten million times that of a sacrifice and the fruit of giving ten million cows. ||5||
By that means, O child, the most dreadful dwelling in the womb has been severed for him by whom the water of the Śālagrāma stone was always drunk from Viṣṇu. (6)
O son, even one who is constantly attached to sensual desires, if he is devoid of the spirit of devotion yet worships the Śālagrāma stone, shall become Acyuta.
Having destroyed an image of Śālagrāma stone, the destruction of ten million [sins] is declared;
whether it is remembered, recited, meditated upon, worshipped, or saluted. ||8||
Upon seeing a Śālagrāma stone, numerous sins depart, just as herds of deer flee in fear upon seeing a lion in the forest. (9)
By performing a salutation during the worship of the Śālagrāma stone—whether with devotion or even without devotion—a person shall attain liberation. (10)
There is no fear of Vaivasvata (Yama), nor likewise of birth and death, for that man who constantly performs the worship of the Śālagrāma stone. (11)

The worship of the Śālagrāma stone is performed with perfumes, water for the feet, respectful offerings, food offerings, lamps, incense, ointments, songs, musical instruments, and likewise with hymns of praise. (12)
The man who, in the Kali age, is solely devoted to devotion,
rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu for thousands of millions of kalpas.
Even if performed with mere devotion, the salutation to the Śālagrāma made by men—who on this earth are my devotees—how could they ever again possess a human state? (14)
Those devotees of mine who are most sinful and do not bow down to my Lord—he, the slayer of me, goes indeed to the hell of Andhatāmisra. (16)
One should perform the touching of the *liṅga* made of clay; no other impurity is prescribed [for this].
Whatever lunar day is dear to Viṣṇu, that lunar day is beloved to me as well. (17)
That mortal who does not fast on that day is a sinner worse than a dog-cooker (outcaste).
O son, I always dwell upon the Śālagrāma stone. (18)
Out of devotion, the gratified Lord has granted me my own abode;
whatever fruit is obtained when I am worshipped with ten billion lotuses—[that has been granted]. (19)
The fruit of that [merit] is multiplied ten millionfold by the worship of the Śālagrāma stone.
I am not truly worshipped by those mortals, nor am I saluted by those men. (20)
Those who have not performed the worship of the Śālagrāma stone in the world of mortals—whoever performs my worship before the Śālagrāma stone [has truly worshipped me]. (21)
As the commander of armies, I was honored by him for twenty-one yugas.
What is the use of worshipping hundreds of lingas if they are devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu? (22)
O son, if the image of the Śālagrāma stone has not been worshipped, my food offering, leaves, flowers, fruits, and water are unworthy [of acceptance]. (23)
In the presence of a Śālagrāma stone, everything attains purity;
yet, having eaten the food offering (naivedya) intended for another deity, a twice-born man must perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance. (24)
By eating the food offered to Keśava, one obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices;
by the water from the Lord’s feet, those burdened by ten million killings [are purified]. ||25||
They are purified by water from a conch shell; of this there is no doubt.
For he who, having been a devotee of Maheśvara, does not worship Vaiṣṇava, [is likewise purified]. 26.
And the hater goes to hell for as long as fourteen Indras endure,
even if he who observes the highest stage of life should rest in that person's house for but a moment.
The father remains for eight great eons as one who partakes of the deathless;
yet the lowest of men sink into the wilderness of suffering within saṃsāra. (28)
For thousands of millions of years, those who have been devoid of the worship of Kṛṣṇa [are purified] by means of Liṅgas originating from Śālagrāma, which are worshipped with affection. (29)
Human beings attain liberation even when devoid of Yoga and Sāṅkhya, through the sight, worship, and praise of ten million of my liṅgas. ||30||
That [merit] which would accrue here from a single Śālagrāma stone is indeed attained by one who possesses twelve stones originating from Śālagrāma. (31)
Listen to me regarding the merit of that Vaiṣṇava who worships daily:
it is equal to that of thousands of millions of Liṅgas worshipped on the banks of the Gaṅgā.
Eight yugas of merit that are gained by residing in Kāśī are obtained in a single day [by one who worships there];
how much more so for a Vaiṣṇava man who indeed performs worship? (33)
I do not intend to enumerate the gods, beginning with Brahmā;
therefore, O my son, for the sake of my pleasure, [this is done] by my devotees through devotion. 34.
One must perform the worship of the Śālagrāma stone with devotion to Me;
for where the Śālagrāma stone resides, there Keśava dwells.
Therein reside the gods, the asuras, the yakṣas, and the fourteen worlds. (35–36)
One may obtain the fruit of all the millions of praises of the gods;
that same fruit of merit is obtained simply by praising Keśava in the Kali age.
If the ancestors are satisfied even once with a funeral cake (piṇḍa) at the edge of a Śālagrāma stone, they dwell [with him] forever; there is no counting that merit. (38)
For those men who drink the water from the Śālagrāma stone with devotion, what need is there for the consumption of thousands of *pañcagavya*? (39)
When an occasion for expiation has arisen, what is the use of gifts, what is the use of fasts, or of Cāndrāyaṇa penances well-performed, after one has drunk the water from the feet of Hari? 40.
Whoever constructs an image of the one who reclines upon the waters in a reservoir, what need is there for millions of other deities who have been worshipped? (41)
The gods, with Viṣṇu as their chief, indeed spoke together there:
"O son, there is indeed proof for every meritorious deed. (42)
There is no limit to the fruit obtained from the worship of a Śālagrāma stone;
he who gives a stone originating from Śālagrāma to Viṣṇu [attains immeasurable merit]. (43)
For a brahmin who is a devotee of Viṣṇu, even though he dwells at home, bathing in the Gaṅgā occurs day after day by virtue of his having performed hundreds of sacrifices. 44.
Having bathed in all sacred fords and being initiated into all sacrifices, one should perform the consecration with the waters from the Śālagrāma stone. 45.
O Guha, in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld, there are indeed stones;
yet there is no stone equal to the Śālagrāma stone—truly, there is none. (46)
In this world where human birth is difficult to attain, the life of one who daily gives a hundred *prasthas* of sesame with devotion is truly fruitful. (47)
One attains that fruit by worshipping the Śālagrāma stone;
likewise, [one attains it] by offering a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, a root, or a blade of dūrvā grass. (48)
Whatever [offering] is presented at Śālagrāma becomes equal to Meru, even if it is offered by someone who is devoid of ritual procedure and bereft of rites and mantras. (49)
One whose arms bear the marks of the wheel attains the fruit proclaimed by the Perfect Teacher;
indeed, that which was previously seen by me in Keśava as the destroyer of afflictions [is attained]. (50)
I shall tell you all of that out of affection for you, my son:
where do you dwell, O Viṣṇu, what is your support, and what is your refuge? (51)
"Or how else do you find delight, O Lord? Tell me all of that.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
"O Śambhu, I always dwell within the stone produced from Śālagrāma. (52)
In that very place, at the mark of the chariot wheel, hear my names:
if two wheels are seen at the doorway level with no gap between them, he should be known as Vāsudeva; he is white and exceedingly beautiful. (53)
Pradyumna has a face like the sun and likewise possesses a blue luster;
it is hollow, full of cavities, and long in shape. (54)
Aniruddha, however, is yellowish in hue, circular, and exceedingly beautiful;
it is marked with three lines at its opening and bears the sign of a lotus. (55)
The god Nārāyaṇa is dark-complexioned, possesses an elevated navel-wheel, is endowed with long lines, and has a cavity on the right side. (56)
One should know that the beautiful form of Hari with the face turned upwards grants desires, grants liberation, and especially grants wealth. ||57||
And Parameṣṭhin is white in luster, endowed with a lotus and a wheel;
likewise, his form is like a disc, and there is a very large cavity on his back. (58)
Viṣṇu is black in color; likewise, on the beautiful wheel at the base, a line is observed above the door from the middle region. (59)
Kapila, Narasiṃha, and Pṛthucakra are beautifully adorned;
he is to be worshipped through celibacy, otherwise he becomes a source of obstacles. 60.
The Vārāha [liṅga] has a Śakti-liṅga; it is remembered as having an uneven number of rings (cakras). Resembling a sapphire, it is thick and auspicious with three lines from the navel. ||61||
That stone which is long, golden-colored, and adorned with three dots should be known as "Matsyā"; it bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 62.
Likewise, the tortoise has a raised back, is circular, and is filled with wheels;
it possesses a green color and is marked by the Kaustubha gem.
Hayagrīva has the form of a horse, adorned with five lines, covered with many spots, and has a blue mark on his back. (64)
Vaikuṇṭha has undivided limbs, as does the single discus and the banner;
likewise, above the door, there is a very beautiful line in the shape of a bud.
Śrīdhara, likewise a deity, is marked with a forest garland;
he has the appearance of a kadamba flower and is adorned with five lines.
Round and very short, he is proclaimed as Vāmana;
he resembles the flower of the linseed plant and is adorned with a dot.
Then the god Sudarśana appeared, dark-complexioned and of great splendor;
on his left side were a mace and a discus, and a line indeed on his right.
Likewise, Dāmodara is thick with a discus established in the middle;
it has the luster of dūrvā grass, is crowded at the gateway, and likewise possesses yellow lines.
For he is of manifold colors and infinite, marked by various enjoyments;
appearing in many forms and diverse, he is the bestower of the fruits of all desires. ||70||
He whose face is seen above in all the intermediate and cardinal directions—he is to be known as Puruṣottama, the bestower of the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. ||71||
On the peak is seen a linga produced from a śālagrāma stone,
by which the Lord Yogeśvara removes even the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Padmanābha, however, is reddish-pink; he holds a lotus joined with a face.
By constant worship of him, even a poor man shall become a lord.
One should point out the network of rays as having wheels as its marks, golden in form, abounding in golden lines, and beautified by the luster of crystal. (74)
An excessively glossy [line] brings success and bestows fame;
a pale [line] burns away sins and grants the fruit of sons from one's father. (75)
A blue [line] bestows prosperity; a red one brings disease;
a rough one generates anxiety; and a curved one leads to poverty. (76)
One should know Sudarśana as the first, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa as the second;
one should know Acyuta as the third, and Janārdana as the fourth. (77)
The fifth is Vāsudeva, the sixth is Pradyumna, the seventh is Saṅkarṣaṇa, and the eighth is Puruṣottama. ||78||
The ninth is the Ninefold Array (navavyūha), while the tenth consists of that [same ninefold nature].
The eleventh is Aniruddha, and the twelfth consists of the twelvefold nature. ||79||
Beyond this point, however, marks of wheels are seen on those known as Ananta;
in the case of a Śālagrāma that is chipped, cracked, or broken, one incurs no fault.
Whichever form is desired by one, that one should worship with effort;
indeed, he who carries the Lord of Mountains upon his shoulder travels the path. (81)
The entire three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile, shall come under his control;
for wherever there is a Śālagrāma stone, there Hari is personally present. (82)
There, charity, recitation, and bathing are more than a hundred times superior [to those performed elsewhere] at Vārāṇasī, as well as at Kurukṣetra, Prayāga, Naimiṣa, and Puṣkara. (83)
In that regard, the merit at Vārāṇasī is ten millionfold and yields great fruit;
whatever sin a man commits, such as the killing of a Brahmin or other such acts, [is destroyed there]. (84)
The worship of the Śālagrāma stone quickly burns away all that;
for there the God born from the Śālagrāma and the one born at Dvārāvatī reside. (85)
Where there is a union of both, there is liberation; of this there is no doubt—whether by celibates, householders, forest-dwellers, or mendicants. ||86||
The food offered to Viṣṇu (naivedya) should be consumed; no deliberation is required in this matter.
By that very worship, there is neither the need for mantras, nor recitation (japa), nor meditative visualization (bhāvanā). ||87||
Neither praise nor ritual conduct is required for the worship of the Śālagrāma stone;
however, one should respectfully draw a svastika before the Śālagrāma stone. (88)
Especially in the month of Kārttika, he purifies his lineage up to the seventh generation;
even he who makes a mandala as small as an atom before Keśava [attains this]. (89)
One might dwell in heaven for ten million eons by making offerings of clay and products of the elements;
yet, he who attends to the *agni-hotra* sacrifice for a full year [attains a far greater merit]. (90)
By making a svastika in the month of Kārttika, this [result] is equal; of this there is no doubt.
This applies even to the case of approaching those who should not be approached and to the eating of what should not be eaten. ||91||
That sin goes to destruction by decorating the house of Hari.
That woman who daily draws a mandala before Keśava never encounters widowhood for seven births. (92)

Thus, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa, in the Glorification of the Month of Kārttika, within the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā,
[this is] the chapter titled "The Greatness of the Śāligrāma."
The one hundred and twentieth chapter. ||120||
(121) The One Hundred and Twenty-first Chapter. The Lord said:
O Guha, those who offer the funeral pinda while taking refuge in the shade of the Dhatri tree attain liberation through the grace of Madhava. ||1||

That man who places the dhātrī fruit upon his head, his hand, his face, and indeed upon his body, being thus adorned with the dhātrī fruits of the "nourisher" (vatsa-dhātrī), [attains prosperity]. ||2||
A man who makes his food of *dhātrī* fruits becomes Nārāyaṇa himself;
O Guha, whatever Vaiṣṇava in this world wears the *dhātrī* fruit [becomes one with me].
He becomes beloved of the gods; what need is there to mention humans?
One should not abandon a garland of tulasī, especially a garland of dhātrī. ||4||
As long as the necklace of the Dhātrī fruit remains upon a man's neck, for that long Keśava remains established within his body. (5)
The *dhātrī* fruit, *tulasī*, and earth from Dvārakā—his life is truly fruitful who possesses these three in his home. (6)
For as many days as a man wears a garland of *dhātrī* in the Kali age, for that many thousands of yugas shall his residence be in Vaikuṇṭha. (7)
He who wears a pair of garlands made from dhātrī and tulasī,
and carries them around his neck, shall dwell in heaven for ten million kalpas.
That man who, having fully restrained the collection of his senses, performs the worship of the Śālagrāma stone with devotion, gains for every single flower the merit born of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.
Just as Viṣṇu is among the gods, so is Tulasī among flowers;
he who daily worships the Lord whose banner is Garuḍa with Tulasī [attains the highest state]. (10)
He who has worshipped Viṣṇu with a garland of Tulasī in the month of Kārttika shall be liberated from the sufferings of birth, old age, and disease, and shall attain final liberation.
Śauri clearly wipes away the garland made of syllables, as well as the auspicious sandalwood with camphor, the aloe-wood, and the saffron. (12)
The offering of a *ketakī* lamp is always dear to Keśava;
by whomsoever the *ketakī* flower is offered in the month of Kārttika during the Kali age, [he attains the highest goal]. (13)
The gift of a lamp delivers a hundred generations of the Mahāsena family;
likewise, the offering of lotuses, tulasī, ketakī, and the flower of the sage (jāti). 14.

And during the month of Kārttika, the fifth [practice] is indeed the offering of lamps for those days; by whomsoever a flower-pavilion is made in Kārttika with a garland of ketaka flowers, [that merit is gained]. (15)
O child, this was done for Keśava, and his residence is in heaven;
the one whose banner is Garuḍa was worshipped with nothing but a ketaka flower. ||16||
Having worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa with flowers produced from the ketakī plant, Madhusūdana becomes well-pleased for a thousand years. (17)
O Guha, when the month of Madhumādhava has arrived, even by means of a *damanaka* flower, one goes to that auspicious and meritorious abode of Keśava, the Lord of Gods. (18)
O best of sages, by worshipping with *agasti* flowers, one obtains the fruit that comes from worshiping the god Janārdana. (19)
O Brahmin, by the sight of him, the fire of hell is extinguished; O brahmin-sage, Hari, being pleased by penance, does not do that which [is accomplished] by his sight alone.
O Mahāsena, whatever one performs while adorned with the flowers of the sages—having set aside all other flowers—one honors Keśava with the flower of the sages. 21.
He who worships with devotion in the month of Kārttika shall obtain the fruit of a horse-sacrifice;
so too he who offers a garland made of sage-flowers to Janārdana.
O Guha, even the Lord of the Gods, the best of sages, recounts the virtuous story of that person;
the fruit which is obtained by the gift of ten thousand cows, O Guha, [is attained by him]. (23)
By offering even a single *muni* flower in the month of Kārttika,
one obtains that fruit which [Viṣṇu] feels when pleased by the Kaustubha gem or by the forest garland.
And likewise, Hari is fully pleased by a Tulasī leaf during the month of Kārttika.
(Sūta said:
Seeing the prince bowed down with humility and solely devoted to devotion, [he spoke]. (25)
Again the Blessed One, Mahādeva, whose banner is the bull, spoke:
(Īśvara said:
"Listen, O you who have a peacock for a vehicle, to the majesty of the lamp during the month of Kārttika."
And the ancestors, always surrounded by their throngs of progenitors, desire:
"In our lineage there shall be a good son who is devoted to his father. (27)
He who pleases Keśava by offering lamps in the month of Kārttika—whether the lamp be fed with ghee or, again, with sesame oil—[attains great merit]. (28)
For whomsoever the commander-in-chief blazes with splendor, what need has he for the horse sacrifice?
By him all sacrifices have been performed, and the immersion in sacred fords has been accomplished. (29)
O son, he by whom the gift of a lamp was made before Keśava during the month of Kārttika—especially during the five days of the dark fortnight—[attains great merit]. (30)
He who offers lamps among them shall obtain inexhaustible merit;
a mouse, having lit a lamp offered by others on the eleventh day, [attained this].
Having attained a human birth which is difficult to obtain, she reached the supreme goal;
and the hunter also, having worshipped Maheśvara on the fourteenth day, [attained the same].
Having attained the supreme state, he became free from worldly consumption and went to the world of Viṣṇu;
for by taking refuge with the outcaste, the Vaiśya woman had used the lamp prepared by others to perform her rites. (33)
Having become pure Līlāvatī, she went to the imperishable heaven;
meanwhile, a certain cowherd, having seen the worship of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow on the new moon day, [attained the same]. ||34||
Having repeatedly exclaimed "Victory!", he became the Lord of the Kings of Kings;
therefore, lamps should be offered at night when the sun has set. (35)
In houses, in all cow-pens, and in all dwellings;
in temples of the gods, in cremation grounds, and by lakes. ||36||
For five days with ghee and other offerings for the sake of auspicious merit,
even those sinful ancestors whose rites of rice-balls and water-libations have been neglected attain supreme liberation through the merit of the gift of lamps. (37)
Thus, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa, in the *Kārttika-māhātmya*,
[this is] the chapter entitled "Description of the Greatness of Lamps, Fragrances, and Emblic Myrobalan."
The one hundred and twenty-first chapter. ||121||
(122) The one hundred and twenty-second chapter. Kārttikeya said:
O Lord, please tell me specifically the fruit of the Dīpāvalī festival;
for what purpose is it performed, and who is its presiding deity? (1)
Furthermore, O Lord, tell me what is to be given there and what is not to be given;
what is designated as "exultation" (praharṣa) here, and what is proclaimed as "playful action" (krīḍākātra)? [2]
Sūta said: O Brahmins, having heard these words of Skanda, the Blessed One, the witherer of Kāma,
spoke "Well said" to Kārttikeya and, smiling, addressed him as follows.
Śrī Śiva said:
On the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight of Kārttika, one should offer a lamp to Yama outside the fire-pit; thus, untimely death is destroyed.
"May the Son of the Sun (Yama) be pleased by this offering of a lamp on the thirteenth day, together with Time, who has Death as his wife and holds a noose in his hand. (5)
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, at the rising of the moon,
those who fear sin must certainly perform their ritual bath.
On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, which is not overlapped by the preceding [thirteenth] day,
one should perform a bath at the time of dawn with great devotion.
Lakṣmī resides in oil and Gaṅgā resides in water; he who performs his ritual bath on the fourteenth day of the Dīpāvalī festival indeed does not behold the realm of Yama.
Likewise, one should whirl Apāmārga, Tuṃbī, Prapunnāṭa,
and Vāhvala during the bath for the sake of the destruction of hell.
Accompanied by clods of earth from a furrow, along with thorns and leaves,
and while the apāmārga plant is being whirled around again and again, one should remove the sin of Hara.
One should wave apāmārga and prapunnāṭa over the head;
thereafter, the libation (tarpaṇa) should be performed with the names of Yamarāja.
To Yama, the King of Dharma, to Death, and to the Ender;
to Vaivasvata, to Time, and to the Destroyer of all beings. ||12||
Salutations indeed to Audumbara, Dadhna, Nīla, Parameṣṭhin, Vṛkodara, Citra, and Citragupta. ||13||
Having worshipped the deities, a lamp should be offered for the sake of [escaping] hell;
then, at the time of Pradoṣa, one should offer beautiful lamps. (14)
Especially in the abodes of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others,
as well as in gabled halls, shrines, assembly halls, and rivers.
Indeed, [he dwelt] within the walls, gardens, and ponds, in the main streets and pleasure groves,
and in the secluded elephant stables that were difficult to approach.
Thus, at the time of dawn on the new moon day, having bathed in the fire-purified water and having worshipped and bowed with devotion to the gods and the ancestors; ||17||
Having performed the *ābhyudayika* (ancestral) *śrāddha* with curd, milk, ghee, and so forth,
and having fed the Brahmins with various kinds of edible foods, he should ask for their forgiveness.
Then, O beloved, in the afternoon, the king should gratify the citizens;
having provided them with a social gathering, honor, and conversation, O King. (19)
O Guha, for as long as a year, delight arises among speakers;
before [Hara] is awakened, Lakṣmī awakens him through women.
If a man awakens Lakṣmī with a beautiful woman at the time of awakening,
Lakṣmī will not abandon him for an entire year.
Having granted fearlessness to the brahmins, the enemy of the asuras, who was afraid of Viṣṇu,
perceived that he was sleeping in the Ocean of Milk, as well as Lakṣmī resting upon a lotus.
You are the light, the glorious sun, the moon, the lightning, and the golden stars; you are the light of all lights, the light that abides within the lamp.

That misfortune which exists on the earth during auspicious days and during the festival of lamps (Dīpāvalī), or in the cow-pen on the full moon day of Kārttika—that misfortune, O Giver of Boons, may it depart from me. 24.
Śaṅkara and Bhavānī were engaged in a game of dice for sport;
Lakṣmī, having been worshipped by Bhavānī, stood there in the form of a cow. ||25||
In ancient times, having defeated Śambhu at dice, Gaurī sent him forth naked;
therefore this Śaṅkara is miserable, while Gaurī remains eternally established in happiness. (26)
First, for one who has victory, there is happiness for a year;
thus, when the night had passed and the people’s eyes were half-closed in sleep, [27]
Meanwhile, the city women, filled with joy, drive away Alakṣmī from the houses and the assembly by playing musical instruments and drums. (28)
If the moon has risen at dawn, it would be a contradiction to perform the worship of Govardhana in the morning; rather, one should carry out the gambling ritual at night. (29)
Likewise, these cows should be adorned, yet they must be spared from being made to carry loads or be milked;
O upholder of Govardhana, O protector of Gokula! (30)
O you who have been raised up by the arms of Viṣṇu, become the giver of ten million cows!
That Lakṣmī who resides among the world-protectors in the form of a cow—[may she be present here]. (31)
May the clarified butter, which carries the sacrifices, dispel my sin.
May cows be before me; may cows be behind me;
may cows be in my heart; I dwell in the midst of cows. (32)
Thus concludes the worship of Govardhana.
One should satisfy the gods and virtuous men with one's very being;
others with food and drink; and the learned with the gift of speech. (33)
With garments, betel leaves, lamps, flowers, camphor, saffron,
and various kinds of foods and delicacies, [he honored] the inhabitants of the inner apartments.
The king gratified them with gifts of village-bulls, with Sāman chants, with wealth,
with foot soldiers, and with auspicious neck-ornaments and bracelets.
The king should satisfy his ministers and kinsmen individually;
having satisfied them according to their merit, he should likewise satisfy the wrestlers and the actors. ||36||
He saw bulls and great oxen fighting with others,
as well as kings, warriors, and foot-soldiers adorned with ornaments.
Mounted upon me, he himself shall watch the actors, dancers, and bards;
he shall cause the warriors to fight, and likewise cause the cattle, buffaloes, and other livestock to be settled.
One should draw in the calves by means of the cows through the practice of dialogue and counter-dialogue;
thereafter, at the time of afternoon, [one should perform this] in the eastern direction, in the southeast.
O Guha, one should tie a divine path-fence made of *kuśa* and *kāśa* grass around that difficult-to-traverse tree with many creepers.
Having inspected the elephants and horses, he should lead them along the path;
likewise, the cattle, bulls, buffaloes, and female buffaloes adorned with loud-bellied ornaments. (41)

Having performed the fire-oblations, the best of the twice-born should tie the *mārgapālikā* [garland] with these; then, being firm in his vows, he should perform a prostration with this mantra: ||42||
Homage to you, the protector of the path, who bestows happiness upon the entire world;
on the surface of the path-protector’s ground, cows and great bulls offer their service. (43)
Kings, princes, and especially brahmins, by crossing over the Mārgapālī, shall be free from disease and attain happiness. 44.
Having performed all of this here during the day and night, one should then perform the worship of Bali, the lord of the Daityas, directly upon a mandala prepared on the ground.
One should draw Bali, the lord of the Daityas, with five-colored pigments, fully adorned with all ornaments and accompanied by Vindhyāvalī. 46.
Born from the *kūṣmāṇḍa* [seed], he was surrounded by the Dānavas Bhīru and Madhu;
he was fully formed, with a joyful countenance, a crown, and prominent earrings. 47.
Having had an image of the King of Daityas made with two arms, one should then worship it within one's own spacious hall in the middle of the house. 48.
Together with his mother, brothers, and kinsmen, he was content along with the gods,
amidst lotuses, water-lilies, flowers, white esculent lilies, and red lotuses.

With perfumes and flowers, with food offerings including milk, jaggery, and milk-rice (pāyasa), and with offerings of wine, meat, liquor, and various kinds of foods to be licked, sucked, and chewed; ||50||
O Indra among kings, whoever— whether a king, a minister, or a priest— performs worship with this mantra, he shall indeed possess happiness for a year.
O King Bali, salutations to you, O Lord, son of Virocana!
O future Indra, enemy of the gods, please accept this worship. (52)
Having thus performed the ritual of worship, one should then keep a vigil at night;
for a moment during the night, one should have actors, dancers, and singers perform.
And people, having established the King Bali within the interior of their homes with white rice, should worship him with fruits and flowers. (54)

In this regard, all that is to be performed in the fire for the sake of the *bali* offering—whatever those things may be that the seers who perceive reality declare to be inexhaustible—[should be done]. (55)
Whatever gift is given here, whether it be small or great, all of it becomes inexhaustible, auspicious, and pleasing to Viṣṇu. ||56||
"Whatever men shall perform your worship instead of that of Bali at night, may all their un-Vedic dharma accrue unto you. (57)
Furthermore, O child, Viṣṇu himself, being pleased, granted a boon that would bring benefit and serve as a great festival for the Asuras. (58)
O General, from that time onwards, the Kaumudī festival has been celebrated constantly;
it drives away all calamities and destroys all obstacles. (59)

Because she removes the sorrow of the world, bestows the wealth of irresistible power, and brings about prosperity and happiness, she should be known as "Ku" (Earth); therefore, he rejoiced at that non-duality. (60)
Because it leads to the realization of the elements (dhātu) through this very means, this is known as Kaumudī;
for it dispels the darkness of mutual diversity among various states of being.
Because they were joyful, satisfied, and attained happiness by it, this is remembered as Kaumudī;
O Ṣaṇmukha, because the kumuda flowers are offered to Bali on that day, it is so called.
For the sake of removing sin, this Kaumudī was ordained by kings;
thus, for one day and night every year in the month of Kārttika.
The earth became like a mirror for the king of the Dānavas;
for that king who acts thus in his realm, whence can there be fear of disease? (64)
There shall be abundance of food, security, and health; his prosperity shall be unsurpassed, and all people shall be free from disease and devoid of every calamity. (65)

Therefore, O Six-faced One, the Kaumudī festival is performed in order to manifest one's inner disposition upon the earth; for whatever state of being one maintains on this day, [that very disposition is manifested].
Indeed, through states such as joy and sorrow, his year passes away:
when he weeps, the year weeps; when he is glad, the year is gladdened.
If one has eaten [on the previous day], one will become an eater for the year; if one is healthy, one will remain healthy.
Therefore, the Kaumudī festival should be celebrated with great joy by auspicious men.
This lunar day in the month of Kārttika is declared to belong both to Viṣṇu and to the Dānavas.
Those who, out of virtue, perform the festival of lamps which inspires joy in all people, and the worship of King Bali with offerings,
belong to families characterized by generosity, enjoyment, happiness, and wisdom.
The entire year proceeds with joy and bestows prosperity. ||70||
These lunar days, beginning with the second, are indeed well-known as the *skanda-tithis*;
thereafter, during the four months of the rainy season, they bring auspiciousness.
The first occurs in the month of Āśvina, the next in Bhādrapada;
the third shall be in the month of Āśvina, and the fourth in Kārttika. (72)
In the month of Āśvina, there is the movement of the deceased;
in Kārttika, there is the desire for the realm of Yama. (73)
Guha said:
Why is she called "Full of Impurity," and why is she considered "Pure"?
Why does she move among the departed spirits, and why is she proclaimed as belonging to Yama?
Sūta said:
Having heard these words of Skanda, the Blessed Lord, the creator of all beings, whose banner bears the bull, spoke these gentle words while smiling. (75)
Maheśa said: Formerly, when the slaying of Vṛtra had occurred and Indra had obtained the sovereignty,
the horse sacrifice was undertaken for the purpose of removing the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Out of anger, Indra struck down the Brahman-slaughter with his thunderbolt;
it was cast into six forms upon the earth: into trees, water, and the ground.
In the case of a woman, [the penance] for killing an embryo and for arson is to be distributed respectively:
before hearing of that sin in the first case, and on the second day in the latter case.
A woman, a tree, a river, the earth, fire, and likewise a killer of an embryo—because these become defiled, they are therefore called "defiled" (kaluṣa). //79//
The earth was submerged in the blood of Madhu and Kaiṭabha;
it is purified by the eight fingers [of the priest] and is the dust from the feet of women. 80.
Rivers are defiled by the mud of the rainy season; fire is defiled by the soot rising upward;
trees are defiled by their exudations; and those who kill embryos are defiled by their association with the wicked.
Because one performs impure acts in this [world], it is therefore considered "impure" (akaluṣā).
Deceitful atheists who revile the duties toward the gods, sages, and ancestors [are reborn here]. (82)
Their second [tongue] is stainless, purified from even the slightest impurity;
they teach and recite the scriptures even on days when study is forbidden.

The followers of Sāṅkhya, the logicians, and those who follow the Vedas—due to the impurity arising from their use of correct and incorrect words, she [the Goddess] became purified; then, on the second day, she was stainless through her meaning.
By the birth of Kṛṣṇa, the three worlds become purified; this very day in the month of Nabhas is designated as the stainless lunar day by the wise. (85)
The Agniṣvātta, Barhiṣad, Ājyapa, and Somapa Pitṛs, as well as the Pitāmahas and the Pretasaṃcaras. (86)
The ancestors are said to be *pretas* and *tusitas*; their movement occurs within that [realm].
When honored with the *svadhā* mantras by sons, grandsons, and daughters' sons, they are satisfied. (87)
Satiated by ancestral offerings (śrāddha) and sacrifices, the departed spirits (preta) proceed from here;
however, during the Mahālaya festival, the wandering of the pretas is seen upon the earth. 88.
Therefore, O Śikhivāhana, this is proclaimed as the procession of the pretas,
because on this day worship is performed by men to Yama in the fire.
Therefore, this has been declared by me as pertaining to Yama; truly, truly have I spoken this.
Those best of men who hear this greatness of the month of Kārttika [attain the highest state]. (90)
The merit arising from the Kārttika bath shall certainly belong to them. ||91||
On the second day of the month of Kārttika, in the forenoon, one should worship Yama;
having bathed on that daughter of the Sun, a man does not behold the world of Yama. (92)
O Śaunaka, on the second day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika,
Yama was formerly fed and honored in his own home by Yamunā.
On the second day, there was a great release, and those in the hells were satiated;
freed from their sins, they were liberated from all bonds. (94)
Having their hopes fulfilled and being contented, they all remained as they pleased;
for them there occurred a great festival that brought happiness to the realm of Yama. (95)
Therefore, this [practice] is renowned as peerless throughout the three worlds;
for that reason, O Brahmin, wise men should not eat in their own homes. 96.
Out of affection, one should eat nourishing food from the hand of one's sister;
likewise, gifts should be bestowed upon sisters according to the prescribed rules.
Adorned with golden ornaments, fine garments, and accompanied by offerings and hospitality, one should eat from the hand of one's co-born sister thereafter. 98.
One should eat strength-increasing food from the hand of every unfortunate woman.
On the second day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika, Yama has been worshipped and satiated.
Salutation to that Lord of the southern quarter, who is mounted upon a buffalo-throne, who wields a staff and a mallet, and who is surrounded by joyful servants. 100.
O sisters, for those by whom well-dressed women have been gratified with gifts of clothing and the like, there shall be neither quarrel nor fear of enemies for as long as a year. 101.

O sinless one, I have fully explained this entire [treatise], which brings merit, fame, and long life, which accomplishes dharma, pleasure, and wealth, and which contains the secrets regarding sons. 102.
On whichever lunar day King Yama was fed by Yamunā out of sisterly affection, on that very same day,
whoever here eats from the palm of his sister’s hand [attains the fruit].
He attains the highest excellence of wealth and auspiciousness. ||103||
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-second chapter, titled "The Greatness of Kārttika," in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses.
(123) Chapter One Hundred and Twenty-Three. Kārttikeya said:
O Blessed One, I wish to hear about the supreme vow among all vows, and the fruit of fasting for a month as it has been declared. (1)
Just as the practice of the vow should be performed by men according to the rules,
so too should it be commenced as before and completed in accordance with the prescribed ritual.
O Maheśvara, O sinless one, O best of gods, please explain to me in detail how many times this vow is to be performed.
The illustrious Rudra said:
"O sinless one, O best among the intelligent, I shall tell you everything that you have asked;
listen with devotion as I speak. (4)
Just as Viṣṇu is among the gods, as the sun is among those that give heat, as Meru is among the peaks, and as Vainateya is among the birds; ||5||
Just as the Gaṅgā is among sacred fords, and just as the merchant is among subjects,
so too is the month-long fast the best among all vows.
Whatever merit exists in all vows and indeed in all sacred fords,
one who observes the month-long fast shall obtain even more than that.
One does not attain through various sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma, accompanied by abundant sacrificial fees,
that merit which is obtained from the observance of this month-long vow.

Therefore, that man who performs the month-long fast according to the prescribed rule has effectively performed recitation, offered oblations, given gifts, practiced austerity, and offered the ancestral libation (svadhā).
Having performed a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice and having worshipped Janārdana,
one should then undertake the month-long fast after obtaining the permission of the guru.
Having performed all the Vaiṣṇava vows as prescribed,
such as those beginning with the twelfth day (dvādaśī), which are meritorious, he should then observe a month-long fast.
Having performed the *atikṛcchra* and the *pārāka*,
he should then perform the *cāndrāyaṇa* and the month-long fast (*māsopavāsa*), after having ascertained the strength and weakness of his body.
O Sage, whether he be a forest-dweller or an ascetic, or even a woman whose husband is living or one who is widowed,
he or she may observe the month-long fast after obtaining the permission of his preceptor or a Brahmin.
Having fasted on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina,
one should undertake this vow for a period of thirty days.
The man who, having worshipped Vāsudeva, fasts throughout the entire month of Kārttika, shall become a partaker of the fruit of liberation. (15)
With devotion, one should worship Acyuta’s abode three times a day with auspicious white water-lilies,
jasmine, blue lotuses, and fragrant red lotuses.
Having anointed [the image] with kuṅkuma, uśīra, camphor, and excellent sandalwood,
one should worship Janārdana with offerings of food, incense, lamps, and so forth.
A man who has conquered his senses and possesses great devotion should worship the one whose banner is Garuḍa through mind, action, and speech—even if he is a woman or a widow. (18)
One should engage in such discourse concerning the names of Viṣṇu day and night;
with devotion toward Viṣṇu, one's speech should be truthful and free from idle chatter. (19)
Endowed with compassion for all beings, peaceful in conduct, and non-violent, whether sleeping or seated on an outer seat, one should glorify Vāsudeva.
Having recollected the sight, scent, and so forth, and having tasted [the food], it is proclaimed that one should avoid taking a mouthful of food and the releasing of morsels. 21.
One observing a vow should avoid body oil, head oil, betel leaf with ointment, and all other things that have been rejected. 22.
One established in the ninefold vow should not touch anyone engaged in improper acts, nor should he move such a person;
remaining in a temple of the deity, the householder should practice the ninefold vow.
Having observed a month-long fast according to the prescribed rule, a man, or a virtuous woman who is not widowed, should worship Vāsudeva. (24)
Having thus observed this vow for thirty days, neither deficient nor excessive, one who is self-restrained and has conquered the senses should perform a month-long fast.
Then, on the twelfth day, one should indeed worship the Meritorious One who has Garuḍa as his banner;
one should honor him with flower garlands, perfumes, incense, and ointments. ||26||
A person should satisfy Acyuta with garments, ornaments, musical instruments, and the like;
and with devotion, one should bathe Hari with water from sacred fords mixed with sandalwood paste.
Having anointed [the image] with sandalwood paste, adorned it with fragrant flowers, and having fed the best of the twice-born with gifts of clothing and other offerings, [he should proceed]. (28)

One should give them a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), prostrate before them, and ask for their forgiveness; having asked the Brahmins for forgiveness, one should dismiss them after honoring and worshipping them.
Thus, according to one's wealth and with devotion, as far as one is able,
having performed the month-long fasts in this manner and having worshipped Janārdana, ||30||
Having fed the twice-born, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu;
likewise, having performed month-long fasts, he should feed thirteen Brahmins. (31)
Then, listen to the method by which one should cause them to attain liberation:
having fasted on the eleventh day (ekādaśī), one should perform a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice.
Having worshipped Hari, the Lord of Gods, with the permission of the preceptor, and having honored him according to one's ability, one should likewise salute the guru. ||33||
Thereafter, one should feed the Brahmins, preceded by a salutation, who are of pure lineage and conduct and are devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu. (34)
Having thus worshipped all of them and fed thirteen people,
one should offer betel, pairs of garments, food, and coverings.
Having indeed given yoga-bands, threads, and sacred threads to the foremost of the twice-born, and having honored and prostrated before them, [one attains the fruit]. (36)
Then, with devotion, one should honor [the deity] with an excellent, beautiful bed, well-prepared with coverings, provided with pillows, and adorned. (37)
Having had a golden image of oneself made according to one's means,
one should place it upon that bed after honoring it with garlands and other offerings.
One should provide a seat, sandals, an umbrella, a pair of garments, shoes, sacred purifiers, and flowers for the bed. (39)
Having thus prepared the bed and prostrated before those twice-born ones, he should request their approval, saying: "I am going to the world of Viṣṇu. (40)
Then a man should go to that most beloved, nameless abode of Viṣṇu;
he should repeatedly say this to the brahmins standing in the pavilion: [41]

O best of the twice-born, may everything that is deficient in mantra, deficient in devotion, and deficient in ritual action reach completion through the grace of your words. Thus has the procedure for the month-long fast been duly proclaimed. (42)
Thus, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses,
in the Uttara-khaṇḍa, in the *Kārttika-māhātmya*, within the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, [this is] the section titled "The Narration of the Month-long Fast."
The one hundred and twenty-third chapter.
(124) The one hundred and twenty-fourth chapter.
Īśvara said:
O best of gods, listen to the majesty of Prabodhinī, which destroys sins, increases merit, and grants liberation to those whose intellects are fixed on reality. 1.
The army roars on the banks of the Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī only so long as the sin-destroying Haribodhinī of the month of Kārttika has not yet arrived.
They visit sacred fords and lakes as far as the ocean,
until the lunar day of Viṣṇu’s awakening arrives in the month of Kārttika.
The merit of thousands of horse-sacrifices and hundreds of royal consecrations is attained by a single fast on Prabodhinī.
That which is difficult to find and hard to attain in the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile—even that, when prayed for, the Pratibodhinī bestows upon the Brahmin. (5)
The Haribodhinī [Ekādaśī], when fasted upon, effortlessly bestows sovereignty, worldly existence, knowledge, kingship, and the abundance of happiness.
The Hari-bodhinī [Ekādaśī] burns away, with a single fast alone, sins as vast as Mount Meru and as heavy as lead.
O tiger among men, he who naturally observes the vow of fasting on the Prabodhinī day according to the prescribed rite obtains the fruit as described.
Whatever sin has been accumulated over thousands of previous births is burned away by staying awake during the Prabodhinī vigil, like a heap of cotton.
Listen, O Six-faced One, I shall describe the characteristics of the vigil (jāgara), by the mere knowledge of which Janārdana is not difficult to attain. (10)
Song, instrumental music, dance, as well as the recitation of the Purāṇas;
incense, lamps, food offerings, flowers, perfumes, and unguents. ||11||

It consists of the fruit, the guest-offering, faith, giving, restraint of the senses, being endowed with truth, freedom from sleepiness, being filled with joy, and being accompanied by ritual action. ||12||
It should be performed with reverence and enthusiasm, free from laziness and other such faults, accompanied by circumambulations and the like, and preceded by prostrations. ||13||
O noble one, with an undaunted mind, performing the lustration ceremony for Hari at every watch of the night, [you shall attain success]. (14)
He who, with a one-pointed mind, performs the vigil for the Lord endowed with these qualities, is not born again on this earth. (15)
Whoever performs the vigil on the day of Viṣṇu in this manner, with devotion and free from stinginess regarding wealth, is led to the supreme goal.
Whoever constantly worships Hari with the Puruṣasūkta during the month of Kārttika has,
by that act, worshipped Keśava for thousands of millions of years.
By worshipping regularly during the month of Kārttika according to the procedure declared in the Pañcarātra, a person shall indeed become a partaker of liberation. (18)
He who worships Hari in the month of Kārttika with the mantra "Namo Nārāyaṇāya" is liberated from the sufferings of hell and attains the state free from ailment.
Whoever recites the Thousand Names of Hari and the story of the liberation of the king of elephants during the month of Kārttika does not undergo rebirth again.
For thousands of crores of yugas and hundreds of manvantaras,
one who keeps a vigil on the twelfth day of the month of Kārttika dwells in heaven.
And those born in his family, by the hundreds and thousands, attain the station of Viṣṇu; therefore, one should perform the vigil (jāgara).
O beautiful lady, he who performs praise and song during the final watch of the month of Kārttika dwells in Śvetadvīpa together with his ancestors.
O best of sages, by offering food to Hari at the end of the day in the month of Kārttika, one dwells in heaven for as many yugas as there are grains of rice in that offering.
O tiger among sages, the worship of Mālatī and Kamalā is inexhaustible;
he who worships the Lord of the gods of gods goes to the supreme state. ||25||
Having observed the Ekādaśī in the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika, a man who offers auspicious water-pots in the morning goes to my abode. (26)
Kārttikeya said:
"O Blessed One, let that meritorious vow which is the supreme among vows—the Bhīṣmapañcaka—be described by you as that which should be performed in the month of Kārttika. (27)
O Grandfather, O best of gods, please tell me, through your grace, the procedure for that [rite] and its fruit, as well as that of the sages. (28)
Īśvara said:
O best among those who know the ordinances, I shall proclaim this most meritorious vow,
since Bhīṣma obtained this five-day rite.
From the presence of Vāsudeva, this Bhīṣma-pañcaka was told by him;
who, other than Keśava, is capable of describing the virtues of this vow?

Now listen to this ancient dharma [to be observed] during the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika, which was practiced by Vasiṣṭha, Bhṛgu, Garga, and others in the Kṛta Yuga and other ages. (31)
In the Tretā Yuga and other ages, Ambarīṣa and others practiced it through enjoyments and such,
while Brāhmaṇas practiced it through celibacy, recitation, fire-offerings, and ritual acts.
It is likewise difficult for Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas who are devoted to truth and purity; it is impossible for those devoid of truth whose minds are like children. (33)
"It is difficult; they call it Bhīṣma; it cannot be accomplished by ordinary men.
O best of Brahmins, he who performs that [rite] has everything performed by means of the Tena-sarva. (34)
This vow is of great merit and the destroyer of great sins;
therefore, the Bhīṣmapañcaka should be performed by men with diligent effort. (35)
Having bathed according to the proper ritual procedure during the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika,
one should undertake the five-day vow on the eleventh day (ekādaśī).
Having bathed especially in the morning and likewise at midday,
the observer of the vow should apply cow dung at a river, a mountain stream, or a pool.
Having bathed, observed silence, and put on clean garments, a man of firm vows should properly satisfy the ancestors in due order with barley, rice, and sesame seeds. (38)
One should diligently offer water libations and the *arghya* offering to Bhīṣma;
worship of Bhīṣma must be performed, and one should zealously bestow gifts. (39)
Having diligently offered the five jewels specifically to the brāhmaṇa, the Lord Vāsudeva, ever accompanied by Lakṣmī, was also worshipped. ||40||
Having worshipped the five [elements], one remains satisfied for ten million eons;
whatever is performed, one should conceive it all as the five elements. ||41||
He obtains the complete fruit of the vows undertaken throughout the year,
having performed the offering of water and likewise the presentation of the *arghya* oblation.
The person who performs [this] with this mantra shall become a partaker of liberation. ||43||
For him of the Vaiyāghrapāda lineage, for the sake of his ancestral seers,
and for this sonless Bhīṣmavarman, I offer this water.
For the attainment of the Vasus, for the welfare of my body and my son, I offer this respectful oblation (arghya) to Bhīṣma, who has been a celibate student since birth. ||45||
Thus ends the mantra for the arghya offering.
By this procedure, one should complete the five [days];
one obtains merit equal to that of a horse sacrifice (aśvamedha), of this there is no doubt. ||46||
O son, I too must diligently perform the prescribed observances; for without such discipline, the ritual of a vow cannot bear fruit.
Hari granted [the boon] to Bhīṣma, who was deprived of the northern solstice;
even though he was deprived of the northern solstice, he attained purification despite the absence of an auspicious conjunction (*lagna*).
Then one should worship Lord Hari, the remover of all sins;
immediately thereafter, the Bhīṣmapañcaka vow should be performed with diligence. (49)
One should bathe [the deity] with devotion using water, honey, milk, and ghee,
as well as with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) and water scented with sandalwood.
One should smear Keśava, whose banner is Garuḍa, with fragrant sandalwood, kuṅkuma, and camphor mixed with uśīra.
One should worship with beautiful flowers accompanied by perfumes and incense;
the devotee should burn guggulu resin mixed with clarified butter for Kṛṣṇa.
One should offer a lamp day and night for five days and so forth; one should present the divine food of the God of gods as an offering of supreme rice-pudding (paramānna).
Having thus worshipped the God, and having recollected and prostrated before Him,
one should mutter the mantra "Oṃ namo vāsudevāya" one hundred and eight times.
One should perform the oblation with sesame, rice, barley, and so forth, smeared with clarified butter, using the six-syllable mantra accompanied by the utterance of "svāhā. ||55||
Having performed the evening twilight devotion, having bowed to the one whose banner is Garuḍa,
and having recited the mantra as before, the observer of the vow should lie upon the ground.
All this ritual procedure should be performed for five days;
however, there is a specific distinction in this vow—listen now to that which is not otherwise deficient. (57)
On the first day, the observer of the vow should worship the feet of Hari with lotuses;
on the second day, he should worship the region of the knees with bilva leaves.
Then, on the full moon day of Kārttika, with his mind fixed upon Him, he should devoutly worship the head of the Discus-bearer, the God of gods, with jasmine flowers. (59)
Having briefly worshipped that Hṛṣīkeśa on the eleventh day,
and having properly consumed cow dung, one should observe the fast on the eleventh day.
On the twelfth day, the observer of the vow should consume cow urine with the recitation of mantras;
on the thirteenth day, milk; and likewise, curd on the fourteenth day.
Having consumed [the fast-food] for the sake of bodily purification and having observed the fast for four days,
on the fifth day he should bathe and worship Keśava according to the prescribed rite.
One should feed the Brahmins with devotion and give them a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), having abandoned sinful thoughts and remaining wise through celibacy (brahmacarya). ||63||
Having abandoned liquor, meat, and sexual intercourse which causes sin, a man devoted to the worship of Kṛṣṇa subsists on vegetables and the food of sages. ||64||
Then, one should consume [the meal] at night, preceded by the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
In this way, for one who has properly completed [the rite], the fruit as described shall be attained. ||65||
If a drinker of liquor should drink liquor from birth until the end of life, by performing this Bhīṣma-vow, he attains the supreme state. ||66||
Women should perform the increase of Dharma according to the words of the Brāhmaṇas;
widows, moreover, should perform it for the sake of increasing the bliss of liberation. (67)
For the sake of fulfilling all desires, for the sake of merit, and likewise for the sake of constant bathing and giving, people observe the month of Kārttika in the sacred fire.
The Vaiśvadeva sacrifice should be performed by those devoted to the meditation on Viṣṇu;
it bestows health and sons, and destroys great sins. (69)
O Six-faced One, one should observe the Kārttika vow at sacred fords with every effort;
indeed, the completion of all year-long vows is considered to take place in the month of Kārttika.
A terrifying image of Evil was produced, wearing fierce garments and appearing most fearsome;
she emerged with a sword in hand, possessing formidable iron fangs.
Placed upon a measure of sesame seeds, she is draped in black garments,
adorned with a wreath of red flowers, and her golden earrings are blazing.
Having worshipped with supreme devotion by means of the names of Dharmarāja,
one should recite this mantra while holding a handful of flowers in the joined palms.
Whatever evil was committed in other births or again in this birth, may it come to pacification through the grace of your feet. (74)
Having thus worshipped that golden image according to the prescribed rules,
he should perform worship, to the best of his ability, for the Brahmins who are exponents of the Vedas.
For the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa, the God of gods, whose deeds are effortless, it should be given to a Brāhmaṇa with the thought: "May Dharma be pleased with me. (76)
A sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should be given according to one's ability to the reciter and the donor;
one should give gold and cows, saying, "May Kṛṣṇa be pleased. ||77||
Having become one who has accomplished what was to be done and remaining established therein, he should be dispassionate and self-restrained;
furthermore, he should give to others according to his own capacity, for giving is supreme.
With a tranquil mind and free from offense, one shall attain the supreme state.
