One should perform [the worship] with the two mantras and the sixteen services;
then, during each subsequent service, one should offer a handful of flowers.
The Vaiṣṇava should invoke the Lord of the World with the [appropriate] mudrā,
and he should offer the seat with the Puṣpaka mudrā.

The offering of a lamp, the respectful water-offering (arghya), the sipping of water (ācamana), and the bath with pure waters contained in vessels, combined with auspicious substances and mixed with tulasī leaves. ||61||
One should offer a reciprocal service with the two root mantras;
thereafter, one should perform an anointing with well-perfumed oil.
One should perform the ritual rubbing with musk and sandalwood, and bathe [the deity] with auspicious waters scented with fragrances and accompanied by mantras. (63)
Having adorned [the image] according to the prescribed rite with divine garments and ornaments,
one should then offer the honey-mixture (madhuparka) and present highly fragrant perfume.
One should devoutly and properly offer fragrant and beautiful flowers,
as well as incense, a ten-wicked lamp, and a most charming light.
One should offer various kinds of food offerings mixed with milk-rice (pāyasa) and cakes;
furthermore, one should devotedly present camphor along with betel leaf.
Having performed the lustration ceremony with lamps, one should worship with a garland of flowers;
then, having circumambulated and prostrated, one should praise [the deity] with unsurpassed hymns of praise.
Having caused the Lord to be seated upon the lap of Garuḍa, one should present the auspicious *arghya* offering;
then, after reciting His meritorious names, one should perform the fire sacrifice (*homa*).
With the remnants of the oblation, he should offer into the circle of fire the Puruṣasūkta,
the Śrīsūkta, and the hymn called Maṅgala, verse by verse.
One should offer into the Vedic fire an oblation mixed with clarified butter, using the proclaimed jewel of a mantra, while endowed with devotion. (70)
Meditating upon Mahāviṣṇu, who is the very form of sacrifice, one should indeed offer the oblation either one hundred and eight times or twenty-eight times.
Resembling a pure jasmine flower, bearing the conch, discus, and mace,
the Lord is endowed with all the Vedas and Vedāntas along with their limbs and subordinate parts.
Having meditated upon [the deity] seated with the Goddess Śrī, one should perform the fire-oblation (homa);
thereafter, one should offer oblations of sacrificial material, one by one, while reciting the names.
With reference to his eternal devotees, the supreme and greatest of great devotees [first manifests] the powers such as Bhū, Līlā, Vimalā, and the others, in their proper sequence.
Immediately following that are the deities beginning with Ananta and Vihageśvara;
thereafter come Vāsudeva and the others, as well as the deities beginning with Śakti. ||75||
The forms beginning with Keśava, as well as those beginning with Saṅkarṣaṇa; likewise the Fish, Tortoise, and others, and the weapons such as the Discus and so forth. ||76||

The Kumudas and other [classes of gods], as well as the thirty-three [gods], likewise the deities beginning with Candra, the world-protectors beginning with Indra, and the deities beginning with Dharma; ||77||
In that [fire], offerings should be made in sequence and especially worshipped;
this is indeed the Vaikuṇṭha-homa performed by the most excellent of great devotees.
In the rite of daily worship, one should always perform it with a well-concentrated mind;
for domestic worship, according to the procedure of the five sacrifices at the threshold of the house. (79)
Having offered the bali-oblation according to the prescribed rite, one should afterwards perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana).
Then, sitting upon an auspicious seat covered with a black antelope skin and kuśa grass, [one should proceed].
For the sake of one's own happiness and for the purpose of enjoyment, one should practice the yoga of mantra;
seated properly in the lotus posture (padmāsana), one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Having conquered the senses, one should perform three breath-control exercises (prāṇāyāma) with the mantra;
then, having turned the face toward the north, one should visualize the unsurpassed heart-lotus.
One should cause its expansion within the heart by means of the sun of consciousness;
within its pericarp, one should contemplate the orbs of fire, sun, and moon in their proper sequence. (83)
The best of Vaiṣṇavas should indeed contemplate those three within that [discus] which consists of the triple Veda;
he should contemplate a seat made of various jewels above them. (84)

In that [lotus], one should visualize a lotus rooted in the heart-lotus, possessing a luster like the rising sun, with eight petals representing the eight sovereign powers, and composed of the syllables of the mantra. (85)
Seated there with the Goddess was he who resembles ten million moons, four-armed, with beautiful limbs, and bearing the conch, the discus, and the mace. (86)
The Lord has eyes as broad as lotus petals, is marked with all the auspicious characteristics, has the Śrīvatsa and Kaustubha on his chest, and wears yellow garments. 87.
Endowed with various ornaments and adorned with divine decorations, his limbs were anointed with divine sandalwood paste and graced by divine flowers. ||88||
Adorned with a forest garland of tender Tulasī leaves,
resembling ten million rising suns in splendor, together with the goddess Śrī.
Having thus meditated upon Śiva, whose body is closely embraced by her who possesses all auspicious marks, one should recite the mantra with a concentrated mind and in a state of purity. (90)
Having performed worship with the mind alone—whether a thousand times, a hundred times, or as much as one's ability allows—one should then desist there with devotion. (91)
One should worship those belonging to him with devotion when they have arrived at that time;
having gratified them with food, drink, and other offerings, one should see them off after following them for a short distance.
Having honored the ancestors and the gods, he should offer libations according to the prescribed rule;
and having fully honored guests and dependents, the husband and wife should then eat together.
One should always avoid the worship of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and bhūtas;
the brahmin who performs such worship out of delusion will certainly become an outcaste (caṇḍāla). 94.
The worship of yakṣas, piśācas, and likewise those who consume liquor and meat, as well as the gods of heaven, is considered equal to the drinking of wine. (95)
For men, the worship of Brahma-rākṣasas, Vetālas, Yakṣas, and Bhūtas is a means for attaining the most terrible hell of Kumbhīpāka. 96.
All merit accumulated over ten million lifetimes—such as sacrifices, acts of charity, and other ritual deeds—is instantly dissolved by the worship of yakṣas, bhūtas, and similar spirits. (97)
Whether it be women or men, by worshipping yakṣas, bhūtas, and so forth, for thousands of koṭis of kalpas and hundreds of koṭis of kalpas, [they do not attain liberation]. (98)
Then, having become a worm in excrement, he sinks down along with his ancestors among the Yakṣas,
Piśācas, and those celestial beings who are characterized by darkness (tamas).
He who eats food that has been offered [to others] becomes a consumer of pus and blood; indeed, he becomes a Yakṣa, a host of Bhūtas, or other cruel Brahma-rākṣasas. 100.
The Brahmin who eats having pointed [the food] out for [such beings] becomes a Cāṇḍāla immediately;
and that woman who worships Yakṣas, Piśācas, serpents, and Rākṣasas [is likewise]. (101)
She goes head-first into the terrible Kālasūtra hell;
having dwelt there in that dreadful place until the end of the kalpa along with her ancestors, [she suffers]. (102)
Indeed, they must consume their own urine and excrement with needle-like mouths through great suffering, being devoured by worms until the dissolution of all beings at the end of the kalpa. 103.
Afterwards, within ten days on the ground, it arises numbering one hundred;
therefore, one should abandon the worship of yakṣas and other deities. (104)
Wherein one should abandon even the independent worship of the Vaidikas, after having worshipped the god Nārāyaṇa Hari, who is adored by the entire world. 105.
One should worship the configuration of their obstructions all around the deity;
one should offer a bali-oblation to them with the remains of what was eaten by Hari.
The Vaiṣṇava should indeed perform the fire-oblation (homa) with the very remnants of that [offering];
having properly offered the oblation to Hari, he should sacrifice the sacrificial food to the gods.
One should also give that to the ancestors; thus one attains everything eternally.
Indeed, the harming of living beings leads the wise to hell. 108.
Whatever property belonging to another is taken by men without it being given—that, O Girijā, you should know to be theft; it is not for the sake of Raka alone. (109)
Garlic, radish—the root of drinking liquor and the like—as well as garlic, sesame paste, drumstick tree, wood-apple, and likewise the kośātakī; ||110||
A man [should avoid] the bottle-gourd, the eggplant, the bījālī, and kavaca fruits; likewise, other such foods that are seen in the scriptures as unfit for consumption. ||111||
By eating the food of those who are not devotees of Viṣṇu, as well as that of the fallen, one attains a manifold and inauspicious hell. (112)
Likewise, food not offered to Viṣṇu is like the flesh of a dog;
it is the food of Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Bhūtas, and is like liquor and wine to a sage. 113.
A man who eats [the food of such persons] goes to hell, where he must consume pus and blood;
this occurs through these acts, such as establishing contact with them, touching them, or living together with them. (114)
They surely go to hell, where they feed on excrement, urine, and worms, due to their association with those who have fallen away from the path and likewise with heretics. (115)
Having known the Ancient One, the Supreme Person, the enjoyer of all sacrifices, one should perform all obligatory and occasional rites. 116.
O Goddess, those who desire the heavenly realm should never worship yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, kūṣmāṇḍas, gaṇas, or bhairavas. ||117||
A twice-born man should avoid the worship of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and bhūtas;
for by doing so, he attains the state of a piśāca for ten million kalpas.
Therefore, the worship of those who have become rākṣasas is forbidden for thousands of millions of kalpas and hundreds of millions of kalpas. 119.
One goes to the Raurava hell by worshipping hosts of yakṣas and bhūtas, or by using other marks most dear to Hari, such as the conch and the discus. (120)

One who is devoid of [virtue] regarding all phenomena and has fallen away from them shall go to hell, due to approaching those who should not be approached, violence, and the theft of another's property. (121)
By eating what is unfit to be eaten, one immediately falls into hell;
likewise, he who abandons a woman held by the hand and goes to another woman [falls into hell]. ||122||
For approaching those who should not be approached causes one to fall immediately into hell;
likewise, it results from associating with those who have fallen [from their caste] and with heretics. (123)
Likewise, a man who persists in forbidden acts goes to hell;
one should avoid association with those who associate [with such people], and one should abandon even that association.
A Vaiṣṇava should avoid even a single family that is joined with sin;
one who is devoted to the One (Ekāntin) should abandon a village that is mixed with great sins.
In the same way, one should avoid even that place where there is supreme exclusivity;
for the Vaiṣṇava path is remembered as consisting of the means such as one's own duty, knowledge, and devotion. (126)
He who performs action, knowledge, and so forth in accordance with the command of Hari, that brahmin becomes a single-minded devotee (ekāntin) who has Vāsudeva as his supreme goal. ||127||
A Vaiṣṇava should completely renounce what ought not to be done with a sinful intent;
he should also mentally abandon the scriptures of the Ekāntins because of their defects.
In that very same way, one should abandon even the supreme single-mindedness with the thought "this is for this world.
Ritual action is traditionally remembered as being of three kinds: obligatory (nitya), occasional (naimittika), and optional (kāmya). ||129||
In this world, knowledge has been proclaimed by the sages as precisely that:
the discernment between what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, and reflection upon the next world. (130)
And the means for attaining that is precisely the knowledge of Viṣṇu’s true nature;
one who is endowed with devotion becomes a devotee, and that is proclaimed as ninefold. (131)
The auspicious marking of the body with the Sudarśana, the vertical *puṇḍra*, and other such signs;
the recitation of mantras from a true guru; and the worship of Hari according to the prescribed rite. (132)
Remembering Viṣṇu, chanting His names, serving the Supreme Soul, prostrating before Him, and worshipping His devotees. (133)
Service to the sacred fords of grace and ninefold devotion are prescribed;
through these, the Vaiṣṇava indeed takes refuge in Hari, the God. (134)
That surrender (prapatti) is to be known as threefold;
it is proclaimed to be of three types: tāmasī, rājasī, and sāttvikī. ||135||
That perfection (siddhi) is also threefold: common to all embodied beings;
O Goddess, a Vaiṣṇava should indeed abandon these four [categories] as things to be relinquished.
A person should indeed take refuge in this Vaiṣṇava Brahman, which has become the means;
having abandoned the state of being a means, such as ritual action, knowledge, and so forth. (137)
The most excellent of great devotees should act for the pleasure of the Blessed One;
he should indeed worship Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, with devotion at the three times of day. 138.
On special occasions, one should worship according to the auspicious rite;
every day during the month of Kārttika, one should worship with jasmine flowers.
One who is self-controlled and firm in his vow should offer an unbroken lamp;
having fed the Brāhmaṇas, he shall attain union with Hari. 140.
For one month without interruption during the month of Uṣasi, one should worship the Lord of Gods with blue lotuses and white and black karavīra flowers.
One should offer incense, lamps, and food offerings according to one's capacity;
at the conclusion, one should feed the brāhmaṇas who are the most excellent of great bhāgavatas. 142.
One undoubtedly obtains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices by bathing in a river, especially on the day of the month of Tapas when the sun has risen. (143)
O lady of auspicious countenance, one should worship Mādhava with flowers and blue lotuses;
there, one should devoutly offer divine milk-rice mixed with clarified butter. 144.
Having bathed, one should worship Viṣṇu continuously for one month;
daily, one should offer a garden filled with sugar and water.

O lady of auspicious appearance, at the end of each month one should worship the Vaiṣṇavas with devotion; likewise, in the month of Madhu, one should always worship them with Bakula flowers and fruits as well. (146)
One should worship the Lord of the worlds and offer sweetened rice (guḍānna);
with a well-composed mind, one should feed Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇas during those months.
One shall daily obtain the merit of a thousand-year-long worship;
in the month of Mādhava, one should worship the God with hundred-petaled lotuses and great blue lilies. 148.
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rite, O Goddess, one should devotedly offer curd-rice mixed with fruit and molasses-water to Him. 149.

O Pārvatī, when conjoined with Lakṣmī, the Lord of the World becomes pleased; [he is likewise pleased] by white lotuses, pale-pink flowers, and white and blue water-lilies during the month of Śukra. 150.
Having worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa with food joined by mango fruits and having offered it with devotion, one indeed becomes the giver of ten million cows. ||151||
Having fed the Vaiṣṇavas, one then attains everything infinite;
[one should worship] Acyuta, the Lord of the God of Gods and the husband of Lakṣmī, in the month of Āṣāḍha. (152)
One should worship daily with auspicious flowers and offer milk-rice (pāyasa);
at the end of the month, one should feed the brāhmaṇas who are the most excellent of great bhāgavatas. 153.
One undoubtedly obtains the merit of performing worship for sixty thousand years by honoring Viṣṇu in the month of Nabhas with *puṃnāga* flowers and *ketakī* petals. (154)
Having worshipped Acyuta with devotion, one shall not undergo birth again;
then, one should devoutly offer cakes mixed with sugar and ghee. (155)
Likewise, one should feed Brāhmaṇas; thus one shall obtain all honor.
In the month of Nabhasya as well, one should worship the Lord with jasmine and kurabaka flowers. (156)
One should devoutly offer milk-rice mixed with jaggery there;
one shall obtain the fruit of giving away ten million cows every day. (157)
One should worship Madhusūdana with blue lotuses on the full moon days of the months of Āṣāḍha and Mārgaśīrṣa;
with devotion, one should offer him milk mixed with cakes.
For thousands of millions of kalpas and hundreds of millions of kalpas, he attains the world of Viṣṇu, joyful and surrounded by his own kinsmen. ||159||
Likewise, having worshipped Acyuta with devotion on the day of Ūrja with tender Tulasī leaves, one shall attain union with Him (sāyujya). ||160||
One should properly offer food accompanied by milk, clarified butter, and sugar, as well as rice cooked with milk (pāyasa) and cakes, in due order and with devotion. 161.
On the new moon day, on the twelfth lunar day, under a Viṣṇu asterism, at the transit of the sun, during Vyatīpāta, and likewise during an eclipse of the moon or the sun.

O lady of beautiful countenance, one should especially worship Viṣṇu according to one's capacity on the day of the preceptor’s passing, as well as on the birth-stars of both the preceptor and Hari. (163)
The best of the twice-born should perform an oblation to Viṣṇu according to his capacity;
there, he should offer handfuls of flowers for each image, equal in number to the Vedas.

One should also perform the breaking of the fast with sacrificial porridge (caru) or milk-rice (pāyasa); one should feed the Vaiṣṇava Brahmins and give them a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to one's ability.
Having uplifted ten million members of one's lineage, one shall attain the station of Viṣṇu;
even if one is unable to perform sacrifices according to all the Vedas, one should worship the Supreme Bhāgavata. 166.
Or, for seven nights without interruption, one should daily perform a thousandfold offering of flowers with Vaiṣṇava hymns (anuvākas) and likewise perform the fire-oblation (homa). ||167||
Or, for the sake of pleasing the Blessed One, the unwise person should offer worship with each verse;
or else, he should indeed recite the jewel of mantras continuously for seven nights. (168)
One should offer oblations with clarified butter one thousand and eight times and perform sacrifice;
moreover, the wise man should especially honor the most excellent of the great bhāgavatas. 169.
And at the end, the twice-born should perform the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) according to the extent of his wealth;
he should perform the avabhṛtha with the Vaiṣṇava anuvākas.
Having bathed here according to the prescribed rule and to the best of his ability, the best of the twice-born should, with devotion, wash his feet in a beautiful and auspicious vessel. (171)
One should worship with perfumes, flowers, and so forth, as well as with garments, ornaments, and the like;
or one should worship according to one's ability with betel-leaf, fruits, or other offerings. 172.
Having fed him with food, drink, and other offerings, and having bowed down again and again,
he followed him as far as the boundary of his domain, and after paying homage, he took his leave.
Having bowed again with devotion, he should then slowly return there; entering his home, he, with a self-restrained mind, should worship the Lord of Gods.
Thus one should worship Viṣṇu without weariness for as long as one lives;
and one should especially worship his devotees always, O auspicious lady. (175)
Of all forms of worship, the worship of Viṣṇu is supreme;
O Goddess, the worship of His devotees is even higher than that. (176)
Even after having worshipped Govinda, if one does not further worship His devotees, he should not be known as a Bhāgavata; he is remembered merely as a hypocrite. (177)
Therefore, a person should always worship the Vaiṣṇavas with great effort;
by honoring the great devotees of Viṣṇu, one crosses over the entire flood of suffering. 178.
Thus, O Goddess, I have described the supreme worship of Viṣṇu, including both the obligatory and occasional rites, as well as the worship of his attendants. 179.

O Goddess, I have explained to you his essential nature as the Puruṣa, as well as the means to the fruit; his abode, his body, and the fourfold group beginning with action—what else do you wish to hear? 180.

Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Ritual for the Worship of Viṣṇu and the Conduct of Vaiṣṇavas," in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, within the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses, in the dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara. ||253||
(254) Chapter Two Hundred and Fifty-Four.
Vasiṣṭha said:
Thus addressed by her husband, who held a spear in his hand,
that goddess then prostrated before the high-souled one and spoke with palms joined in reverence.
Pārvatī said:
"O Lord, you have indeed spoken well regarding the supreme Vaiṣṇava dharma—the most secret of secrets, the true nature of Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self. (2)
I am blessed, I have accomplished my purpose, O you who are saluted by all the gods;
through your grace, I worship the eternal Lord of Gods. (3)
Vasiṣṭha said: Then, having heard those words, Bhava, the destroyer of Tripura,
embraced the Goddess and spoke with a heart full of joy.
Rudra said:
"Excellent, excellent, O Great Goddess! Excellent, excellent, O fair-faced one!
Worship Hṛṣīkeśa, the infallible husband of Lakṣmī."
"O blessed lady, I have accomplished my purpose through you, the wife of Viṣṇu;
and through your guru, O fair-limbed one, the wise Vāmadeva."
"Permitted by me, O daughter of the mountain, worship the ancient Lord, Puruṣottama;
for only by worshipping Keśava according to the path of the guru’s instruction does one obtain all that is desired, and not otherwise. (7)
Vasiṣṭha said:
O King, having been addressed thus, the goddess then went at once to the presence of Vāmadeva, joyful and longing to worship Viṣṇu. 8.
Having approached that guru, O Goddess, and having worshipped and prostrated before him, she, being humble and with palms joined in reverence, spoke to the best of sages. (9)
Pārvatī said:
"O Blessed One, O best of the twice-born, by your grace I shall perform the perfect worship of Hari; you ought to grant me your permission. (10)
Vasiṣṭha said: Thus addressed by that goddess, the great sage Vāmadeva,
acting as her preceptor, bestowed upon her the most excellent and supreme mantra according to the prescribed ritual.
The best of sages, the spiritual preceptor, having proclaimed the thousand names of Viṣṇu and having also explained the procedure for worship,
spoke with supreme affection to Pārvatī, who was firm in her vows. 12.
Vāmadeva said:
O fair-faced one, having daily worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa in the morning,
you should thereafter recite the Thousand Names.
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having been thus addressed by that preceptor, who was delighted in his inner soul, he honored him and bowed down, then returned once more to his own abode. 14.
Pārvatī was thus instructed by her preceptor Vāmadeva;
then, after some days had passed, on the twelfth day, the bull-bannered Lord [Śiva] appeared.
Having worshipped Viṣṇu on the delightful peak of Kailāsa, Śaṅkara sat down to eat; then Śaṅkara spoke to Pārvatī. (16)
Śaṅkara said:
"O Pārvatī, come with me to eat, O you who are honored by the world.
Vasiṣṭha said:
The goddess Pārvatī spoke to him after having recited the Thousand Names.
"Then, O Lord, I shall eat; let it be eaten by you first, O Master.
Thereupon, the Supreme Lord spoke to Pārvatī with a smile: ||18||
Śaṅkara said:
"O Pārvatī, you are blessed, you have accomplished your purpose, and you are a devotee of Viṣṇu;
for devotion to Viṣṇu is difficult to attain without great fortune, O Goddess. (19)
"Rāma, Rāma, Rāma—rejoice in the delightful Rāma!
O fair-faced one, the name of Rāma is equal to a thousand names. (20)
O Pārvatī, as I hear names beginning with the letter 'ra', my mind becomes serene through the suspicion that they might be the name of Rāma. (21)
"O Great Goddess, having uttered the name 'Rāma,' eat now together with me.
Vasiṣṭha said:
Then, having uttered the name 'Rāma' and having eaten together, Pārvatī [did so]. 22.
Addressed as "Rāma" by Śambhu while seated together with him, the Great Goddess,
her mind filled with affection and the syllable *praṇava*, questioned the god Śaṅkara.
Pārvatī said:
You have declared that the name of Rāma is equal to a thousand names;
if there are other names for the enemy of Rāvaṇa, please tell them.
"Let it be told to me, O Lord of Gods; devotion has arisen in me toward that. (24)
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
Listen, O Pārvatī, I shall declare the names of Rāmacandra;
whatever worldly or Vedic words exist, O Pārvatī, [I shall speak them]. (25)
There are more than a thousand names of Rāmacandra;
among them, the one hundred and eight names are indeed the most preeminent.
Even a single name of Viṣṇu is considered superior to all the Vedas;
indeed, thousands of such names are equal to the name of Rāma.
O beloved, whatever fruit is obtained from the recitation of all the Vedas and mantras, that same fruit is attained by the name of Rāma alone, multiplied ten millionfold. ||28||
Listen to the principal names of Rāma, O lady of auspicious appearance;
I shall declare them to you, my beloved, as they have been celebrated by the sages. (29)
Oṃ! Śrī Rāma, Rāmacandra, and Rāmabhadra, the eternal;
lotus-eyed, glorious, lord of kings, the preeminent scion of Raghu. ||30||

The beloved of Jānakī, the victorious, the conqueror of enemies, the agitator of men (Janārdana), the friend of Viśvāmitra, the self-controlled, and one who is intent upon protecting those who seek refuge. ||31||
The subduer of Vālin, eloquent, truthful in speech, and of true valor; one whose vows are true, who is the fruit of his own observances, and who is ever the refuge of Hanumān. (32)
The son of Kauśalyā, the destroyer of Khara, the one skilled in slaying Virādha, the protector of Vibhīṣaṇa, and the remover of the ten-headed Rāvaṇa’s heads. ||33||
He who shattered the seven palm trees, the destroyer of Hara’s staff, the crusher of the great pride of Paraśurāma, and the slayer of Tāḍakā. (34)
He has mastered the Vedānta; he is the soul of the Vedas; he is the sole medicine for the bondage of worldly existence;
he is the destroyer of the three-headed Dūṣaṇa; he is the triple-formed one; he possesses the three qualities; and he is the triple Veda.
Trivikrama, the soul of the three worlds, whose virtuous conduct and fame are celebrated;
the protector of the three worlds, the wielder of the bow, who made his dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest. ||36||
He is the purifier of Ahalyā, devoted to his father, the bestower of boons, one who has conquered his senses, conquered anger, and conquered greed—the preceptor of the world. ||37||
Taking refuge on Citrakūṭa with his hosts of bears and monkeys, he who grants protection and boons was there served by the son of Sumitrā. ||38||
He is the supreme god of all gods, the one who restored the life of the immortal monkey, the slayer of Māyāmārīca, the highly fortunate one, and the mighty-armed one. ||39||
Praised by all the gods, gentle, devoted to Brahman, the best of sages;
a great yogi, most magnanimous, he who grants Sugrīva a stable kingdom. ||40||
He is remembered as the one whose fruit exceeds all merit, the destroyer of all sins;
he is the primal person, the great person, and likewise the supreme person. (41)
Rāghava is the source of merit, the great essence, the ancient Supreme Person; he has a smiling face, speaks measuredly, and is the first to speak. 42.
Profound with infinite virtues, steadfast, supreme in the quality of self-control, possessing the conduct of a human through illusion, he is worshipped by the great gods. ||43||
Hari, the builder of the bridge, the conqueror of the lord of waters, who embodies all sacred fords;
he of the dark-blue body, the beautiful one, the hero, clad in yellow garments, and the wielder of the bow.
He is the Lord of all sacrifices and the sacrifice itself, free from old age and death; he is the establisher of the auspicious Liṅga, devoid of all primordial qualities. ||45||
The Supreme Self, the Supreme Brahman, whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss;
the supreme light, the supreme abode, the supreme ether, higher than the highest. ||46||
The Supreme Lord, the one who has gone beyond, the further shore, the soul of all beings, the auspicious one—thus are the one hundred and eight names of Śrī Rāmacandra. 47.
O Goddess, out of affection for you, this which is more secret than the secret has been proclaimed;
whoever should read or even hear it with a mind endowed with devotion. (48)
One is liberated from all sins arising from hundreds of millions of eons;
waters turn into dry land, and enemies become friends. (49)
Kings fall into servitude, fires become mild, living beings become favorable, and even fickle fortunes attain stability. (50)
The planets bestow their favor and calamities subside for the man who recites [this] with a spirit of devotion to the one born of the mountain. 51.
One who recites this with supreme devotion brings the three worlds under his control;
whatever desire he forms, he attains it through such recitation. (52)
For thousands of crores of kalpas and hundreds of crores of kalpas,
he rejoices eternally in Vaikuṇṭha, together with ten ancestors and ten descendants.
Those people who praise Rāma—who is dark as a blade of dūrvā grass, lotus-eyed, and clad in yellow garments—with divine names, are not worldly beings. 54.
Salutations to Rāma, the auspicious Rāma, Rāmacandra, the Creator; to the Lord of the Raghus, the Protector, the husband of Sītā. ||55||
O Great Goddess, by reciting this mantra day and night, one is completely liberated from all sins and attains union with Viṣṇu. ||56||
Thus, O fair-browed one, this majesty of Rāmacandra, which is equal to the Vedas and bears an auspicious name, has been narrated by me to you out of affection. 57.
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having heard that majesty of the Supreme Self spoken by Śaṅkara, she attained incomparable joy, drenched in tears of bliss. (58)
Having prostrated, Pārvatī spoke to the Lord of Gods, her husband whose banner bears the bull:
Pārvatī said:
"Oh, how incomparable is the majesty of Rāma, the Supreme Soul!"
The satisfaction of his ears shall not cease even for hundreds of ten-thousand kalpas. (59)
"I am blessed and I have accomplished my purpose; everything has been told by you, O sinless one.
By your grace, may devotion to Hari be mine in birth after birth. (60)
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having spoken thus to her husband, Gaurī, the supreme devotee of the Lord,
[offered salutations] to Rāma, the auspicious Rāma, Rāmacandra, the Creator.
Salutation to the Lord of Raghunātha’s lineage, the husband of Sītā. ||61||
Reciting this very mantra in all circumstances, Pārvatī dwelt happily on Kailāsa together with her husband.
All this has been declared to you, O King, which is the most secret of secrets;
the scriptures proclaimed by Rudra are indeed tāmasa, O Ruler of the Earth. (63)
For the sake of deluding the worlds,
the bull-bannered Lord Hara spoke this one secret to the Goddess.
O King, for the sake of pleasing the Goddess, Mahādeva, being intent upon it, explained the true meaning of the mantra, its secret essence, and its core significance.
O King, whoever shall read or even hear this wonderful dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara with a mind endowed with devotion, [shall attain the highest goal]. (66)
He shall become worthy of universal veneration, omniscient, and a great devotee;
liberated from all phenomena, he attains the supreme state. ||67||
O mighty lord of kings, you are indeed blessed in this world;
for in your lineage dwells the glorious Hari, the ancient Supreme Person. (68)
"The son of Daśaratha shall indeed be born for the welfare of all the worlds;
therefore, O King, the Ikṣvākus are worthy of worship even by the gods. (69)
"For those by whom the lotus-eyed Lord Rāma has been born...

Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-fourth chapter, titled "The Recitation of the One Hundred and Eight Names of Rāmacandra," within the Umā-Maheśvara Saṃvāda of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the compendium of fifty-five thousand verses.
(255) Chapter Two Hundred and Fifty-Five.
Dilīpa said:
O Brahmin, you have explained all dharmas without exception—the common and the specific natures of both the Supreme Self and the individual soul. (1)
Heaven and liberation have been described, as well as the means for attaining them;
O best of the twice-born, O eternal teacher, by your grace I am blessed. (2)
O best of the twice-born, out of curiosity I ask you another question;
please tell me the truth, out of your affection and respect for me. (3)
Why did Rudra, the destroyer of Tripura and the most excellent among the great devotees of the Lord, assume a censurable form along with his wife? (4)
And how could the nature of the yoni and liṅga belong to that Great-Souled One? He has five faces, four arms, holds a trident in his hand, and possesses three eyes. (5)
O bull among the twice-born, how did you come to possess such censurable form?
O delighter of Mitra and Varuṇa, explain all of this to me.
Vasiṣṭha said:
Listen, O King, for out of respect you ask me;
in a person whose heart is pure, wisdom arises regarding the highest good. (7)
Formerly, Svāyambhuva Manu went to Mandara, the best of mountains, together with sages to perform an unsurpassed long sacrificial session (dīrghasattra).
All the sages of pure vows, the best among those learned in various scriptures, possessing a radiance like that of the rising sun or fire, assembled there. (9)
The Brahmins were knowers of all the Vedas and devoted to all duties;
during this great sacrificial session, they were sages whose impurities had been destroyed.
To investigate the true nature of the deities, those whose wealth is penance spoke among themselves:
"Among the Brahmins who are knowers of the Vedas, which one is the most worshipful deity? (11)
Among Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, which one grants liberation to men when praised? Whose water from the feet is to be served, and whose remains of food are purifying? (12)
Who is the imperishable one, the supreme abode, the eternal Supreme Self? By whose grace would this sacred ford become a source of satisfaction for the ancestors? (13)
As they were seated together, a great discussion arose;
some of those great sages there declared that Rudra is one.
"The Brahman alone is to be worshipped," say some of the best of sages; "The Sun alone is to be worshipped by the souls," say others who are most excellent. (15)
He who is all-pervading, glorious, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person, imperishable, lotus-eyed, Vāsudeva, higher than the highest. ||16||
"Viṣṇu, who is without beginning or end, is indeed the Supreme Lord;
he is the most excellent of deities to be worshipped"—thus other twice-born ones also proclaimed. (17)
While they were disputing there, Manu Svāyambhuva said:
"That Lord who consists of pure sattva and possesses auspicious qualities," (18)
The lotus-eyed, glorious Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person, is the one and only Master worshipped by the Brahmins who are learned in the Vedas. (19)
"Among the Brahmins, and not among others, are those who are unmixed with passion and darkness.
Having heard these words of his, all the great sages,
with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus to the Brahmin Bhṛgu, that treasure-house of asceticism.
The sages said:
"O observer of noble vows, you are capable of cutting through our doubt;
O observer of noble vows, go into the presence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa. (21)
Having gone into their presence and seeing them so extremely agitated,
O Sage, he perceived within them the quality of pure sattva.
He alone is worthy of worship by the Brahmins, and never anyone else;
he will truly be one composed of pure *sattva* and devoted to the Brahmanas.
In this world, he shall possess the sanctity of sacred fords among the Brahmins;
even his remnants after eating shall be highly purifying for the gods and the ancestors. (24)
Therefore, O best of sages, O Lord, quickly create a dwelling for the gods that is for the benefit of all the worlds. (25)
Having been addressed thus, that best of sages then went quickly to Kailāsa,
where Vāmadeva was with the bull-bannered Lord Śiva.
Having approached the door of the great-souled Śaṅkara, the twice-born one, seeing that most fierce [deity] with a trident in hand, spoke to him. ||27||
"I have arrived, the brahmin Bhṛgu, to see Hara, the best of gods;
announce me quickly to the high-souled Śaṅkara. (28)
Having heard those words of his, the Lord of all the hosts spoke harsh words to the great sage of immeasurable splendor.
"Śaṅkara sports with the Goddess within that Lord's secret treasury;
turn back, O best of sages, if you desire to live. (30)
Thus repulsed by him, that great ascetic remained there for many days at the gateway of the Great Lord's residence. (31)
"Since he, intoxicated by union with women, has treated me with contempt, therefore his own form shall become that of the female organ and the male organ. (32)
Do not despise a Brahmin; he who has fallen into darkness has become devoid of devotion to the Veda and is unworthy of honor among the twice-born. (33)
Therefore, food, water, flowers, and likewise the oblation offered to him—all this shall become his discarded remains (nirmālya); of this there is no doubt. (34)
Having thus cursed Śaṅkara, who is worshipped by the worlds, the one of great splendor spoke to the exceedingly fierce Gaṇa, Naṃdi, the wielder of the trident, O King.
Those in the world who are devotees of Rudra, wearing ashes and carrying bone-lingas, have attained the state of being *pākhaṇḍas* (heretics); indeed, they have become outsiders to the Veda.
Having thus cursed Rudra, the destroyer of Tripura,
the sage went there to the world of Brahmā, which is honored by all the worlds.
There, seeing Brahmā Parameṣṭhin seated together with the gods, the high-minded one prostrated before the Lord with palms joined in reverence.
Having bowed down before him, I, a great ascetic, remained silent;
yet, upon seeing that tiger among sages, I was enveloped by the quality of passion (rajas). ||39||
Dhātṛ did not honor that approaching sage; neither did the Creator rise to meet him nor offer him kind words. ||40||
Thus, by means of his great sovereignty, he who has the lotus as his seat remained there.
Seeing that lotus-seated one overflowing with passion, the great sage—
The Grandfather of the worlds, possessed of great splendor, spoke these words:
"Since you disregard me because you are overwhelmed by excessive passion."
"Therefore, you shall attain a state of being unworthy of worship by all the worlds.
Having thus cursed the high-souled Brahmā, who is honored by the world, [he departed]. (43)
The Brahmin Bhṛgu went suddenly to the temple of the Blessed One;
having entered the Vaiṣṇava world on the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk.
There, being honored by those illustrious men as was fitting for an Arhat,
the twice-born one entered the inner city unopposed.
Having entered that spotless celestial chariot which resembled the sun,
he beheld the Lord of Kamalā reclining upon a serpent-couch.
Seeing him with his two feet being massaged by the lotus-hands of Lakṣmī, Bhṛgu, that tiger among sages, was filled with anger.
O beautiful one, he cast his left foot upon Viṣṇu’s chest;
the Blessed One, rising quickly and saying with joy, "I am blessed," [spoke thus]. 48.
Rejoicing, he pressed his feet with both hands;
having gently massaged that foot, he spoke these sweet words: ||49||
"O brahmin-sage, I am blessed this very day; I have achieved my life's purpose forever.
By the touch of your feet, my body shall attain auspiciousness. (50)

May the waters from the feet of the Brahmins—which are the cause for attaining all prosperity, the comets that extinguish the rising masses of calamities, and the bridges across the shoreless ocean of saṃsāra—purify me once again. (51)
For him whose body always bears the dust from the feet of a Brahmin,
all sacred fords such as the Gaṅgā undoubtedly abide.
Having spoken thus, Janārdana rose suddenly and, together with the Goddess,
worshipped [him] with devotion using divine garlands, sandalwood paste, and other offerings.

Seeing him, that tiger among sages, filled with joy and with eyes brimming with tears, rose from his excellent seat and bowed down to that ocean of compassion. Joining his palms in reverence, the one of great austerity spoke out of delight: ||54||
Śrī Bhṛgu said:
Oh, what a form! Oh, what peace! Oh, what knowledge and great prosperity!
Oh, how pure is the vision of Hari’s sattva-guṇa! (55)
The innate auspiciousness of that ocean of virtues is such that it does not exist at all in any other among all the inhabitants of the heavens. (56)
You alone are the friend of the Brahmins and their refuge; you alone are the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama).
You alone are the Lord of the Brahmins; there is no other god to be worshipped anywhere.
O Puruṣottama, those who worship other gods excluding you—
Having fallen into the state of being devoid of the three Vedas, they were censured by the entire world. ||58||
O Janārdana, you alone are the one to be worshipped by the Brahmins who are learned in the Vedas;
no other among the gods is ever to be honored. 59.
Brahmā, Rudra, and the others are devoid of self-control and are mixed with the qualities of rajas and tamas;
you, however, possess the quality of pure sattva and are worthy of worship by the twice-born.
The water from your feet is to be served to the ancestors, the gods, and all the brahmins;
it bestows liberation and removes all impurities.
The remnants of what you have eaten shall be worthy of consumption for the ancestors, the gods, and the brahmins, but never for anyone else. (62)
But for all other gods, food, flowers, and likewise water— all such offerings become untouchable once they have been used as *nirmālya*, being equal to liquor.
Therefore, having always worshipped the eternal [Lord], a wise brāhmaṇa should constantly partake of the food eaten at your sacred ford. 64.
A brāhmaṇa should not look upon another god, nor should he worship him; he should not eat the prasāda of another, nor should he enter the temple of another. 65.
O Brahmin, if one does not give water here at the time of the ancestral rite (śrāddha),
all that food you have eaten and that sacred place (tīrtha) shall become entirely fruitless.
For thousands of millions of eons and hundreds of millions of eons,
his ancestors fall into hells filled with pus and blood.
O Lord of the Universe, whatever one offers as an oblation or gives away after it has been dedicated to you,
that brings about the satisfaction of the deities and the ancestors, and one enjoys supreme bliss.
Therefore, you alone are worthy of worship among the Brahmins; there is no other whatsoever.
He who, out of delusion, should worship others will become a heretic.
You are indeed Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Vāsudeva, the eternal Viṣṇu, the omnipresent, the permanent Supreme Self, and the Great Lord. ||70||

You alone are to be served by the Brahmins, for you are devoted to the Brahman and possess pure sattva; indeed, this is because of your venerability toward the Brahmins and also because of your quality of pure sattva.
"Attain the status of a Brahmin among all these gods;
for the Brahmins always worship you alone as the Supreme Person."
They became Brahmins there, and none other; of this there is no doubt.
Devakī’s son is devoted to Brahman; Madhusūdana is devoted to Brahman.
The lotus-eyed one is devoted to Brahman; Viṣṇu, the infallible, is devoted to Brahman;
the Lord Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, the infallible Hari, is devoted to Brahman.
The benevolent toward Brahmins is Nārasiṃha, as well as the imperishable Nārāyaṇa;
the benevolent toward Brahmins is Śrīdhara, the Lord of Śrī, Govinda, and likewise Vāmana. (75)
Keśava, the Supreme Person, is the friend of Brahman, the sacrificial Boar;
the glorious Rāma, the lotus-eyed descendant of Raghu, is the friend of Brahman. ||76||
Padmanābha is devoted to Brahman, as is the Lord Dāmodara;
Mādhava is devoted to Brahman, as is the Lord Trivikrama, the sacrifice itself.
Hṛṣīkeśa, Janārdana, who is clad in yellow garments, is devoted to the Brahmins.
Homage to Vāsudeva, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the deity who is devoted to the Brahmins. (78)
Salutation to Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, whose eyes are like lotuses;
salutation to Vāsudeva, Viṣṇu, the deity who is the friend of Brahman.
Salutations to you, the Supreme Self, filled with auspicious qualities;
salutations to the God of Brahman, who embodies the form of all the gods. ||80||
Salutations always to You who possess the form of a boar, the Lord of the Three Vedas;
salutations to the God who is the friend of Brahman, who reclines upon the serpent-couch. 81.
Salutations again and again to Rāghava, whose eyes are like lotus petals;
all the gods and sages have been deluded by your illusory power (māyā). ||82||
They do not know you, O Lord, the Great-Souled One, the Sovereign of all worlds;
for even those who know all the Vedas do not know you, O Blessed One.
O Lord, neither by the qualities of name and form, nor even by your glorious conduct or your difficult deeds,
is anyone able to fully comprehend your supreme nature.
Sent by the great seers, I have come to your presence, O Keśava, to learn of your virtuous conduct and qualities; this is my purpose. (85)
"O Govinda, O ocean of mercy, that which was given [by me] upon your chest must be forgiven.
Having spoken thus, Bhṛgu bowed repeatedly to the Lord. (86)
Being honored there by divine and great-souled sages,
he returned with a joyful heart to the sacrificial ground known as Śubhāhvaya.
Seeing the Great-Souled One arrived there, the great sages rose to meet him, paid their respects, and performed worship according to the prescribed rites. ||88||
The bull among sages informed them of all that:
how the two supreme gods, Brahmā and Śiva, were overwhelmed by the qualities of rajas and tamas.
"O best of sages, these two were cursed by me;
having fallen into a state of hostility toward Brahmins, they have assumed this contemptible form. (90)
On the peak of Kailāsa, Śaṅkara was cursed by him; he was enveloped in darkness, whereas Viṣṇu consists of pure goodness and is an ocean of auspicious qualities.
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Brahman, Hari is the deity of the brahmins;
he is the friend of the brahmins, the Lord of Śrī, Viṣṇu, Vāsudeva, and Janārdana.
O bulls among men, he alone— the lotus-eyed Govinda, Hari, the infallible Acyuta, who is devoted to the Brahmins— is worthy of worship by the twice-born, and no other.
He who, out of delusion, worships another shall become a heretic;
yet by the mere remembrance of Kṛṣṇa, even sinners attain liberation.
His water for washing the feet should be used, and the remnants of his food are purifying;
they bestow heaven and liberation upon men, especially for Brāhmaṇas. 95.
One should daily offer oblations to the gods with what has been offered to Viṣṇu, and likewise give that to the ancestors; thus one attains all desires. (96)
O twice-born ones, if one should offer food already eaten by Hari to the ancestors during the śrāddha rite,
his ancestors shall constantly consume feces and urine.
Therefore, the grace of Viṣṇu should be sought by the twice-born;
however, the remains of offerings (nirmālya) belonging to other deities are to be censured. (98)
A Brāhmaṇa who, being weak in knowledge, eats even once the remains of offerings (nirmālya) made to Śaṅkara and others, will certainly become an outcaste (caṇḍāla). 99.
O best of the twice-born, the remains of offerings (nirmālya) belonging to Rudra and the other celestial dwellers are cooked by the fires of hell for thousands of millions of kalpas.
The food of Rākṣasas, Yakṣas, and Piśācas is considered equal to liquor and meat;
therefore, it must not be eaten by Brāhmaṇas, for such food is the sacrificial oblation (havis) consumed by the gods. 101.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, abandoning all else, worship Viṣṇu alone, the eternal one, with vigilance for as long as you live. (102)
Those of pure mind, free from doubt, having sought [the truth] through the five purifications beginning with heat (tāpa), perceive that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. (103)
"O best of the twice-born, worship Hari, who is beyond the ordinary, with perfect devotion; O Brahmins, you have become extraordinary and auspicious, for your arms are marked with the discus. (104)
Those who are devoid of the marks of the discus and other signs are considered common folk belonging to the quality of darkness (tamas).
Therefore, [one should seek] Hari’s [devotion], which burns away the flood of sins arising from such common worldly existence. 105.
One should bear the heated discus and conch at the roots of the arms,
and having applied vertical marks (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) on the limbs according to the path prescribed in the scriptures.
One should worship Puruṣottama with the jewel of mantras according to the prescribed rite, and one should constantly and unweariedly perform service to him out of devotion. 107.
In the worship of that [deity], one should always honor the thirty gods, as well as that Supreme Lord who is the enjoyer of all sacrifices. 108.
O twice-born ones, having indeed understood this, one should constantly offer oblations, give gifts, and recite prayers. ||109||
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having been addressed thus, all those sages, whose taints were exhausted, bowed properly to Bhṛgu and then spoke with palms joined in reverence. 110.
The sages said:
O Blessed One, you alone are the dispeller of doubt, O best of the twice-born;
O Brahmin, you are indeed the refuge of the worlds, and you alone are the supreme goal.
You alone are the supreme dharma; you alone are the supreme austerity.
By your grace, O Brahmin, may we become as if we were not deluded.
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having thus praised the brahmin Bhṛgu, all those great ṛṣis,
having received the mantras from him, worshipped the Imperishable One (Acyuta).
All this has been related to you incidentally, O best of kings;
indeed, O supreme monarch, it was through the touch of Rāma’s lotus-like hand.
That form will be stainless, though censured by the world;
Rāghava is the Supreme Person, the purifier of all the gods. (115)
By his very touch, Śaṅkara and the others became stainless;
Janārdana is the father and mother of all the gods. (116)
He is the protector of all worlds and an ocean of the quality of affection;
one who desires the supreme state should go to him alone for refuge. (117)
All this ancient lore, equal in measure to the Vedas, was told by Brahmā to Manu Svāyambhuva on the earth, O King. 118.
Just as for one who is humble through devotion to Viṣṇu and possesses pure being (śuddhasattva), one should constantly cause him to hear those stories of the Lord which lead to liberation. 119.
A man who is marked with the conch, the discus, and the vertical sectarian mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) is one who proclaims [the truth];
O son, listen constantly from his mouth as to how you may become his spiritual son. 120.
But he who constantly causes this to be heard, or reads it with a well-composed mind and undivided devotion to the Lord of Śrī, shall always possess such devotion. 121.
One seeking knowledge obtains knowledge; one seeking dharma attains dharma;
one seeking liberation obtains liberation; and one seeking desire obtains happiness. 122.

On the twelfth lunar day, during the conjunction with the Śravaṇa asterism and the Sun, at the time of a solar or lunar eclipse, and on the new moon and full moon days, one should recite [this] endowed with devotion. (123)
Whoever, being composed in mind, recites even half a verse or a quarter of a verse, obtains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices; of this there is no doubt. ||124||
Thus has been told this ancient secret, which is conducive to well-being;
worship Hṛṣīkeśa if you desire the supreme state. 125.
Sūta said:
Having been addressed thus by his preceptor Vasiṣṭha, that best of kings bowed to his guru and honored him as was fitting.

Therefore, having received the mantra according to the prescribed rite from an excellent brahmin, he should worship Hṛṣīkeśa without laziness for as long as he lives; in the end, he shall attain the eternal abode of Hari, which is accessible only to yogis. 127.

Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Test of Bhṛgu," in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of fifty-five thousand verses composed by Vyāsa.
Thus ends the sixth section, the Uttara-khaṇḍa, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
The Greatness of Puruṣottama.
Now begins the seventh section, the Kriyā-khaṇḍa, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
(1) Now begins the first chapter.
Salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa.
Now begins the section on the Essence of Kriyā-yoga:
We perpetually salute the stainless pair of lotus-feet of Lakṣmīnātha, upon which the mass of hair from the heads of the rows of gods, beginning with Brahmā and Īśvara, bow down in prostration.

Through devotion, [one attains] that which causes the abundant blossoming of the exquisite beauty of the lake of the yogi’s mind—a multitude of drops of nectar from the waters of the Gaṅgā that dispel the suffering of saṃsāra. ||1||
The Blessed One, having manifested His forms in many ways, protects the entire world; those who are intent upon worshipping His feet do not sink again into the ocean of worldly existence.
That Lord whose dwelling is eternally within the lotus-hearts of all living beings—[to Him I bow].
Salutation to that Lord Hari, who assumes the form of the lovely boar. ||2||
Having extracted all dharmas from the Vedas,
the Lord,
in the form of Vyāsa, proclaimed this [Purāṇa] for the welfare of the world.
I bow to Him, who is accompanied by Kamalā. ||3||
Once, all the sages, desiring the welfare of the entire world, held a delightful assembly in the most beautiful Naimiṣa forest. (4)
In the meantime, the highly illustrious Sūta, a disciple of Vyāsa endowed with great splendor, arrived accompanied by a multitude of disciples while remembering Hari. (5)
Beholding the charioteer approaching, who had reached the further shore of the meaning of the scriptures,
Śaunaka and all the other ascetics rose and paid him homage.
Then he, the best among those who know all dharmas, suddenly prostrated himself like a staff upon the ground before those supreme Vaiṣṇava sages with great devotion.
On that excellent seat provided by those best of sages, the one of great intelligence sat down;
surrounded by all the hosts of disciples, he dwelt there as a sage.
As the Sūta was seated there, Śaunaka, the best of sages, with palms joined in reverence and full of humility, addressed him with these words: 9.
Śaunaka said:
O great sage Sūta, omniscient one, now that the Kali age has arrived, by what means, O Blessed One, may men possess abundant devotion? (10)
In the Kali age, all people will be devoted to sinful deeds and devoid of Vedic knowledge; how can there be any welfare for them? (11)
In the Kali age, living beings will have their vital breaths and light dependent on food; likewise, they will have short lifespans, be destitute, and be tormented by various sufferings.
O twice-born one, in the scriptures, meritorious deeds are prescribed as being accomplished through great effort;
therefore, in the Kali age, only a few people will perform such meritorious acts. (13)
When their good deeds have perished and evil karma has set in, all those of wicked intent will go to destruction. 14.
O best of men, O son of Sūta, tell us how great merit may be attained with very little effort, little wealth, and in a short time. (15)
It is certain in the scriptures that a mortal who, by his instruction, causes people to perform either merit or sin, shall partake in a portion of that [result]. (16)
One who gives instruction on merit, one who is compassionate, one who is free from deceit, and one who opposes the path of evil—these four are equal to Keśava. ||17||
To him who, having attained knowledge within this world, imparts it to others, Hari, whose very form is knowledge, looks with favor. (18)
A person who repeatedly gladdens others with the jewels of knowledge and the jewels of conduct is surely to be known as one of excellent intellect, a Hari bearing the form of a human being. (19)
O tiger among sages, you have thus mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas;
for there is indeed no other speaker besides you, since you have been instructed by Vyāsa. (20)
Sūta said:
You are blessed, O best of sages; you are indeed the foremost of Vaiṣṇavas, since you always desire the welfare of all the worlds. 21.
Listen, O Śaunaka, I shall speak that which you desire to hear, for the benefit of all the worlds, and especially for the Vaiṣṇavas. (22)
Listen to all that he said when questioned by Jaimini:
"The great seer named Jaimini was always devoted to the practice of yoga. (23)
Having bowed his head to Vyāsa, the best of sages, Jaimini asked:
"O Blessed One, knower of all dharmas, son of Satyavatī, Vyāsa! (24)
"In the Kali age, how can liberation occur? Tell me that from its very root.
The son said:
"Having heard Jaimini’s words, Vyāsa was delighted in his mind. (25)
O tiger among sages, we have begun this discourse endowed with auspiciousness.
Vyāsa said: O Jaimini, tiger among sages, you are blessed, O high-minded one! (26)
Since you always desire to hear the narrative of Nārāyaṇa, whoever’s intellect is inclined toward listening to such excellent stories [attains this]. (27)
For each of them, there shall arise knowledge; know that such knowledge bestows liberation.
But for the sinner on this earth who does not delight in the stories of Viṣṇu, [there is no such knowledge]. 28.
Having created it in vain according to the Creator's decree, the earth has been made heavy with burdens;
yet it is praised by Vaiṣṇava people as the "Jagatī" (the world) for the sake of narrating stories. 29.
O best of sages, he who says on that day, "The story of Hari is not heard," should be known as the foremost among sinners, speaking falsely. (30)
I consider that day to be a foul day, even if it is not a day of stormy clouds, on whichever part of the earth the story of Viṣṇu does not prevail. (31)
The Blessed One never abandons his presence there;
indeed, whatever man should become an obstacle at the commencement of the discourse on Viṣṇu, [he is cast into that treasury]. (32)
Having cursed him thus, the Blessed One departed along with the deities;
those people who, having heard of the power of Vāsudeva, rejoice [are likewise cursed]. ||33||
Those best of beings who,
having heard of the power of Nārāyaṇa, indeed mock it, should be known as gods of evil nature, unworthy of worship, and invisible.
O best of the twice-born, those who possess the knowledge of the three Vedas and take up their vows share in both heaven and hell;
all the sacred fords there, such as the Gaṅgā and others, [are likewise situated]. (35)
The celestial sages, the gods, and the ascetics whose wealth is penance [proclaim] this [teaching], which destroys the disease of sin for the multitudes of people who listen. (36)
Wherein the story of Nārāyaṇa occurs every day—a discourse on the essence of the sage’s yoga-practice, rich in meaning and destructive of sin. (37)
Listen to this account concerning Nārāyaṇa, together with its ancient history.
Thus ends the first chapter in the Śrī-Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the Kriyāyogasāra, within the dialogue between Jaimini and Vyāsa. ||1||
(2) Second Chapter. Vyāsa said:
In the beginning of creation, Mahāviṣṇu, desiring to create the entire universe, himself became the triad of forms—the creator, the protector, and the destroyer. (1)
For the sake of creating this world, the Supreme Person, having gone toward his own southern aspect, created by himself the one named Brahmā.
Then, O Sage, for the sake of protecting the world, the Lord of the World created from his own left side Viṣṇu, Keśava, who brings welfare to himself and others.
Then, for the sake of withdrawing the universe, the Lord, having made his abode in a lotus, emerged from the center of the sage’s body and emitted the imperishable Rudra.
Some say that the Puruṣa, whose nature consists of the three qualities—rajas, sattva, and tamas—is Brahmā; others say he is Viṣṇu; and some say he is Śaṅkara. ||5||
The one Viṣṇu, having become threefold, creates, consumes, and protects;
therefore, the best of men should not make distinctions among the three worlds.
This primordial nature belongs to that Mahāviṣṇu, the Supreme Self; it is celebrated as both ignorance and knowledge, the cause of the entire universe of beings.
The eternal cause of the universe, whose nature consists of both existence and non-existence,
suddenly manifested as the triple form of Brāhmī, Lakṣmī, and Ambikā.
O Sage, having thus appointed her to the tasks of creation, maintenance, and destruction,
the Primordial Being vanished there as if into her very self.
By whose command Brahmā then created the five great elements—
earth, ether, air, water, and fire— through meditative absorption.
Likewise, the lotus-seated one created Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, as well as Mahas, Jana, Tapaḥ, Satyam, and the others.
O twice-born one, Brahmā created Atala; below that, Vitala;
below that, Sutala; and below that, Cātālatala.
Below that is Mahātala; below that is Rasātala;
and below that is Pātāla—thus are the worlds in their proper order.
For the sake of providing a dwelling for the deities, he created the great mountain with jeweled peaks, resplendent with Jāmbūnada gold, in the midst of the earth.
He created Mandara, Carama, Trikūṭa, Udayācala,
and various other mountains as well.
Beyond that is Lokāloka, and in its midst, O best of Brahmins, are the seven oceans and the seven islands, created by the Supreme Lord Svayambhū himself.

O best of the twice-born, the continent of Jambūdvīpa is joined with the continent of Plakṣa; it should be known that the latter is double the size of the former, and Śālmaladvīpa is double the size of that.
The islands beginning with Tecaplakṣa are endowed with all portions;
they are possessed of every excellence and are the very forms of the gods and divine sages. 18.
These seven islands are surrounded by seven oceans;
I shall state their names—listen to the names of those oceans. (19)
O divine sage, these oceans— consisting of salt water, sugarcane juice, wine, clarified butter, curd, milk, and fresh water—
are each successively twice the size of the one preceding it.
All the Ālokāloka mountains are twice the size of the objects they surround.
In each successive continent, there are likewise trees, shrubs, creepers, and so forth.
O best of the twice-born, he created creatures belonging to the animal womb, as well as gods, humans, nāgas, and vidyādharas. (22)
In due order, he created sons, beginning with Dakṣa and other sages,
as well as the Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and other castes.
And Prajāpati assigned to them their respective duties, such as the turning [of the earth],
as well as the region south of the Golden Mountain (Hemādri) and likewise that north of the Vindhya mountain.
They call that the land of Bhārata, which bestows both auspicious and inauspicious fruits;
having attained birth in the land of Bhārata, O best of men, [one should strive for the highest goal].
Those who perform righteous deeds are all equal to Keśava;
for whatever action is performed in the land of karma, whether auspicious or inauspicious, [it bears fruit].
The world enjoys that fruit in the lands of enjoyment, O best of beings;
then, having arrived at the land of action, one becomes intent upon righteous deeds.
There is no one equal to him found in the three worlds;
his birth shall be fruitful, his life successful, and his existence truly lived.
He whose mind finds no interest in the service of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, despite the merits accumulated over ten million births, remains under the sole dominion of worldly existence. 29.
May men possess firm devotion toward Nārāyaṇa, the God of gods;
for he bestows all happiness, is praiseworthy, and is also fearless. (30)
That region should be abandoned immediately; one should not dwell where a Vaiṣṇava resides, whether the sin acquired in another birth be small or great.
At that very moment, it reaches destruction through the sight of a devotee of the Blessed One;
for the water from the feet of a Vaiṣṇava removes all sins.
What need has he for bathing in the Gaṅgā who would carry it on his head with devotion?
He who would maintain association with the devotees of the Lord (Bhāgavatas) even for a single moment [attains the highest goal]. 33.
O best of Brahmins, one is liberated from all sins, even those headed by the murder of a Brahmin, as well as from whatever ritual actions and religious duties are performed. 34.
In the presence of the devotees of the Blessed One, those [merits] become inexhaustible;
wherever Vaiṣṇavas remain for even a moment or half a moment, [there they are preserved].
Truth, truth, and again truth—that is the ultimate sacred ford, that is the penance grove;
whether it be food, water, or even a fruit, [it is offered] to a Vaiṣṇava. (36)
Whatever gift is given to any ascetic, O Brahmin, that gift becomes inexhaustible;
for a Vaiṣṇava is proclaimed to be the embodiment of all the deities. (37)
If all the deities are satisfied by this water-offering, they will be pleased even in this most terrible saṃsāra, which is filled with manifold sufferings. (38)
A person who is a devotee of the Blessed One never comes to grief;
therefore, O best of Brahmins, you too [should worship] Keśava through the yoga of ritual action. (39)
Having attained the supreme abode of Vraja-Viṣṇu through constant devotion to the Perfect One, Sūta said:
"Having heard these words of the high-souled son of a remarried woman (Kānīna)... (40)
Taking his joined palms to his head, Jaimini questioned him.
Jaimini said:
"O Blessed One, you have described the greatness of the devotees of the Lord again and again. (41)
O Guru, tell me all that at once: what are their characteristics?
And how, O best of sages, are the Vaiṣṇavas to be recognized in this world? (42)
"If you have favor toward me, tell all of that from the beginning.
Vyāsa said:
"Formerly, when Madhu and Kaiṭabha had been slain by the Creator himself,"
When asked, the Blessed One said: "Listen to that which I know:
at the end of the kalpa, in the form of Rudra, I shall withdraw the entire universe."
The Blessed One himself alone caused [all beings] to sleep by means of his yogic power (yogamāyā).
While that Blessed One was thus asleep, deluded by his yogic sleep (yoganidrā), the entire earth became submerged in a flood of water. 45.
Having meditated upon that Primordial Person (Ādipurusha) seated upon the lotus from Brahmā’s navel—the creator of the universe—he praised him with his mind fixed upon him. 46.
O twice-born one, at that most terrible time, two formidable great asuras named Madhu and Kaiṭabha were born from the ear-wax of Viṣṇu.
Wandering through the intermediate space, those two extremely fierce sons of Tvaṣṭṛ beheld Brahmā in the lotus of Śrī Viṣṇu’s navel.
O Brahmin, with their eyes bloodshot from anger, that Haṃtumatha and Daityauta, possessed of great strength and prowess, exerted themselves.
Then Brahmā, the creator of the world, reflecting in his heart upon the inconceivable means of slaying him,
praised the divine Yoganidrā with gentle words.
Having heard that hymn of praise from Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, he spoke these words with affection: "Tell me, what is desired by you? Let it be spoken. (51)
Brahmā said:
"These two exceedingly fierce Dānavas have resolved to kill me;
delude them quickly with your Māyā and abandon Acyuta as your protector. (52)
Then the divine sleep (Nidrā) abandoned that Great Viṣṇu;
thereafter, out of compassion for those two Dānavas, [he remained] in the intermediate space.
Compassionate toward those who seek refuge, he fought with hand-to-hand combat; having waged a most terrible battle for five thousand years, [he remained].
No one there attained victory, nor did anyone suffer defeat;
meanwhile, those two sons of Diti were utterly deluded by Mahāmāyā.
"Choose a boon from us," they both said to Keśava;
then, O twice-born one, the two lords of the gods laughed and spoke these words.
When those two Daityas, who were difficult to slay, became quickly satisfied,
then those two terrible Dānavas [attacked] that Lord Janārdana.
Thus spoke the two great illusionists, deluded by the Great Illusion: "This very boon has been granted to you; there is no doubt in this matter. (58)
"O Janārdana, let us slay them where there is no water on the earth;
therefore, O great Asura, bring them toward me. (59)
Seeing the two Dānavas, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, slain by the wielder of the discus with the edge of his wonderful discus,
Brahmā, his fear dispelled, praised the Lord of the gods.
Brahmā said: Salutations again and again to you, the Supreme Lord, the destroyer of all the afflictions of those who have sought refuge;
salutations again and again to you, Nārāyaṇa, whose nature consists of the three *guṇas* and whose prowess is immeasurable. (61)
People who have taken refuge at the pair of your lotus feet never encounter misfortune anywhere;
this I have known from Anantakīrti, for whom this great calamity has been instantly removed. (62)
O Lord of Yoga, you are the wielder of the sword and other weapons; you are the sovereignty over the three worlds, O God of gods, protector of those who have come for refuge!
You are merciless in the destruction of the multitude of enemies, since these two asuras, whom I was protecting, have been slain by you.

Although Madhu and Kaiṭabha were considered exceedingly cruel, nevertheless, with a heart desiring the welfare of your own kin, you, the Lord who bestows all auspiciousness, were satisfied by them through the granting of boons that resulted in the destruction of their own lives. 64.
This entire triple world becomes delightful for that man, and all his enemies, together with their own kinsmen, perish;
meanwhile, all his friends and relatives attain prosperity—this you behold here through the mercies of the Lord of the Immortals. (65)
O bee at the lotus-face of Lakṣmī, O God of gods, O destroyer of the fear and sorrow of the world;
protect me, who have taken refuge in Your two beautiful lotus-feet, by Your grace, O Lord—salutations to You forever! (66)
Be gracious, O lotus-eyed one; be gracious, O Lord of the Lotus;
be gracious, O Lord of all beings! Salutations to You who sustain the universe.
Salutations to you, who are pleased by devotion; salutations to you, the bestower of devotion;
salutations to you, whose nature is knowledge; O sinless one, may you be my refuge. 68.
Homage to you, homage to you, homage to you; homage, homage!
Protect me, protect me, protect me, O You who pervade the universe! 69.
Vyāsa said:
Praised with these and other hymns by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, the Blessed Lord attained supreme delight.
The Blessed Lord said:
"O Lotus-seated One, I am pleased with this hymn of yours and with your devotion.
Tell me what you desire; I shall grant it to you on this earth. (71)
Brahmā said:
"O Lord of Gods, O Ocean of Compassion, O Pervader of the Universe, if you are pleased with me, then let this be my boon: that no calamities shall ever befall your devotees. (72)
The Blessed Lord said:
"So be it, O best of gods; this boon has been granted by me.
May my devotee never encounter any calamity whatsoever upon the surface of the earth."
I dwell constantly within the bodies of Vaiṣṇavas;
therefore, calamities never befall those men who are devotees of Viṣṇu. (74)
Brahmā said:
"O Lord of the World, everything has indeed been granted by you, there is no doubt;
for even these two great Daityas have been struck down in battle. (75)
O Lord, for however long he may approach you and praise you with this hymn with supreme devotion, you shall become his protector. (76)
Aha! You cannot indeed be meditated upon even by the gods through their meditations;
that you wander within the bodies of the devotees of Viṣṇu is a great marvel. (77)
O Master, if you were pleased for even a single moment, what could not be achieved?
That you wander in the company of Vaiṣṇavas is a great wonder indeed. (78)
O Slayer of Kaiṭabha, who indeed are the Vaiṣṇavas, and what is their characteristic? How are they all to be recognized? Tell me that, O Keśava. (79)
The Blessed Lord said:
O best of beings, I am not able to describe the characteristics of Vaiṣṇavas even in hundreds of millions of kalpas; listen to them in brief. 80.
Saṃsāra is indeed under the control of Vaiṣṇavas; the gods are protected by Vaiṣṇavas;
and I too am under the control of Vaiṣṇavas; therefore, Vaiṣṇavas are the most excellent. ||81||
O Brahmin, I do not remain anywhere else even for a single moment apart from a Vaiṣṇava; Vaiṣṇavas are my kinsmen. ||82||
Those who are free from lust and anger, devoid of violence and hypocrisy, and bereft of greed and delusion—these indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. ||83||
Those who are free from envy and endowed with compassion, who desire the welfare of all beings, and who speak only truthful words—they indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. ||84||
Those who provide instruction in the Dharma, those who uphold the practice of the Dharma, and those who serve their gurus—these indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. ||85||
Those who perceive you and me, Maheśvara, as equal, and offer worship to a guest—they indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. ||86||
Those who are learned in the Vedas and etymology, who are always devoted to the Brahmins, and who are like eunuchs toward the wives of others—those indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. ||87||
Those who observe the Ekādaśī vow with a spirit of devotion and sing my names—those people indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. ||88||
Those who build temples for the gods, who wear garlands of *tulasī*, and who carry *padmākṣa* beads—those people indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. ||89||
O Brahmin, those whose bodies are marked with my weapons—the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus—should indeed be known as Vaiṣṇava people. (90)
O Lotus-seated One, those whose necks wear garlands of dhātrī fruits and who worship me with its leaves—those people should indeed be known as Vaiṣṇavas. (91)
Those who apply sectarian marks with the soil from the root of the tulasī plant, as well as those who do so with the powder of tulasī wood, should indeed be known as Vaiṣṇava people. 92.
Those who delight in bathing in the Gaṅgā, those who are devoted to the name of the Gaṅgā, and those who proclaim the majesty of the Gaṅgā—these indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. ||93||
Those in whose house a Śālagrāma stone always resides, as well as the Bhāgavata scripture, should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. 94.
O best of beings, those who daily cleanse my shrines and offer lamps there—those people indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. 95.
Those who restore my dilapidated temple to its former state and enhance the beauty of that sanctuary should indeed be known as Vaiṣṇava people. ||96||
O Four-faced One, those who grant fearlessness to the frightened and bestow the gift of knowledge upon Brahmins—those people indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. ||97||
Those whose heads have been sprinkled with the water from my feet and who eat my food offerings—those indeed are to be known as Vaiṣṇava people. 98.
Those who give food and water to those afflicted by hunger and thirst, and those who perform service with devotion—those indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. (99)
Those who establish groves, those who plant pipala trees, and those who perform service for cows—these indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. ||100||
O Brahman, those who perform the sacrifice to the ancestors with ultimate devotion, and who practice service to the distressed—they are indeed to be known as Vaiṣṇava people. 101.
Those who construct ponds and villages, those who delight in the gift of a maiden, and those who serve their mothers-in-law and fathers-in-law—these indeed are to be known as Vaiṣṇava people. ||102||
Those who do not treat their elder sister or elder brother as another's wife or husband should be known as Vaiṣṇava people. (103)
In Vaiṣṇavas, all virtues are present and not even a trace of a fault exists;
therefore, O Saṃpāti, become a Vaiṣṇava and attain the state of the four-faced Brahmā.
O Lord of Creatures, by constantly propitiating me through the yoga of ritual action, everything auspicious shall swiftly come to pass for you; of this there is no doubt. (105)
O Four-faced One, those who view the property of the gods, the wealth of Brahmins, and the possessions of others as being like poison—they indeed are to be known as Vaiṣṇava people. (106)
Those people who are devoid of devotion to heretics, are solely devoted to Śiva, and are intent upon the vow of the fourteenth day (Caturdaśī)—they indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. 107.
What is the use of saying more here again and again?
Those who perform my worship are indeed to be known as Vaiṣṇavas. (108)
"Let the entire world be created once more, as if it had remained in its former state.
Having spoken thus, the Supreme Lord vanished right there. 109.
Then, as before, Brahmā created the entire universe;
and having worshipped Hari through the yoga of action (kriyā-yoga), he went to the supreme abode.
Those who recite this while meditating upon me with devotion in the presence of Nārāyaṇa, being completely liberated from all sins, go at the end to the abode of Hari. (111)
Thus ends the second chapter in the Śrī-Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the Kriyā-yoga-sāra. ||2||
(3) The Third Chapter. Jaimini said:
O Vyāsa of great intelligence, tell me the true nature of *kriyā-yoga*;
I desire to learn about *kriyā-yoga* from you. (1)
Vyāsa said:
O Brahmin, a human body is difficult to obtain here on this earth;
having attained such a body, a wise man should practice yoga for the sake of liberation.
Both *kriyā-yoga* and *dhyāna-yoga* are proclaimed as forms of yoga;
of these two, the first, *kriyā-yoga*, grants all desires to those who practice it. (3)
O best of the twice-born, [I have heard of] the glory of the Gaṅgā, the worship of Viṣṇu, gifts, devotion to Brāhmaṇas, and likewise devotion to the vow of Ekādaśī. (4)
