Then, along with the king, he was gratified by Viṣṇu, who is exceedingly patient, with various kinds of divine foods that are very difficult even for the gods to obtain.
Thus the king remained every day at the temple of Viṣṇu for thousands of Manvantaras and nine hundred years.
Devoted to righteousness, that king protected his subjects;
Hari constantly honored him with supreme devotion. (71)
With beautiful campaka flowers and various kinds of food offerings,
that king, when his life was nearly spent, met his death in the waters of the Ganges.
Having attained liberation through the grace of the wielder of the discus (Viṣṇu), Vyāsa said:
"This power of the flower of the *vipracampaka* has thus been proclaimed. (73)
By worshipping Hari with what [materials] would sinful people be liberated?
The Blessed Lord Hari was worshipped with a *caṃpakapuṣpa* flower. (74)
O brahmin-sage, those who worship the Supreme Self— whether with desire or without desire— attain the supreme state before long.
They too, liberated from all sins, go to the supreme abode. ||76||

For when Hari is propitiated, no one suffers from evil; thus, even that king, though he had committed a sin, attained liberation through the grace of Murāri by crossing over this deep ocean of worldly existence.
The mortal who worships Nārāyaṇa—with eyes as broad as lotus petals—with divine, fragrant golden flowers, with devotion and supreme reverence, shall go there, having cast off all sin. (78)
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Campaka Flower," in the Kriyā-yoga-sāra of the glorious Padma Purāṇa.
— o)0(o— (11) The Eleventh Chapter.
Vyāsa said:
O Jaimini, I shall describe that method by which Hari is always to be worshipped; listen with a concentrated mind, O child, O brahmin-sage. (1)
Having risen at dawn and taken his bowl from the bed,
the wise man should go outside, covering his head with a cloth.
There, having placed the *maunīya* and *yajñasūtra* on his ears and facing the northern direction, the wise man should sit and discharge feces and urine. (3)
In a temple, on a path, in cow-pens, and in dust-heaps;
on a carriage road, in ploughed land, at the root of *darbha* grass, and likewise in a courtyard. (4)
One should not discharge feces or urine on the sandy banks of a river, at the foot of a sacred tree, in a forest, or within the depths of a pond or a large reservoir. ||5||
As long as a wise man has not discharged his excrement and urine, he does not look at the sun, the moon, the twice-born, cows, or the ten directions.
One should not take earth for the purpose of purification that has been dug up by mice and other creatures dwelling within their burrows, nor earth that has been turned over by a plow. (7)
A wise person, having brought water from water, should perform purification;
the learned one does not perform purification by merely placing his foot in the waters. ||8||
A wise man should perform his external purification at night facing south;
having covered his head with a cloth, he should then carry out the rite of cleansing.
The wise should apply one application of clay to the forehead,
three to the anus, seven to the left hand, and ten to both hands.
Having performed the rites of purification with clay and cow-dung from a six-foot distance for his feet, the wise man should perform the cleansing of his teeth.
One should perform the cleansing of the tongue with the teeth-cleanser and other such means,
while facing either southward or westward.
O twice-born one, one should perform the cleansing of the teeth while making a sound; if one does not do so, one will become a denizen of hell.
One should use the middle and ring fingers along with the thumb.
A wise person should perform the cleansing of that [toothbrush] with the bark of the Aśvattha, Vaṭa, Dhātrī, or Kaithika trees, but never with the forefinger. 14.
If one performs the rinsing of the mouth while making a noise, as was done by Indra against the Asura, all the fruit of his daily rites will surely perish. (15)
If one should perform the cleaning of teeth at the time of bathing, his ancestors, the gods, and the celestial sages depart disappointed. (16)
If one should perform that rinsing (of the mouth) at midday or in the afternoon, the deities do not accept his worship, nor do the ancestors accept his water-offering. ||17||
He who cleanses his teeth in a lotus pond at the time of bathing should be known as a Cāṇḍāla until he beholds the Gaṅgā. (18)
If one should perform the cleaning of the teeth when the sun has risen upon the Blessed One, the ancestors, having consumed that tooth-stick, depart in sorrow. (19)
On the day of fasting, as well as on the day of the ancestral Śrāddha rite for Brahmins, a man who brushes his teeth does not obtain the fruit of those acts. (20)
At dawn, the wise man should cleanse his teeth with a cloth and likewise his waistband;
he should perform the twelve "surges" (kallola) for the lords of brahmins with water.
O Jaimini, by performing the brushing of teeth according to this procedure during the ancestral Śrāddha fast, a mortal obtains the full fruit [of the rite]. (22)
Having performed the external rites according to this procedure, the far-sighted one should then go to his own home and discard the night-garment.
Then, having sat down at the door of the temple, the pure Budha should remember the god Nārāyaṇa, the infinite Supreme Lord.
O Rāma, O Viṣṇu of dark-complexioned body, O Nārāyaṇa who consists of compassion, O Janārdana, O abode of the world, O Hari, O Keśava, take away my sin. 25.
O yellow-robed one, wearer of the sacred thread, whose navel is a blazing lotus and who pervades the universe;
O Lord, O All-pervading One, you who are the refuge of the humble Vāmana, be my protection! 26.
O Dāmodara, best of the Yadus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, ocean of compassion! O lotus-eyed one, Indra of gods, Vāsudeva, grant me your grace! 27.
O Garuḍadhvaja, Govinda, Viśvambhara, Gadādhara!
O Śaṅkhapāṇi, Cakrapāṇi, Padmahasta, remove our calamities. (28)
O Lakṣmīvilāsa, Vaikuṇṭha, Hṛṣīkeśa, best of gods! O Puruṣottama, Kaṃsāri, Kaiṭabhāri, dispel my fear! 29.
O Lord of Śrī, O Sovereign who upholds Śrī, O Mādhava who bestows the fortune of Śrī;
O Supreme Brahman, O Supreme Abode, O Imperishable One, be my refuge. 30.
Having done this, O best of the twice-born, the wise man, remembering Śrī Viṣṇu, says "Jalir baddhā" (the salutation is bound) and, entering his abode, departs. ||31||
O Lord, Śrīpati, Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Devakī and Nanda; O Lord of the World, abandon sleep, for the time of dawn has arrived. (32)
Then the wise man, having abandoned sleep, should contemplate with his own mind the son of Devakī, who is endowed with Lakṣmī, as if he had just arisen from his couch. 33.
Then, for the purpose of washing his face, the Vaiṣṇava should indeed offer to Kṛṣṇa a divine vessel filled with water and provided with a lid. (34)
Just as servants serve a lord for the sake of their livelihood, even so do the wise serve the Supreme Lord. (35)
But he who serves the Lord of the World in the form of a servant, O brahmin sage, his heart's desire is fulfilled without delay. (36)
Just as servants perform service with fear in the presence of a lord, so too do the wise always serve Hari, the Lord. 37.
If a man, out of his own desire, worships Viṣṇu through this [image], he is indeed a bad servant; O twice-born one, he shall certainly not attain fearlessness at that time.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, a man who desires liberation must always perform service to the Lord of Kamalā with all haste. (39)
A Vaiṣṇava devotee should remove from the body of Hari the floral offerings, the night-garment, the scent, and likewise anything stale at dawn.
Then, in that temple, the wise man himself should personally sweep it;
he should perform the clearing away of dust very slowly with a broom.
As many particles of dust as go out from that abode,
for so many hundreds of manvantaras shall a person remain in the house of Viṣṇu.
But even a killer of a Brahmin who performs the sweeping in the house of Hari goes to the supreme abode; what is the use of further words? (43)
Likewise, O twice-born one, the wise man should perform the smearing with woolly cow-dung;
in that temple of Viṣṇu, he should remember the Lord Nārāyaṇa. 44.
O Jaimini, listen as I briefly describe the merit of one who performs the smearing of the temple of Keśava with plaster. ||45||
O best of the twice-born, for as many particles of dust as perish there,
for that many thousands of kalpas shall one dwell happily in the abode of Viṣṇu.
O Lord, what person who knows the fruit of the worship of the Master does not obtain the supreme abode after performing the sweeping and the smearing of the ground in the temple of Viṣṇu? 47.
When he himself is unable [to act] due to opposition from the king of the gods, then he should also appoint his lawful wife in the house of Viṣṇu. 48.
Alternatively, one should employ in the temple of the deity one's own son who is devoted and of good conduct, or likewise one's brother or sister.
One should personally and with great effort wash the articles for the worship of Hari seven times, or at least three times, with pure water.
Copper vessels are purified by acid, vessels made of bell-metal by ash, and iron vessels by fire; of this there is no doubt.
Keśava is pleased with that wealthy person who bathes Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the World, with waters contained in vessels of iron. ||52||
If it is argued that one is purified by bathing in the Ganges even through ignorance,
then, O best of Brahmins, a religious observance must always be performed when prosperity is attained.
"There is no fixed rule regarding failure in the scriptures; such is the certainty.
When a conch shell, though washed with effort, touches the ground again," (54)
Then, O best of Brahmins, together with his conch, he becomes pure after being washed a hundred times;
thus, having diligently cleansed the ritual materials of the Wielder of the Discus.
Having taken the articles for bathing, one should go to a lake for the purpose of bathing;
however, he who returns home again without having performed the act of bathing [is at fault]. (56)
On that day, the host of his ancestors does not receive the libation;
it creates an obstacle for him as he goes for the purpose of bathing or eating. 57.
But he who, O best of the twice-born, out of delusion goes to a lake for the purpose of bathing and voids his excrement there, will surely become a denizen of hell. (58)
The ancestors of that person who eats excrement and urine shall undoubtedly become consumers of such things themselves;
therefore, one should perform the ritual bathing, the libations (tarpaṇa), and other rites according to the prescribed rules.
Upon arriving at his own home, the wise man should remember Nārāyaṇa;
then, in the early morning, he should wash both his feet before a brāhmaṇa.
A most excellent Brahmin, being pure, should enter the temple;
yet that person who enters the sanctuary with unwashed feet [is at fault]. (61)
The merit accumulated over a year perishes for him at that very instant;
having performed his ablutions and returned, the wise man should enter among the hosts of attendants.
Therefore, having washed his feet, he should enter the temple of the deity;
having sat down, the wise man [should wash] his pair of feet with his left hand.
O Brahmin, one should then diligently wash both hands; O best of Brahmins, likewise wash one foot with the other foot, and likewise with the right hand.
Lakṣmī certainly abandons that fool who washes [the image];
therefore, once seated, the wise man should begin the worship of Keśava. (65)
Having become single-minded, [one should worship] that which bestows the fruit of all desires,
seated upon a deer-skin or even a pure tiger-skin seat.
Seated upon a cloth seat, a bare seat, or likewise a seat made of kuśa grass,
or upon a seat of flowers, one should worship the Lord of Kamalā.
A learned Brahmin should not perform the worship of Viṣṇu on a wooden seat;
for by Viṣṇu the earth was upheld, and by you all the worlds are upheld. (68)
"Therefore, this place is the supreme abode for me, the refuge of all embodied beings.
Having spoken thus, the worshiper of Nārāyaṇa should spread out a seat and sit down. (69)
Facing south, one should perform the worship of Viṣṇu;
having placed water, purified by mantra and well-scented, into a conch shell. (70)
One should bathe the Lord, the beloved of Kamalā, together with Kamalā;
indeed, he who bathes that Blessed One Janārdana with a conch shell [attains great merit].
I shall declare its fruit; listen, O Jaimini, best of Brahmins! [It purifies one] from the sins of killing a Brahmin, a cow, a woman, or an embryo, from drinking liquor, and other such crimes. (72)
Liberated, he goes to Vaikuṇṭha and enjoys every happiness;
O twice-born one, a human being who, having seen Hṛṣīkeśa, worships him [attains this]. (73)
O best of Brahmins, through the grace of the Lord of Kamalā, the wise man quickly attains that very state; however, in the absence of a conch, he should use fragrant water. 74.
Having placed the incomparable tulasī in a vessel, the wise one should bathe Keśava;
then, having bathed the Lord and established him upon an excellent seat.
One should perform a complete anointing of his body with fragrant sandalwood pastes, and protect the body of the Discus-bearer with pieces of Tulasī wood. (76)
Hari is always pleased with that person who makes this garland of tulasī leaves, which bestows the pleasure of its own fragrance.
O best of Brahmins, by this mantra and with a garland of tulasī leaves, the Lord of the World is offered [this gift]; may He be well-pleased at all times. (78)
Once Mahāviṣṇu has been adorned and is pleased, why does he not grant [the desired fruit]?
Therefore, the recitation of the Svasti-mantras should be performed with Vedic hymns. (79)
The wise should perform the binding of the directions with Vedic mantras:
"May Kṛṣṇa protect in the east; may the son of Devakī protect in the southeast. (80)
May the enemy of the Daityas protect [the temple] in the south, and Madhusūdana in the southwest;
may the illustrious one protect the intermediate directions, and the Lord Śrīdhara protect the zenith. ||81||
May the Soul of All, the embodiment of compassion in the form of the Tortoise, protect [us] from below;
for all those who act as obstacles indeed arise at the time of worship. (82)
"Go far away, all of you, struck by the weapon of Hari's name!
Having thus performed the binding of the directions, he then bowed down with palms joined in reverence.
With the mantra that is about to be recited, he performs the firm consecration:
"O Janārdana, God of gods, may this worship undertaken by me [be accepted]. (84)
"O Supreme Lord, be gracious so that I may attain unimpeded success.
Then, having made this resolve, the devotee of Viṣṇu, who knew all principles, [proceeded]. (85)
Having performed the placement of syllables (gaṇanyāsa) and other rites, one should meditate upon Nārāyaṇa within the heart—resembling a fresh cloud, with eyes like the white lotus. (86)
The god, wearing yellow garments, with a face most beautiful with a smile, adorned with garlands of kadamba flowers, and possessing very long arms. ||87||
With his crest tied with a row of peacock feathers like sacrificial grass, he enchanted the ten directions with the sweet sound of his flute. 88.
Thus one should meditate upon Govinda, the Lord of Gods and granter of all desires, who stands in the forest of Vṛndāvana surrounded by the beautiful cowherd women. 89.
Then the Vaiṣṇava should perform the invocation with a spirit of devotion for Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of the four aims of human life, who has been invoked. 90.
There, the wise and discerning person should offer water for the feet, the respectful oblation (arghya), and water for sipping (ācamanīya), using tender tulasī leaves or fresh flowers. 91.
One should worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, the Lord of all gods. Homage, repeated homage, to Matsya, to Kūrma, and to Varāha! ||92||
Homage be to you, Hari; salutations again and again to Vāmana.
Homage to Rāma, to Rāma, to Rāma, and homage to the Mighty One.
Homage to the Buddha, the pure one, who is endowed with compassion; homage, repeated homage! Homage be to you, Kalkin; homage to you of manifold forms! ||94||
Salutation to you, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Govinda, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, Dāmodara, the God, the God of gods. ||95||
Salutations indeed to Hṛṣīkeśa, the peaceful one, whose feet are the sky;
let there be salutation to the Lord of Padmā, salutations to You, the lotus-eyed one. ||96||
Salutation to you, the infinite; salutation indeed to you who hold the mace in hand. Salutation to you whose banner is Tārkṣya; salutation to you who bear the discus in your palm. ||97||
Salutations again and again to you, the lotus-handed Acyuta;
salutations to you, the enemy of the Daityas, the bestower of all desires. ||98||
Salutations ever be to Mādhava, the Lord of gods, Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self, the one adorned with a crown and earrings—to Hari! 99.
Homage to you, O Blessed One; the wise one [should invoke] the vehicle called Garuḍa with the mantra: "Oṃ, homage to Garuḍa. (100)
Salutations to the conch, to the discus, and repeated salutations to the mace;
salutations to the lotus, to the sword, and repeated salutations to Nandaka. ||101||
Having thus worshipped the Lord of Gods, together with his consort, his vehicle,
and his weapons, the wise man should then mutter the eight-syllabled mantra.
Then, having chanted the eight-syllabled mantra with his own devotion, the wise one should offer various excellent food-offerings (naivedya) to Govinda. (103)
A devotee of Viṣṇu should offer incense, lamps, betel, and other various offerings to Viṣṇu, the God of gods. (104)
O best of the twice-born, for him who offers incense scented with sandalwood and agallochum to the Enemy of Mura, his desired object is swiftly accomplished. (105)
The brahmin who offers incense scented with ghee to Hari shall go to the abode of Viṣṇu, liberated from tens of millions of sins.
One should offer incense scented with guggulu to Nārāyaṇa;
he goes to that supreme abode which is difficult even for the gods to attain. 107.
O Keśava, he who offers a lamp with ghee or again with sesame oil—Keśava removes all of that person's sin in the blink of an eye. 108.
O Jaimini, best of the twice-born, for him who offers betel leaf scented with camphor to the wielder of the discus (Cakrapāṇi), liberation is attained. 109.
But he who offers betel leaf accompanied by khadira wood, having enjoyed all pleasures here in this world, goes in the end to the abode of Hari. 110.
By offering betel leaf prepared with ṣaṣṭhīmadhurikā as well as nutmeg and other spices to Hari, a person attains heaven. ||111||
O Jaimini, a Vaiṣṇava person, having taken water in a conch shell, should perform the circumambulation of Viṣṇu with the mantra that is about to be recited. 112.
O Janārdana, friend of the world, protector of those who seek refuge! O Lord, grant to me, your servant, the status of being the servant of the servant of your servants. 113.
O Jaimini, listen as I briefly describe the fruit of the merit for one who performs the circumambulation of Nārāyaṇa with this mantra. 114.
Whatever great sins there may be, such as the killing of a Brahmin and others,
they all perish at every step of the circumambulation.
For as many steps as a man shall go with devotion in circumambulating Viṣṇu,
for that many thousands of kalpas he rejoices together with Viṣṇu.
As long as a person proceeds very slowly during the circumambulation of Hari, that human being obtains the fruit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice at every step. ||117||
Whatever fruit may arise from circumambulating everything within the entire cycle of existence, the fruit from circumambulating Hari is ten million times greater than that. (118)
Whoever circumambulates [the site] starting from "Aṃ Gaṃ" in front of Nārāyaṇa obtains that very same fruit; what is the use of further words? (119)
The wise one should protect the Soma-thread during the circumambulation of the earth;
for if that thread is not protected, the worship performed by the Brahmin becomes fruitless. (120)
O best of Brahmins, he who approaches Hari while performing a single circumambulation will certainly become a sovereign emperor in birth after birth. (121)
But he who performs the circumambulation of Viṣṇu twice shall attain the supreme state within three days; of this there is no doubt. ||122||
The person who performs the circumambulation of Viṣṇu twice shall be liberated from all sins and enter the body of Mādhava. (123)
O Jaimini, one should circulate the conch filled with water over Keśava;
having gone to that temple, he shall be honored by the gods. ||124||
Whoever prostrates like a staff upon the ground seven times before Keśava, the sin residing within his body is reduced to ashes at that very moment. (125)
Placing his joined palms upon his head, one should bow down to Yojanārdana;
to him, Viṣṇu, the Lord of Lakṣmī, grants the supreme abode. (126)
O brahmin-sage, listen attentively as I describe the power of the merit of those men who, having cast all their sins upon the earth, bow down to Hari. 127.
For as many particles of dust as there are in the body of men that has been thus adorned,
for that many thousands of kalpas do they remain in the presence of Hari.
Thereafter, the remains of the offerings (nirmālya) from Keśava are bestowed upon the Vaiṣṇavas.
O Jaimini, best of men, listen as I describe those Vaiṣṇavas to you. 129.
Śuka, Sūta, as well as Vyāsa, Nārada, the sage Kapila, Prahlāda, Ambarīṣa, and likewise Krūra and Uddhava. 130.
Bibhīṣaṇa, Hanumān, and likewise other Vaiṣṇavas accept the remains of offerings (nirmālya) of Vāsudeva, which grants all desires.
Having spoken thus, the Vaiṣṇava should place the remains of Viṣṇu's offerings upon the ground;
thereafter, he himself receives the remains of Hari's offerings with devotion. (132)
O best of the twice-born, he on whose head is seen the excellent offering made to Hari should be known as Hari himself in person. (133)
The food offerings to Viṣṇu and his floral remains are difficult to obtain and destroy all sins; even the gods accept them all, so what need is there to mention human beings? (134)
Whatever Vaiṣṇava indeed smells a Tulasī leaf from Jaimini, all the sin residing within his body is destroyed. ||135||
If the dust from a Tulasī leaf enters anyone's nostrils, the calamities residing within that person's body immediately go to their destruction. (136)
O best of the twice-born, he who smells the fragrance of the Tulasī leaves and offers praise, in his home there shall always be prosperity. (137)
Having praised Acyuta, the Lord of the World and beloved of Kamalā, with hymns of praise, one should then join the palms in reverence and recite this mantra: 138.
O Nārāyaṇa, whose form is the world, O Lord of the universe, go to Your own divine abode; be forever gracious. (139)
O Lord of the World, O you who pervade the universe, may this worship of yours performed by me according to my own ability be rendered flawless through your grace. 140.
Then, with a spirit of devotion, one should receive the water from the feet of the wise Mahāviṣṇu, the Supreme Self, which destroys all sins. (141)
O Jaimini, it is said as a truth that he who carries even a mere drop of the auspicious water from Viṣṇu’s feet has effectively bathed in all sacred fords.
One should touch the water from the feet of Viṣṇu; it yields the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, because the cow, song, water, the Brahmin, and the water from Viṣṇu’s feet are all one and the same.
There is no untimely death, nor is there any fear of disease, for one who touches the water from the feet of the great-souled Keśava. (144)
For the sake of destroying the disease of sin, [drink] the medicine of the water from Viṣṇu’s feet;
even those who are sinful men should drink it every single day. 145.
If a Vaiṣṇava person drinks the water from the feet of Viṣṇu offered by a brāhmaṇa, the sin residing within his body perishes in an instant. (146)
Just as a medicinal herb residing within the body completely destroys the ailments of the embodied being,
even so does the water from Viṣṇu’s feet destroy every sin.
O Brahmin, I shall describe the merit of that person who carries upon his head the pure water from Viṣṇu’s feet, combined with a tulasī leaf. 148.
Freed from sins such as the killing of a Brahmin and assuming the form of Viṣṇu, he goes to the city of Viṣṇu and rejoices together with Viṣṇu. (149)
Whatever fruit is obtained by giving gold equal in size to Mount Meru, a greater fruit than that is obtained by touching the water from Viṣṇu’s feet. (150)
That fruit which people obtain by the gift of ten million horses, and the fruit one would obtain by giving the earth with its seven continents to the twice-born; [that fruit is attained here]. (151)
A mortal who touches the water from Viṣṇu’s feet obtains that fruit which results from performing thousands of horse-sacrifices. 152.
By touching the water from Viṣṇu’s feet, one obtains a fruit even greater than that merit which is proclaimed to result from the gift of a hundred large ponds. (153)
Therefore, one who touches even the water from his feet would obtain merit even greater than that;
what need is there for much speaking here? I shall state it in brief.
O best of Brahmins, by the touch of the water from Viṣṇu’s feet, a human being becomes liberated;
this is told by me again and again with great firmness. (155)
Furthermore, he who touches the water from the feet of Hari and partakes of the remnants of Viṣṇu’s food offering—which destroys all sins—does not undergo birth again. (156)
O best of the twice-born, he who eats with a spirit of devotion shall go to the supreme state; for one who partakes of the food offered to Viṣṇu is exceedingly rare.
Even sins such as the killing of a Brahmin abandon the body of one who eats the food offered to Hari; she becomes like a maidservant, remaining under his control. ||158||
The ground of liberation is difficult to attain even for the gods, the best of deities;
yet, having fully worshipped the Beloved of Kamalā, he did not leave behind even a small portion of the food offering.
In no time at all, Viṣṇu leads him back to his own body;
what more can I say regarding the qualities of this Great Viṣṇu? 160.
O Lord of the twice-born, by this method, Keśava himself becomes dependent upon you every month; thus, O Brahmin, [one should worship] Janārdana.
Even if it is deficient in ritual procedure, he who performs the excellent worship of the Lord of Śrī-Kamalā with a spirit of devotion shall also become dear to Keśava. (162)
O Brahmin, whatever fruit one who knows the ritual obtains by worshipping Viṣṇu according to the prescribed rite, that same fruit is obtained,
O Lord, through many offerings presented according to the stated injunctions.
Even when worshipped, he would not be satisfied if devotion does not remain;
for whatever the extent of one's devotion toward Janārdana, the God of gods— ||164||
To that very extent is the attainment of fruit for him; there is no doubt in this matter.
Yet, on this earth, worship of Hari is performed by men without devotion. (165)
That worship indeed occurs at the time of the worship of the best of Brahmins;
for devotion to Hari is the root of knowledge, and [devotion] to the Lord of the Universe is the root of devotion. (166)
In the growth of the tree of worship that leads to liberation, the root is the propitiation of Hari;
for even a very small amount, when performed by a wise person with faith, indeed bears fruit.
All ritual actions performed with complete faith become inexhaustible.
O twice-born one, he who worships Viṣṇu with devotion, even if it be only with water, [attains this]. (168)
He attains the form of Viṣṇu, since Hari is subject to the power of his devotees. ||169||
O Brahmin, this entire world is devoid of essence; the only essence is the worship of Hari.
Therefore, a person who desires his own welfare [should practice it].
One should worship Kṛṣṇa, whose form is infinite, with devotion. ||170||
Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Procedure for the Worship of Hari," in the *Kriyā-yoga-sāra* of the glorious *Padma Purāṇa*.
(12) The Twelfth Chapter.
Vyāsa said:
In the month of Phālguna, O best of brāhmaṇas, a Vaiṣṇava person should worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is adored by the gods, every single day with a spirit of devotion. (1)
I shall declare the fruit for him who bathes the Son of Devakī with clarified butter during the month of Phālguna; listen now to it correctly from me. (2)
Having obtained the fruit of all sacrifices as well as the fruit of all gifts, he, freed from all sins, reaches the abode of Hari which removes all distress. (3)
Having enjoyed pleasures in the abode of Hari for thousands of millions of yugas,
one attains liberation there upon reaching supreme knowledge.
But he who offers a divine sweetmeat of sesame seeds to Kṛṣṇa, whose form is like a cowherd boy in the cool season, shall go to the abode of Hari.
One should offer milk-based sweetmeats (laḍḍukas) to the high-souled Keśava;
he shall drink nectar in heaven for the duration of a hundred manvantaras.
O Jaimini, for whoever bestows this section, the *Harayelalita-khaṇḍa*,
Viṣṇu, with a gracious soul, severs the bonds of worldly existence.
O twice-born one, he who gives a divine, variegated fruit to the Blessed One shall go to the city of Indra and become honored by the gods. ||8||
O Brahmin, does he who is devoted to Kṛṣṇa obtain pure sugar-candy by the grace of Vāsudeva? ||9||
Listen to the fruit that belongs to him who gives a sweet jujube fruit, well-ripened in the month of Phālguna, to Kṛṣṇa. (10)
Having enjoyed every happiness here together with his sons and grandsons,
he ascends a beautiful chariot and goes to the abode of Hari.
O best of Brahmins, one should not offer a jujube fruit mixed with molasses to Hari; if one should offer it out of ignorance, he will become a denizen of hell.
If one should offer or take up a pomegranate fruit in the month of Phālguna, listen attentively, O Brāhmaṇa, as I describe that well-ripened fruit. (13)
In that regard, for as many seeds as remain within the pomegranate fruit, for so many intermediate kalpas (manvantaras) does that fortunate person remain in the abode of Viṣṇu. 14.
O best of the twice-born, he who offers balls of wheat flour mixed with jaggery to Hari in the month of Phālguna should be known as one who has performed a thousand horse-sacrifices.
O best of the twice-born, in the month of Caitra, a mortal who bathes Madhusūdana with honey attains that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. 16.
He who bathes the healthy Nārāyaṇa with honey shall never be scrutinized by the son of the Sun (Yama). 17.
Whoever worships the Lord of Kamalā with *śukapuṣpa* flowers on the full moon day of Caitra, his name is not written by Citragupta upon the tongue of Yama. (18)
Those who worship the Lord of the worlds with *lakapuṣpa* flowers during the month of Caitra have no further birth on this earth. 19.
A person who worships the crest-jewel of all the gods with a *kṛṣṇa-vajrula* flower shall never encounter misfortune anywhere. (20)
O Blessed One, he who honors you with springtime songs and skillful prayers is honored even by the gods, for his soul is serene.
Likewise, he who worships Hari with divine, unbroken sprouts, even one who is seated upon a throne, rises up of his own accord to salute him. (22)
The person who worships Hari with fresh, tender leaves of the *dhātrī* tree attains all their desires without delay. (23)
He who worships Viṣṇu and the Lord with Śāṇḍilya leaves, Akaṇḍa leaves, Dhattūra flowers, and Arka flowers, shall cross to the further shore of the ocean of worldly existence.
To him who gives an excellent plantain fruit to Viṣṇu, all the thirty gods, headed by Śakra, pay homage day and night. (25)
O Brahmin, he who with devotion offers wheat flour cakes to the one in the form of Gopāla during the month of Caitra is liberated from all sins. (26)
O beloved Mādhava, in this pure month of Mādhava, a devotee of Vi�ṣṇu should renounce meat, sexual intercourse, and oil. (27)
Having arrived during the month of Vaiśākha, a Vaiṣṇava should perform his ritual bath;
he should avoid the food of others and should not eat twice.
O twice-born one, at dawn one should worship Viṣṇu according to the previously mentioned procedure;
in the month of Vaiśākha, one should bathe Viṣṇu with water scented with flowers.
One should bathe Acyuta with cool water at the end of the twilight;
one should worship the Lord with devotion during the three junctions of the day with various kinds of food offerings.
O brahmin-sage, what will the Supreme Lord not grant when he is pleased, having been fully adorned with garlands of *udumbara* flowers during the month of Vaiśākha? (31)
Who among the learned is capable of enumerating the merits of one who offers barley-rice to the wielder of the discus (Viṣṇu) in the month of Vaiśākha? ||32||
Whatever is given in the month of Mādhava for the sake of pleasing Mādhava, all that becomes inexhaustible for Mādhava himself. ||33||
Whatever other meritorious deed is performed during the month of Mādhava, there is no destruction of that [merit] for the sake of pleasing Mādhava. (34)
If one should establish a water-station (*prapā*) in the month of Vaiśākha for the pleasure of Mādhava, that person obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice (*aśvamedha*) day after day. ||35||
The month of Vaiśākha is difficult to obtain and bestows the fruits of all actions;
therein, Hari should be worshipped, even setting aside hundreds of other rites.
Whoever performs worship of Hari for even a single day in the month of Vaiśākha obtains that same fruit which one attains by worshipping Hari for six years. (37)
In the month of Vaiśākha, a devotee of Viṣṇu should constantly worship Viṣṇu in the form of the Aśvattha tree for the sake of attaining the fruits of the four aims of human life.
He who performs the service of the Aśvattha tree with even a mere mouthful of water shall go to the supreme abode, liberated from ten million sins.
O brahmin-sage, if one binds the root of an aśvattha tree with stones and other materials, the Blessed One, assuming the form of an aśvattha, grants him whatever he desires. (40)
If one beholds the Aśvattha tree and offers a salutation, he too goes to the supreme abode; there is no doubt that his lifespan will increase. (41)
O Jaimini, when one who is a preeminent knower of the Dharma performs a ritual action under an Aśvattha tree,
there may be a deficiency or an excess in that action.
In that place, O Jaimini, all the sacred fords such as Trisrotas and others are present wherever even a single pipal tree stands, the best among all trees. (43)
O twice-born one, he who worships the Aśvattha tree is indeed a worshiper of Viṣṇu;
for the Blessed Lord himself exists in the form of the Aśvattha. 44.
O best of the twice-born, that fool who, out of contempt, destroys an aśvattha tree—there is no action in this world by performing which he becomes purified. (45)
This Aśvattha tree is the king of trees and is proclaimed to be the very form of Hari;
therefore, there is no protector of those who have taken refuge in the Aśvattha even to be found. 46.
For the Brahmin who beholds, touches, or even stands beyond the Aśvattha tree,
Hari removes all the sins residing within his body as he bows down.
If anyone, upon seeing a crying horse-fig tree, is able to prevent it [from being cut],
Yama himself will pluck out that person's pair of eyes with hooks.
If a fool should say, "Do not cut down the Aśvattha tree," the King of the Pretas himself shall cut out his tongue with a knife. (49)
That man who indeed destroys even a single, very small branch of the Aśvattha tree obtains the fruit of ten million murders of Brahmins. ||50||
Whatever sin exists in the killing of a Brahmin, in approaching the wife of a guru, in drinking liquor, as well as in theft and the misappropriation of a deposit; ||51||
O best of the twice-born, whatever sin exists in the killing of a fetus, in the killing of a cow, in the killing of a woman, and likewise in approaching another's wife; ||52||
In the killing of one who has sought refuge, in the killing of a friend, in failing to speak words of trust, and in the betrayal of one who has been protected; ||53||
Whatever terrible sin is incurred by people through censuring others, eating on the day of Hari, or cutting down the Aśvattha tree—that very same sin is obtained [by those who act thus]. (54)
There is no sinner equal to him who, out of delusion, destroys the Aśvattha tree, which is the very body of Viṣṇu; such a person has never been heard of on this earth.
O best of the twice-born, listen with a concentrated mind, my child, as I recount the greatness of the Aśvattha tree, which destroys all sins, along with its ancient history. (56)
In the Tretā Yuga, there was a brāhmaṇa named Jayo who possessed wealth; he was a devotee of Hari and was devoted to the welfare of all living beings. (57)
Constantly devoted to honoring his kinsmen, always intent on offering lamps, truthful in speech, having conquered anger, free from pride and hypocrisy—such was I. (58)
O best of the twice-born, desiring liberation, he always worshipped the Supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Sovereign, with supreme devotion. (59)
Then, having recognized his devotion as great and very firm,
the Lord took away all his wealth by some pretext.
Nevertheless, O best of the twice-born, that wise man performed the worship of the high-souled Keśava every day with supreme devotion. (61)
O twice-born one, seeing that all his wealth, which had been acquired with great hardship, was lost,
that brahmin became distressed and his mind was filled with inconceivable sorrow.
Having firmly bound his own mind to the worship of Mahāviṣṇu, that brāhmaṇa, who knew the supreme truth, practiced avoidance of meat-eating.
Furthermore, having recognized the devotion of that brahmin, Janārdana,
who is firmly established in tranquility and bestows peace, brought about the separation from his kinsmen.
O best of the twice-born, the relatives of that brāhmaṇa, deluded by the māyā of Viṣṇu, began to practice violence at all times. (65)
Then, having attained liberation from his persistent efforts, the Brahmin, being constantly delighted, worshipped Puruṣottama with abundant devotion.
By worshipping Keśava, he acquired wealth that was merely imagined;
and by worshipping Mādhava, the Lord of the World, he cast off the grief for his kinsmen.
Furthermore, O Jaimini, the ever-curious Mahāviṣṇu, out of compassion for him,
carried away his sons day after day.
Nevertheless, O best of the twice-born, he constantly worshipped Viṣṇu Keśava, the destroyer of afflictions, with devotion twice as great as before.
His wife, exceedingly distressed by grief and sorrow,
went to her father’s house, utterly deluded by the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu.
Then, that solitary god, devoted solely to the worship of Viṣṇu,
once reflected upon his misfortune with a clear mind.
Once, O best of the twice-born, that foremost among the devotees of Viṣṇu took up his axe and went into the forest for the sake of wood. (72)
Just as a twice-born man, having taken wood from the forest, constantly makes a protection against the cold when winter arrives, being himself devoid of clothing. ||73||
Once, that best of the twice-born was unable to go into the forest;
he struck a branch of an aśvattha tree located near the assembly hall. (74)
In the meantime, Mahāviṣṇu, the best of the Asuras, emerged from that Aśvattha tree with a distressed mind. ||75||
Together with the brahmin, he beheld Viṣṇu before him— four-armed, with eyes as broad as lotus petals,
wearing yellow garments and earrings, possessing beautiful hair, and bearing his own weapons such as the lotus and others.
With fresh clouds beautifully reddened by streams of flowing blood spreading wide,
he beheld the Lord of the gods, the Supreme Master, who is invisible even to the hosts of deities, appearing as easily as the fire itself.
With streams of tears of joy flowing from his beautiful pair of eyes,
the brahmin praised him with gentle words.
The brahmin said:
"O Hari, O Murāri, O sole Lord of the world, O Govinda, O Dāmodara, O Mādhava!"
O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Keśava, O enemy of Keśin, O Nārāyaṇa, O Infinite One, O All-pervading Lord, be gracious! ||78||
What can I say regarding your incarnation?
For without you, there is no one else here on earth; or rather, what can I say of you who pervade the entire world with your virtues?
Or rather, why do you not show compassion that is equal toward friends, enemies, and strangers alike? ||79||

Having bestowed my own devotion to Lord Viṣṇu upon someone, and having taken away the prosperity of Hara which resides within the body of Acyuta, I shall grant them joy; truly fortunate is the devotion offered to the Great One. (80)

I think that for this very reason, the pair of your feet—which is like the constant refuge for the great-souled and the foremost among the sinful—is not seen by the sinner, a matter to be considered as ordained by fate. (81)
O Viṣṇu, although I consider myself the foremost among those who suffer, nevertheless, today I would behold you— the very Self of the worlds— with my own eyes, just as Indra beheld himself.
"Even if I offer you only a small amount at the end of my worship, I never give any substance to you;
nevertheless, O Keśava, you alone, the sole object of worship, have appeared before me in embodied form. (83)
O Lord, this tree of devotion which you bestowed upon me— consisting of the three aims of virtue, wealth, and desire—
having been watered by the rain of your vision, has today borne the fruit of absolute liberation (kaivalya).
O Keśava, whose universal form is the head of all the heads of the worlds, may my mind now truly abide in the pair of your lotus feet, O God of gods. (85)
Vyāsa said:
Having thus praised Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the World, who is free from all ailment, that virtuous twice-born man, with palms joined in reverence, spoke to him again with devotion. (86)
The Brāhmaṇa said:
O God of gods, Lord of the world, benefactor of the worlds!
This body of yours has been drenched with blood by the strokes of whips. (87)
All the Daityas have been slain by you in battle;
O Lord, who on earth is capable of slaying you? This is a great wonder. (88)
The Blessed One said:
"O child, what you have spoken is true; there is no doubt in this matter.
Whether it be a Dānava, a Rākṣasa, or anyone else, no one at all is capable of slaying me. (89)
"I am indeed the very form of the Aśvattha tree, struck by you with an axe; therefore, O twice-born one, blood has now fallen upon my body. (90)
Vyāsa said:
Having heard these words of his, that brahmin, overwhelmed by fear,
censured himself in many ways by means of his own mind.
Fie upon that truly wretched fortune, the worst among all sinners,
which has given such great pain to the heart of the Lord of the Three Worlds!
Viṣṇu, the remover of all sins, has been offended by me through this transgression; this boundless sin cannot be remedied by me alone. (93)
When he is satisfied, even sinners become honored by the gods; yet I am afflicted and struck down by this painless [state] bestowed by me. 94.
He whom the gods, beginning with Brahmā, propitiate with supreme devotion—alas, for me, a sinner, he has been placed within my heart as it were. 95.
Of what use are austerities, recitations, or even houses and livelihoods?
This one alone is the swift bestower of virtue, wealth, pleasure, and liberation. (96)
Having spoken thus, O best of the twice-born, he set his mind upon giving that very axe back to himself for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu. (97)
Perceiving his firm devotion, the compassionate Lord of Kamalā, who is kind to His devotees, swiftly led him from that hand to the Supreme. 98.
The Blessed Lord said:
O child, why do you perform such an extremely cruel deed?
I am never pleased with men who commit suicide.
"I am exceedingly pleased by your devotion; do not fear, O best of beings! Choose a boon, O chief of brahmins, whatever dwells in your mind. (100)
The Brāhmaṇa said:
"O Supreme Lord, O Master, let this great body which has been bestowed by me remain within you as your own supreme form. (101)
The Blessed Lord said:
"O twice-born one, this action was performed by you out of ignorance;
therefore, this great offense must not be disregarded by you."
"I am to be constantly protected by you, for you are the best among devotees;
day after day, I consider all faults as yours alone. (103)
Nevertheless, my devotion to you has always increased greatly;
therefore, child, I now wish to attain freedom from my debt to you. (104)
"O Vāyu, ward off all fear from before me!
The Brāhmaṇa said:
"In birth after birth, you are the best among all the gods. (105)
"Let there be firm devotion to Hari while he remains; what is the use of other boons?
Vyāsa said:
Having heard these words of his, spoken out of affection for Keśava, [the sages remained silent]. (106)
Then, being pleased, the Lord gave him the garland that was upon his own neck;
thereafter, he embraced the brahmin as a father embraces a son.
With his four long arms, the Blessed Lord spoke these gentle words: "O brāhmaṇa, since you are My devotee, by My grace it shall be so. (108)
O best of beings, by means of the yoga of ritual action, you shall before long attain my form as the Aśvattha tree in its entirety and forever. 109.
"Propitiate them all, and I shall accomplish your desire.
Having spoken thus to that best of the twice-born, Keśava embraced him once more. (110)
Thereupon, that brāhmaṇa, the best of Vaiṣṇavas and an abode of compassion, suddenly became like Viṣṇu himself upon receiving the garland from His neck. 111.
O brahmin-sage, considering himself as one who had accomplished his purpose, he remained in his own home; thereafter, Kubera [resided] in the house of that brahmin.
At the command of Keśava, he himself rained down vast amounts of wealth upon many [people];
a palace was constructed for him by the artisan Viśvakarman.
By the command of Nārāyaṇa, the excellent Vaijayanta [palace] was established there,
provided with male and female servants and adorned with various articles.
His palace, crowded with tens of millions of elephants and horses, shone brilliantly;
even his lost kinsmen became reunited with him. (115)
Having thus insulted his wife, he himself went to her house;
out of compassion for Keśava, whose wife had lost her son, he [Kṛṣṇa] went there. (116)
The subjects became stable, and the brahmins were devoted solely to their master;
having enjoyed all pleasures for a long time, he was accompanied by his sons and grandsons. (117)
The best of Brahmins, Āstīka, attained liberation from his life.
Vyāsa said:
"The Aśvattha tree, the best of trees, is Viṣṇu himself in person. (118)
For those men who practice devotion to Him, no inauspiciousness exists anywhere;
O best of men, he who serves the Aśvattha tree while meditating upon Viṣṇu [attains this]. 119.
The Blessed One, being pleased with him, bestows the supreme state.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Aśvattha Tree," in the Kriyā-yoga-sāra of the glorious Padma Purāṇa. ||12||
(13) Chapter Thirteen.
Vyāsa said:
O best of the twice-born, in the month of Jyeṣṭha, one should worship that Lord Janārdana with a spirit of devotion, having bathed him with cool waters. (1)
One should offer a fragrant scrubbing powder as well as fragrant *āmalaka* fruit;
one should offer fragrant oil to Hari day after day during the summer season. (2)
Every day, one should install the Beloved of Kamalā within a very beautiful pavilion that is well-perfumed, cool, and provided with a canopy.
O best of Brahmins, one should not install the Lord of Kamalā in a place that is fierce, smoky, or a repository for charcoal,
nor indeed in a lying-in chamber.
O best of the twice-born, why does he, being well-pleased, carry the Lord of Kamalā—who is fanned by long, white chowries—on his head during this month of Jyeṣṭha? (5)
O best of beings, Hari, fanned with long-handled yak-tail whisks,
grants all that is desired in no time at all.
Those by whom Viṣṇu is fanned during the summer with the pure wind of a palm-leaf fan, all of them go to heaven.
In the summer, one should apply fragrant pastes to the body and enter the form of Mādhava, which is cool with sandalwood.
O best of the twice-born, there is no doubt that one attains the state of heat (uṣman) in a garden of blossoming flowers as well as in a grove of tulasī. ||9||
At twilight, one should establish Viṣṇu in a place where the wind is steady,
having adorned him with garlands of *pāṭala* flowers by which Viṣṇu has been fully embellished.
That person who, during the summer, offers a pearl necklace to the Lord of Vaishrīpati in the month of Jyeṣṭha, should be known as one who has performed a thousand horse-sacrifices.
Hari shall grant the status of a sovereign ruler to him in birth after birth, who adorns Śrī Kṛṣṇa with a garland of jewels during the summer season. 12.
O Jaimini, listen attentively as I describe the fruit of that merit,
as far as Brahmā created this entire world.
He shall dwell in the city of Viṣṇu for that long, adorned with garlands of jewels,
as well as with ornaments of gold and ornaments of silver.
He who gives a variegated couch with pillows during the summer heat attains that very same fruit.
One should never cause distress to the God of gods;
during the summer season, one should provide garments to one's gurus.
O best of brāhmaṇas, one should offer that pure and beautiful body to Hari; he who worships Hari with divine, fragrant, and unfading fruits.
Having gone to the city of Śakra, he shall joyfully drink the nectar of immortality—he who worships the Lord of Kamalā with divine priyāla fruits. (18)
He obtains that very fruit; what is the use of much further talk?
He who offers very cold barley-gruel to Hari during the summer heat [attains this]. (19)
In the month of Āṣāḍha, a devotee of Viṣṇu, endowed with faith, [should worship] the God of gods, the Teacher of the World, amidst a multitude of various people, O best of Brahmins. (20)
Having bathed [the deity] with curds, the wise man should worship with devotion;
thereafter, he shall never again drink the milk from his mother's breast. (21)
O brahmin-sage, by worshipping Hari with kadamba flowers— He who is dark as a dense rain cloud— one shall attain the supreme state.
He who [decorates] the pavilion, which resembles a blazing fire, with garlands of kadamba flowers shall obtain the fruit of the horse sacrifice (vājimedha) of the best of brahmins. ||23||
O best of the twice-born, the Lord of Kamalā, when worshipped with fragrant ketakī flowers,
removes all the suffering of human beings in this manner.
When the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu is worshipped with divine, well-ripened jackfruit fruits mixed with ghee, he shall bestow supreme sovereignty.
O best of the twice-born, a Vaiṣṇava who desires liberation should, with faith, offer curd-rice to Hari every day during the month of Āṣāḍha.
The Vaiṣṇava person who gives the butter from Kṛṣṇā’s milk becomes purified of all sins and goes to the world of Brahmā. ||27||
He who worships the Supreme Self with *śephālikā* blossoms as well as *yūthikā* flowers shall go to the supreme state. (28)
O twice-born one, the merit of him who worships Hari with fragrant, fully blossomed mālatī flowers shall be such that no other merit will ever equal it.
A person on earth who worships Janārdana, the friend of the world, with *kaṃda* flowers and *vakula* blossoms, attains every desire. (30)
He who worships Hari with great *mahāprasūna* flowers as well as blossoming *kurubaka* flowers—Hari is always pleased with him. (31)
He who worships Viṣṇu with *sairīyaka* flowers, with *prasūpa* flowers,
and with *karavīra* blossoms, attains the presence of Hari.
And whoever should offer parched grains mixed with ghee to Hari in the month of Śrāvaṇa,
O brahmin-sage, prosperity shall be manifest in every direction in his home.
O best of the twice-born, in the month of Bhādrapada, a wise person should worship the flawless Nārāyaṇa with faith, for he is the bestower of the four aims of human life. 34.
One should install the lotus-eyed Lord Janārdana in a newly constructed temple that is free from all calamities.
A human being should certainly not place Hari upon an ancient tree that is infested with gadflies, mosquitoes, flies, and the like. (36)
A wise man should not install Lord Hari, the Supreme Controller, in a house that has a door leading to a muddy place or where the walls are crumbling during the rainy season. ||37||
O best of the twice-born, that man who performs the *candrātapa* rite at the temple of Viṣṇu goes to the wonderful world of the Moon. (38)
At night, during the time of worship, one should ward off gnats and mosquitoes from the Lord of the World with various kinds of incense.
One should establish Viṣṇu, who is covered by female sarika birds and reclining there, in his divine palace during the night of the rainy season. 40.
Likewise, a mortal desiring liberation should worship the Lord of Gods with white lotus petals and fragrant substances every day during the month of Bhādra. 41.
The Destroyer of the World (Viṣṇu) should be worshipped with *ketakī* flowers in the month of Bhādrapada;
for in the month of Bhādrapada, the *ketakī* is equal to wine.
He who worships the scion of the Yadu dynasty with divine, ripe tāla fruits shall never again experience the great suffering of dwelling in a womb. ||43||
If a mortal should offer a ripe palm fruit combined with ghee and milk to the Enemy of Mura with faith, he shall go to the abode of Hari. (44)
O best of the twice-born, in the month of Bhādrapada, a Vaiṣṇava should offer a Tāla-piṣṭaka cake with ghee to Hari for the sake of attaining Kevala.
In the month of Bhādrapada, a brāhmaṇa should consume only vegetables;
a person who is a Vaiṣṇava seeking liberation should not eat at night. (46)
In the month of Āśvina, O best of Brahmins, when water is offered with effort by people to Keśava—the destroyer of afflictions—for Hari during the forenoon; ||47||
The Lord of Kamalā accepts that water as if it were nectar;
and that water which is offered at midday is for the wielder of the discus (Cakrapāṇi).
O best of the twice-born, that [water] should be understood as being like water;
it is taken up by him, and in the afternoon, that water is offered to Govinda.
Then that water would become like blood, and Hari would not accept it;
for this very reason, O best of the twice-born, one should worship Hari in the forenoon.
O best of Brahmins, by the compassion of Keśava, one obtains every desire;
however, one should not perform the worship of Hari while wearing only a single garment.
Or even if one should perform worship in that manner, Keśava does not accept it; likewise, he who performs the worship of Hari with unwashed clothing [is disregarded]. (52)
The worship performed by those people who offer it with their hair-tufts untied shall be fruitless, and Viṣṇu will not be pleased. (53)
They do not obtain the fruit of worship, and she [the deity] would become a consumer of offerings;
thus, worship of the Lord of the World is performed in an unconsecrated house. (54)
O best of Brahmins, that worship indeed becomes worthy of receiving the sacrificial offering (bali), as well as bathing, the worship of the gods, giving gifts, and the honoring of the ancestors. (55)
One who is not discerning does not perform a service without a sectarian mark (*tilaka*); for whatever meritorious deed is performed without taking up the sectarian marks [is incomplete]. (56)
All that is reduced to ashes, and the doer shall become a denizen of hell—unless one is seen marked with the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus. (57)
O best of Brahmins, he who, as a Vaiṣṇava, would draw the conch and the lotus upon his right arm—that very person is to be known as the imperishable Lord himself. 58.
On the left [hand] there is a discus and a mace; he is undoubtedly Viṣṇu.
One should draw a lotus on the right arm above the conch shell.
All his sins perish in an instant,
O twice-born one, who draws a mace upon the wheel with his right hand.
O best of the twice-born, even the gods led by Śakra pay homage to him;
therefore, a wise person should draw the pair of feet of Murāri upon his forehead.
Even a person of sinful nature, upon seeing him, becomes liberated from sin;
likewise, one who holds the great eight-syllable mantra, as well as the Fish and Tortoise incarnations, within his heart [is liberated].
The best of all Vaiṣṇavas should draw [these marks], for he purifies the three worlds;
his body becomes marked by the weapons of Kṛṣṇa day after day.
To him, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the World, grants the supreme state—
that man whose body is marked by the weapons of Kṛṣṇa performs whatever action he does.
Whether it be auspicious or inauspicious, all that has been sown shall become inexhaustible;
likewise for the Dānavas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, and Vetālas. (65)
Piśācas and pannagas, as well as yakṣas and vidyādharas;
kinnaras and guhyakas, and likewise grahas and bālagrahas. ||66||
The Kūṣmāṇḍas, the Ḍākinīs, and likewise other creators of obstacles,
all fled in fear upon seeing him marked by the weapons of Kṛṣṇa.
The island-dwellers, the forest-dwellers, and likewise those living in the marshes,
fled in terror upon merely seeing him, who was armed with the dark weapon.
Great diseases such as jaundice and others that cause the body to fall away—by means of devotion, one who possesses yoga beholds them as having bodies marked by the weapons of Kṛṣṇa. (69)
A human being obtains a fruit equal to the vision of Kṛṣṇa by worshipping Hari with three-folded dūrvā grass on the day of the Aśvinī constellation.
His lineage proceeds uninterrupted like a cluster of dūrvā grass. He who offers a karkaṭī fruit to Hari in the month of Āśvina [attains this]. (71)
O twice-born one, sorrow never arises in his heart when the auspicious Kārttika, the best of all months, has arrived. (72)
O best of Brahmins, a wise person should worship Dāmodara, the God of gods, with devotion during the month of Kārttika for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu. (73)
The wise man should perform the morning bath according to the prescribed rule;
he who renounces meat and sexual intercourse during the month of Kārttika [attains great merit]. (74)
O best of the twice-born, one who bathes at dawn when the sun has entered the zodiac sign of Libra is liberated from the sins accumulated in other births and attains the supreme state. (75)
The consumption of sacrificial food and the practice of celibacy destroy even the greatest sins;
yet he who indulges in meat and sexual intercourse during the month of Kārttika [incurs great fault]. (76)
O best of Brahmins, in birth after birth,
that person who eats twice a day, eats the food of others, eats oil, and is not a devotee of Viṣṇu, shall become a village pig.
When the month of Kārtika has arrived, one should abandon [other lights] even with effort; yet he who offers a lamp to Dāmodara during the month of Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa) [attains great merit]. ||78||
I shall proclaim its fruit; listen briefly, O twice-born one!
One is liberated from sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, which bring about suffering. (79)
Having gone to Dāmodarapura, one should remain there for ten million yugas;
that lamp burning in the sky is beheld by the dwellers of heaven, Indra, and the others.
Seeing him, they were all delighted and said to one another:
"This man is the best among those of meritorious soul, for he is devoted to the worship of Keśava. (81)
O best of Brahmins, Hari is always pleased with him who offers a lamp to the Wielder of the Discus (Viṣṇu) during the month of Kārttika. (82)
That person who offers an imperishable lamp in the temple of Hari during the month of Kārttika obtains, day after day, the fruit of a horse sacrifice. ||83||
He who worships Hari with a hundred thousand Tulasī leaves during the month of Kārtika obtains the fruit equal to that of a hundred thousand horse-sacrifices. (84)
He who worships the imperishable Viṣṇu with one hundred thousand bilva leaves attains supreme liberation through the grace of the Lord of the World. (85)
Whatever is given during the month of Kārttika dedicated to Viṣṇu, all that becomes inexhaustible; this which I speak is the truth. (86)
O Brahmin, he who offers a lotus leaf smeared with ghee day after day during the month of Kārttika, sacred to Viṣṇu, shall dwell in the city of Viṣṇu.
What on earth is difficult for one to obtain who worships the Beloved of Kamalā with a white or even a dark petal from a blossoming lotus? (88)
O foremost of the twice-born, has he who did not offer a lotus to Hari in the month of Kārttika not given anything at all to Viṣṇu, the conqueror of the Daityas, O Brāhmaṇa? (89)
If one steals even a single lotus and gives it to the enemy of Kaiṭabha, what will Lord Viṣṇu, the husband of Śrī, not bestow upon him? (90)
In whose house Lakṣmī does not abide throughout birth after birth, by whom Hari has not been worshipped with lotuses in the month of Kārttika? 91.
Whoever should give lotus seeds to the high-souled Keśava shall be born into a pure family of Brahmins in every birth. 92.
Born into a brahmin family, he shall be a friend of the four Vedas;
he shall be wealthy, have many sons, and be a supporter of his dependents. (93)
"There is no flower equal to the lotus; this is truly said by Jaimini.
By worshipping Govinda with it, even a sinful soul becomes a partaker of liberation. (94)
O best of the twice-born, I shall now specifically describe the majesty of the lotus flower; listen attentively along with its ancient history. 95.
There was once a single non-Brahmin among the people who was a knower of all the scriptures, in whose heart-bee there was a constant dwelling upon the lotus-feet of Hari. (96)

O best of the twice-born, for one who has always performed worship of the gods, the brahmins, and their gurus, even hundreds of deeds—whether they ought to be done or ought not to be done—[are purified]. 97.
He regards another's property as poison and another's wife as his own mother; he treats an enemy exactly as he does a friend. (98)
Seeing a guest approaching, that brāhmaṇa who knows the supreme truth does not feel excessive pride, even if the guest is a most excellent twice-born seeking alms. (99)
By him who desires to cross the terrible and shoreless ocean of worldly existence, all sacrifices have been performed and all vows have been observed. (100)
Once, that best of the twice-born, who was solely devoted to the worship of Hari,
reflected in his mind upon his own death and his original birth.
Who was I that stood before this? What speech or action was performed in the past?
How was this birth attained, and where shall I go again? (102)
Having reflected thus, that brahmin sighed again and again and went to the sacred field of Śiva to learn of his former history.
There, the Brahmin, with palms joined in reverence and filled with supreme devotion, praised the auspicious Lord Śaṅkara with sweet speech.
The Brāhmaṇa said:
Salutations to you, O Mahādeva; salutations to you, O Supreme Lord. Salutations to you, O Śaṅkara, O Īśāna; salutations to you, O Lord who grants boons. (105)
Homage to you whose form is wisdom; homage to you, the giver of wisdom;
homage to you who dwell in the lotus-heart of all beings. 106.
Salutations to you, the creator of the world; salutations, salutations to the father of the world.
Salutations to the performer of the withdrawal of all things, and salutations to the Lord of creatures (Paśupati). 107.
Homage to you whose mind is fire and whose eyes are fire;
homage to you whose eyes are the moon and whose eyes are the sun. 108.
Homage to you who are adorned with ashes; homage to you who are clothed in an animal skin. Homage to you who wear a garland of bones; homage to the one with a blue throat.
Homage to you, the five-faced one; homage to you, the wielder of the trident;
to you who possess a terrifying form and who bring about the destruction of the pride of Kandarpa.
Homage to you, the God of gods; homage to you, the enemy of Tripura; homage to you, the Lord of Pārvatī; homage to you, whose form is terrifying. 111.
Salutations to you, whose mind is exceedingly pleased by the devotion of Bāṇa;
salutations indeed to you of manifold forms, salutations indeed to you of universal form. 112.

Salutations to you, the bearer of the Gaṅgā; salutations to you, the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice; salutations to you, the lord of the departed spirits; salutations to you, the wielder of the Pināka bow.
Salutation to you, the Sovereign; salutation again and again to the Wise One.
Salutation be to you, the Visible; salutation again and again to the Invisible. Salutation to you, the Thinkable; salutation again and again to the Unthinkable. ||114||

You alone are Brahmā, the sole lord of the thirty gods; you alone are Viṣṇu, and you alone are the Sun; you alone are the Moon, the remover of all suffering. Salutations, repeated salutations to You, the Supreme Lord! 115.
Having heard his hymn of praise, the Supreme Lord, the benefactor of the world who brings happiness to the world, suddenly appeared, gracious and serene. ||116||
Beholding him who had manifested and was saluted by all the gods,
that brahmin, filled with supreme devotion, bowed at his feet.
Once again, that best of the twice-born, his mind overflowing with joy,
joined his palms in reverence and praised the Great Lord, the boon-bestowing Master.
The Brāhmaṇa said:
"O Lord of Gods, whom even the gods together with Indra do not behold, I see him directly; this is my great good fortune. (119)
With a mind established in meditative absorption, I behold this invisible Supreme Lord directly; what else remains for me to accomplish? 120.
"By the mere remembrance of your name, even those who have committed great sins go to the supreme abode; I shall behold that Lord. (121)
I have achieved my purpose, I have achieved my purpose, I have achieved my purpose; I am fortunate!
Salutations to you, salutations to you; be gracious, O Supreme Lord.
Mahādeva said: "O best of the twice-born, I am pleased by these words of yours. Choose a boon, O highly fortunate one; indeed, I desire to grant you a boon. (123)
The Brahmin said:
"O Lord, I behold you directly as the Supreme Self, invisible even to the gods; what need have I for other boons? (124)
Nevertheless, O Supreme Lord, you are compassionate and desirous of granting boons to Mahādeva; therefore, please tell me what it is that I am asking. 125.
Who was I that stood here in the past, O Devakī? What deed was performed by me formerly?
O Lord, how have I fallen into this ocean of worldly existence? (126)
A body is obtained through karma, and the embodied soul is defiled by sin;
furthermore, by the power of that sin, one attains a miserable rebirth. (127)
"By the power of which actions, O Lord, have I obtained this birth that bestows manifold sufferings? O bringer of peace, if you are pleased with me, please tell me. (128)
This evil is the root, the cause of suffering in birth after birth;
therefore, I desire to know my own previous history. (129)
I remained within my mother's womb, tormented by the fire of the stomach,
amidst urine and excrement, as a result of my past karmas.

O Lord, destroyer of the suffering of your devotees, how is it that one does not consider the dwelling in the womb to be as much suffering within this cycle of existence? How could I have experienced that [without your grace]? 131.
In this great and terrible saṃsāra, which is filled with manifold sufferings, devoid of essence, deluded by the illusion of Viṣṇu, and a refuge for sins; ||132||
It is difficult to cross, devoid of kinsmen, and possessed of desire, anger, and the like;
it brings about sorrow and disease, and likewise bestows birth and death. ||133||
O Śiva, I have fallen into the state of being a master over the worlds that are beyond the reach of others; O All-pervading Lord, if you have favor toward me, tell me all of this.
Mahādeva said:
"O best of the twice-born, although this is a great secret, more secret than the secret, and not to be disclosed, nevertheless I shall speak it to you, for you are my devotee. (135)
Formerly, O best of Brahmins, you were born into the lineage of the Śabaras;
known as Daṇḍapāṇi, you remained there causing suffering to the world. (136)
Having abandoned the fear of the next world and being devoid of discernment, he has adopted the conduct of a robber, which brings about supreme suffering and distress for those in need. (137)
Seeing him engaged in the conduct of a bandit, I became exceedingly merciless;
all my other brothers likewise became bandits. (138)
O best of Brahmins, I shall now declare the names of those brothers with whom you formerly committed acts of banditry.
Daṇḍin, Daṇḍāyudha, Datta, Dattabhu, Suṃdaḍa, and Daṇḍaketu—these six are proclaimed to be his brothers. (140)
By those most terrible brothers, devoid of compassion, all people were constantly kept in a state of agitation by means of unjust punishment. (141)
Driven by greed for wealth, you, along with those wicked brothers,
slaughtered hundreds of thousands of people in the depths of the forest.
O twice-born one, you always killed [beings] with sharp arrows while living in the forest,
and you ate the raw flesh of cows along with liquor.
Then, out of fear of you, all those merchants abandoned the method of travel in that forest; thus, misfortune has always befallen them.
He whose wealth is not wealth, whose house is not a house, and whose wife is not a wife—when you have become a bandit, all these things cease to be such. (145)
Thus, with those brothers of his, he went toward a lake in that very great forest for the purpose of bathing, weary from the fatigue of the journey.
There, O best of the twice-born, having performed his ablutions, he who was hungry ate lotus stalks and drank water along with those brothers. (147)
Furthermore, O best of the twice-born, O most excellent one, you ate many blooming lotus flowers there out of curiosity. (148)
At that very time, a Brāhmaṇa who roamed the forest, known as Sarvavedas, arrived there for the purpose of bathing. ||149||
Having bathed there, that virtuous-souled one, desiring to sacrifice to you, Lord Janārdana, requested Bhoja with great humility. (150)
Furthermore, O best of Brahmins, you have offered a single, perfectly pure lotus with supreme devotion for the purpose of worshipping the Lord of Kamalā. (151)
Pleased by the lotus given by you, that best of the twice-born worshipped Viṣṇu, the creator of all, right there. (152)
Seeing that brāhmaṇa, who was devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu and possessed of all Vedic knowledge, you too laughed and bowed to Viṣṇu, the granter of happiness and desires. (153)
Then, having worshipped the Supreme Self, who bestows the fruits of the four aims of human existence,
according to the prescribed rite, O Brahmin, he departed just as he had come.
O best of beings, by that offering of a lotus, by that prostration, and by witnessing the worship of Viṣṇu, all his sin was destroyed. (155)
Then, after some days,
O best of the twice-born, you, having reached your time, passed away in that very great forest.
Not satisfied with that very deed, the Blessed One, the abode of compassion,
bestowed upon you a supreme station that is extremely difficult even for the gods to attain.
For thousands of manvantaras and hundreds of manvantaras, various pleasures were enjoyed there through the grace of the Lord of Kamalā. (158)
Then, O twice-born one, at the conclusion of that karma, having returned to this land of action by virtue of those fruits of merit, you were born into a lineage of the twice-born. (159)
O best of beings, having obtained birth in a pure brahmin family, you have attained unwavering devotion to Hari, which is the refuge of all virtues. (160)
The Lord Mahāviṣṇu has been propitiated by you through the practice of kriyā-yoga; He will grant you supreme knowledge, and through that knowledge, you shall become liberated. 161.
Go, O Brahmin; may it be well with you. Being well-pleased, return to your own home. You have obtained a vision of me and are liberated from the bonds of worldly existence. (162)
Vyāsa said:
Having spoken thus, O Brahmin, the Lord of the Universe vanished right there;
and that Brāhmaṇa, having achieved his purpose, went to his own home.
Then, for three days, he diligently propitiated Viṣṇu, the Supreme Lord, with beautiful lotus flowers for the purpose of offering praise.
Having propitiated Viṣṇu for a long time with various lotus flowers and beautiful blossoms, he fell into a deep sleep; then,
having attained gnosis, he went to liberation.
By the grace of the illustrious Garuḍadhvaja. ||165||
If even one who offers a lotus without any desire obtains such a fruit, I know not what would happen for one who offers it with devotion to Viṣṇu. ||166||
Truth, truth, and again truth—truth alone is spoken by me:
by worshipping Hari with lotuses, the supreme state is attained. (167)
Whoever offers even a single lotus to the Enemy of Mura shall have no further birth within the terrifying cycles of saṃsāra. (168)
Those who, even for a single day, worship Nārāyaṇa— the embodiment of compassion and the granter of desires— with full-blown lotuses, though they may be burdened by intense sins, [are purified].
Even those who are sinful attain liberation. ||169||
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the Kriyā-yoga-sāra of the glorious Padma Purāṇa. ||13||
(14) Chapter Fourteen. Vyāsa said:
O best of the twice-born, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, a Vaiṣṇava should worship the imperishable Viṣṇu together with Mahālakṣmī with a spirit of devotion.
O best of brahmins, one should not worship Viṣṇu in a land of barbarians (mleccha), nor in the abode of the fallen, nor in a place surrounded by impassable fortresses or enemies. ||2||
One should not perform the worship of Viṣṇu in the presence of heretics, great sinners, or those who speak untruths. (3)
One should perform the worship of Hari even while walking, or in the presence of others, or even while quarreling, as well as while laughing at someone, or while standing. ||4||
One should not worship Viṣṇu in an improper place, nor in the house of those who delight in receiving gifts, nor in the home of the miserly, nor where there is a longing for the wealth of others.
Likewise, one who is devoted to supreme devotion should not perform the worship of Viṣṇu through deceitful conduct;
rather, in the worship of Nārāyaṇa, he should be intent upon the Brahmins.
Abandoning all other thoughts, O best of the twice-born, one should become intent on meditation upon Hari; [one should avoid] cries of "Alas!", sighs, and amazement. (7)
One should perform the worship of Hari, the God of gods and Teacher of the World, with an undivided mind, without engaging in conversation with heretics. 8.
O twice-born one, even if a flower is offered into ashes, it reaches Hari;
likewise, for one exhausted by hundreds of anxieties, [offering] even upon stone discs [yields the same result].
Whatever flower a mortal offers, he shall obtain that very thing from the Lord;
having become single-minded, the wise man should conquer Viṣṇu through devotion. 10.
Whatever action is performed with a deluded mind is fruitless; all action is dependent on the mind, and the three worlds are dependent on the mind. 11.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, one should worship the Lord of Kamalā with a firm mind; for wherever the mind is directed, there the worship truly resides.
And for him, no result shall bear fruit even in hundreds of millions of eons, despite his having performed purification with effort and being devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu. (13)

O twice-born one, if one is devoid of purity of mind, he is regarded as a Cāṇḍāla; even if penance has been performed for a very long time according to the rules, it is rendered fruitless by a lack of devotion.
All of it would be useless, being merely the purification of the body, even if one were to give gold equal in size to Mount Meru to a Brahmin who maintains a family. (15)

That which is given for the sake of a request, or even without devotion, leads to what is not beneficial; therefore, becoming single-minded and endowed with devotion and faith, [one should give]. (16)
Whoever offers vegetables such as *savāstuka* and other greens at the assembly of Viṣṇu, he obtains the divine fruit of a human birth, fully ripened. (17)
O best of the twice-born, Keśava is worshipped by us with great effort because he is fond of new articles belonging to the Lord Hari. (18)
One should offer that very same [offering] to Murāri with devotion during the month of Āgrayaṇa;
and when the month of Pauṣa has arrived, [one should worship] the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of boons. 19.
A devotee of Viṣṇu should indeed bathe [the Lord] with divine sugarcane juices;
O best of Brahmins, he who bathes the Lord Viṣṇu with sugarcane juices [attains great merit].
All the happiness enjoyed here on earth passes away upon death;
yet he who offers sugar-cane as an oblation to Viṣṇu, the God of gods, [attains eternal bliss]. 21.
He obtains that very fruit; what is the use of much further talk?
[It is like] well-milked parched grain in the month of Pauṣa, combined with curds. (22)
By giving [this] to Murāri, a mortal shall attain all desires;
having discarded all old garments, one should offer them to Murāri. (23)

To ward off the cold, one should give a new garment to a Brahmin on the day of the sun’s transit into Capricorn (Pauṣa-saṃkramaṇa), for that Brahmin is none other than Viṣṇu, the embodiment of Prosperity (Lakṣmī).
A person desiring liberation should give a pedestal made of ten types of materials;
moreover, one who, having worshipped the Lord of Kamalā, should sound the conch shell.
I shall describe the fruit of his merit; listen with a concentrated mind, my child.
He is liberated from all sins, such as approaching those who should not be approached.
Having gone to the city of Viṣṇu, he rejoices together with Viṣṇu—he who sounds the conch of Hari made of the tusks of Airāvata. (27)
O best of the twice-born, I shall now describe the merit of that person at the time of worship:
he is liberated from all sins, such as the eating of forbidden food. (28)
Then, having ascended that beautiful celestial chariot of Viṣṇu,
he shall enjoy all his desires there for a period of a hundred crores of kalpas.
Having returned to the earth, that best of the twice-born, learned in the four Vedas,
enjoyed all his desires there for a duration of hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Furthermore, he who plays the lute at the time of worship of the Lord of the World goes to the city of Viṣṇu and attains unsurpassed liberation.
He who prepares clay for the worship of the Enemy of Kaiṭabha (Viṣṇu) shall become the foremost among the wise among mortals in every birth. (32)
The Lord, being pleased with him, grants his desired fruit:
namely, the *ḍamaru*, the *ḍiḍima*, the *jharjharī*, and likewise the *madhurī*.
He who plays the paṭaha, the duṃdubhi, the kāhala, the siṃdhuvāraka, the kāsya, the cakra, the tāla, and the flute; 34.
Listen to the merit of that [person] at the time of Mahāviṣṇu’s worship:
freed from sins such as theft, he goes to the temple of the Wielder of the Discus.
Having attained supreme knowledge, one is liberated right there;
